subset_name: Restricted Python for Airborne
detail: Mandatory PEP 484 type hints; programs must pass static type checking (e.g. mypy) with zero errors before integration.
rationale: Python defers most error detection to runtime; type checking compensates for lack of compile-time enforcement and latent faults (DO-178C A-4 Obj 5, A-6 Obj 4).
failure_class: type error / latent runtime error (e.g. NameError in unexecuted branch)
quote: Mandatory type hints following PEP 484, enforced with static checkers such as mypy. Programs must pass type checking with zero errors before integration.

subset_name: Restricted Python for Airborne
detail: Mandatory PEP 8 as part of the Restricted Python profile (Table 2 mitigation for A-4 Obj 5).
rationale: Source code must conform to standards (DO-178C A-4 Obj 5).
quote: Define Restricted Python profile: mandatory PEP 8 and PEP 484; ban reflection/dynamic execution; use only vetted libraries

subset_name: Restricted Python for Airborne
construct: Reflection and dynamic code execution (eval, exec, compile)
detail: Reflection and dynamic code execution via eval, exec, compile are prohibited.
rationale: To ensure determinism and traceability.
quote: Reflection and dynamic code execution (eval, exec, compile), dynamic imports, and runtime code generation are prohibited to ensure determinism and traceability.

subset_name: Restricted Python for Airborne
detail: Dynamic imports prohibited; static analysis of imports / static import graph used for partitioning evidence.
rationale: To ensure determinism and traceability; partitioning integrity (A-6 Obj 2).
quote: NR

subset_name: Restricted Python for Airborne
detail: Runtime code generation prohibited.
rationale: To ensure determinism and traceability.
quote: NR

subset_name: Restricted Python for Airborne
detail: Shared-state threading disallowed; only multiprocessing or subprocess-based isolation with strict IPC contracts permitted.
rationale: GIL limitations; threading experiments missed 1 s deadlines due to the GIL (A-7 Obj 4); process isolation gives fault containment.
quote: Shared-state threading is disallowed due to Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) limitations. Only multiprocessing or subprocess-based isolation with strict inter-process communication (IPC) contracts is permitted.

subset_name: Restricted Python for Airborne
detail: External C or Rust extensions must be vetted, version-frozen, and explicitly release the GIL when safe.
rationale: A C extension holding the GIL during long operations defers signal handling; explicit GIL release restores near-immediate interrupt response.
quote: External C or Rust extensions must be vetted, version-frozen, and explicitly release the GIL when safe.

subset_name: Restricted Python for Airborne
construct: Uncertified or dynamically loaded binary modules
detail: Use of uncertified or dynamically loaded binary modules is prohibited.
rationale: NR
quote: Use of uncertified or dynamically loaded binary modules is prohibited.

subset_name: Restricted Python for Airborne
detail: Heap usage must be bounded and monitored.
rationale: Predictable memory allocation needed for partition integrity (A-7 Obj 4 timing, sizing and stack usage).
quote: Heap usage must be bounded and monitored.

subset_name: Restricted Python for Airborne
detail: Recursion depth must be explicitly limited.
rationale: NR
quote: Recursion depth must be explicitly limited

subset_name: Restricted Python for Airborne
detail: GC parameters must be configured to avoid unbounded pauses.
rationale: GC introduces nondeterministic pauses that interfere with real-time guarantees.
quote: garbage collection parameters must be configured to avoid unbounded pauses.

subset_name: Restricted Python for Airborne
detail: Exceptions must be caught at subsystem boundaries (explicit try/except at boundaries).
rationale: Robustness to abnormal conditions (A-6 Obj 4); Python detects exceptions only at runtime.
quote: Exceptions must be caught at subsystem boundaries.

subset_name: Restricted Python for Airborne
detail: Silent exception suppression is prohibited.
rationale: NR
quote: Silent exception suppression is prohibited.

subset_name: Restricted Python for Airborne
detail: Logging must follow a structured, timestamped format.
rationale: Traceability and certification audits.
quote: Logging must follow a structured, timestamped format suitable for traceability and certification audits.

subset_name: Restricted Python for Airborne
detail: Only a curated set of vetted, version-controlled libraries; all dependencies documented and archived.
rationale: NR
quote: Only a curated set of vetted, version-controlled libraries may be included. All dependencies must be explicitly documented and archived.

subset_name: Restricted Python for Airborne
detail: Disable JIT in certification builds (Table 2); JIT generally inappropriate unless runtime behaviour frozen and documented; AOT/static compilation preferred.
rationale: JIT introduces non-deterministic timing and warm-up phases that make WCET difficult to bound and undermine traceability/reproducibility of verification evidence.
quote: JIT execution is generally inappropriate for certified airborne systems unless the runtime behavior is frozen, its optimization pathways are documented, and timing evidence is formally recorded.

subset_name: NR (input constraints of CodoMo/PyExZ3 pipeline)
construct: class methods / object-oriented code as concolic-testing targets
detail: PyExZ3 only accepts functions as targets; CodoMo's state extractor rewrites designated methods into functions, replacing class attributes (self.current_state) with module-level variables (current_state__Tello_TEST).
rationale: PyExZ3 cannot directly verify class libraries
quote: PyExZ3 can only accept functions in a given code as its targets and thus, any class methods cannot directly undergo concolic testing.

subset_name: NR (input constraints of CodoMo/PyExZ3 pipeline)
construct: specific function calls that affect PyExZ3 execution
detail: Such calls are manually deactivated in the transformed code before concolic testing (the 'first factor' of manual modification).
rationale: They interfere with PyExZ3 execution
quote: deactivating specific function calls that affect PyExZ3 execution

subset_name: NR (input constraints of CodoMo/PyExZ3 pipeline)
construct: state tracked across repeated calls (reactive functions)
detail: For functions called repeatedly, all expected patterns of state variables and their values must be assigned to the target function so concolic execution covers them.
rationale: Concolic execution does not retain values between calls
quote: The state extractor can address its problem by assigning all expected patterns of state variables and their values to the target function.

subset_name: PTB-FLA restricted actor-based programming model
detail: Within the application program a developer only writes client and server callback functions, which are called by generic FL algorithms hidden inside PTB-FLA.
rationale: Restricted model allows systematic translation of Python code to CSP# models.
quote: It is restricted because within the application program, a developer only writes callback functions for the client and server roles, which are then called by the generic federated learning algorithms hidden inside PTBFLA.

subset_name: PTB-FLA restricted actor-based programming model
detail: Developer writes a single application program instantiated as independent processes; each process has its own incoming message queue (actor); communication only via mpapi sendMsg/rcvMsg.
rationale: Actor model maps straightforwardly to CSP channel model.
quote: It is actor-based because each process has its own incoming message queue and in fact represents an actor.

subset_name: PTB-FLA restricted actor-based programming model
detail: For modelling, key functions are rewritten in functional style: recursion (tail recursion) used instead of loop constructs.
rationale: A Python function in functional style is closer to the CSP model.
quote: Mainly it means that recursion must be used instead of loop constructs, which is relatively straightforward transformation.

subset_name: PTB-FLA restricted actor-based programming model
detail: Message format (number of fields) must be hardcoded in CSP#, so all messages received by one CSP process must have the same format, whereas Python allows varying fields.
rationale: CSP# encoding limitation.
quote: One restrictive point of this template comes from the already mentioned fact that the message format (the number of message ﬁelds) must be hardcoded in CSP#

subset_name: PTB-FLA restricted actor-based programming model
detail: fl_centralised/fl_decentralised made free functions; class data members passed as parameters; constants (noNodes, flSrvId) set as globals for the model.
rationale: Simplifies derivation of the CSP model.
quote: NR

subset_name: PTB-FLA restricted actor-based programming model
detail: Callback functions are not modelled; the only assumption is that they terminate.
rationale: Termination of callbacks is necessary for correctness verification of orchestration.
quote: The only assumption about the callback functions necessary for correctness veriﬁcation of orchestration is that they terminate

subset_name: EB2Py-supported subset of Event-B (and the Python patterns it generates)
construct: Event-B functions other than total functions
detail: Only total functions (→) are translated, mapped to Python def with inputs/outputs from each side of the arrow.
rationale: Prototype tool limitation
quote: The developed prototype tool supports only the total function from Event-B.

subset_name: EB2Py-supported subset of Event-B (and the Python patterns it generates)
construct: abstract operations and unsupported Event-B symbols
detail: The concrete model must be refined to eliminate abstract operations and unsupported symbols before generation; supported symbols listed in Table 3.
rationale: Only a subset of Event-B notation is translatable
quote: Before employing the tool, we refine our concrete model to eliminate any abstract operations and unsupported symbols.

subset_name: EB2Py-supported subset of Event-B (and the Python patterns it generates)
detail: All newly generated proof obligations must be discharged before generating Python code.
rationale: Guarantee correct code generation
quote: it is necessary to discharge all newly generated proof obligations (POs) to guarantee correct code generation.

subset_name: EB2Py-supported subset of Event-B (and the Python patterns it generates)
detail: Event-B constants are emitted with typing.Final; mypy checks for unauthorised reassignment.
rationale: Python has no constant syntax; Final aligns with Event-B semantics
quote: The mypy command can be utilised to check for any unauthorised reassignment of these constants

subset_name: EB2Py-supported subset of Event-B (and the Python patterns it generates)
construct: implication and equivalence operators in guards
detail: Rewritten into equivalent expressions using only conjunction, disjunction and negation.
rationale: Guards are ambiguous to translate; recursive parsing for effective transformation
quote: it automatically reformulates the predicates into equivalent expressions that only use conjunction (∧), disjunction (∨), and negation (¬) operators.

subset_name: EB2Py-supported subset of Event-B (and the Python patterns it generates)
detail: Translated into loops over a fixed number of steps (bounded ranges).
rationale: To check quantified predicates in executable code
quote: we utilize for loops to determine a fixed number of steps when checking the specified Event-B predicates.

subset_name: EB2Py-supported subset of Event-B (and the Python patterns it generates)
construct: events whose guard is false ('null' events)
detail: No code generated; a comment is inserted for traceability.
rationale: Prevent generation of unreachable runtime code
quote: This automatic exclusion is designed to prevent the generation of unreachable runtime code

subset_name: EB2Py-supported subset of Event-B (and the Python patterns it generates)
detail: Temporary variables capture pre-state; actions assign through them and state is updated after all actions, so no assignee is updated before use.
rationale: Preserve Event-B atomic/simultaneous action semantics
failure_class: state variable updated before it is used
quote: it is important to perform dependency checks to ensure that no state variable, designated as an action assignee, is updated before it is used.

subset_name: EB2Py-supported subset of Event-B (and the Python patterns it generates)
detail: Generated code uses global-scope constants/variables and functions; integrating Python classes is future work.
rationale: Not yet implemented
quote: we will focus on integrating advanced concepts of Python classes to enhance our tool capabilities.

subset_name: ePython
construct: Python language features beyond the imperative core
detail: Mainly the imperative aspects of Python are supported; the interpreter supports the minimum functionality and higher-level functionality is moved into importable modules. The exact subset is not enumerated.
rationale: Limited on-chip memory per core (32KB) makes porting a full interpreter impractical
quote: It is mainly the imperative aspects of Python that are currently supported with a number of extensions for parallelism provided as importable modules.

subset_name: ePython
detail: Interpreter supports only the minimum functionality; complex functions (string concatenation, complex maths, error messages) are delegated to a host monitor.
rationale: Reduce per-core memory footprint
quote: For memory reasons the interpreter itself is designed to support the minimum amount of functionality that ePython requires

subset_name: ePython
detail: Custom compact byte code generated on the host, different from standard Python byte code.
rationale: Memory: byte code optimised to be as small as possible
quote: For memory reasons this byte code is different to Python’s standard byte code and optimised to be as small as possible.

subset_name: ePython
detail: Omitted during host-side parsing.
rationale: Memory optimisation
quote: memory optimisation is also performed to omit unused functions that the programmer might have imported into their code but not used.

subset_name: ePython
detail: Only scalars or lists of integers, reals, booleans and strings can be communicated; all communications are blocking (non-blocking is future work); no shared-memory communication model.
rationale: NR
quote: Scalars or lists of integers, reals, booleans and strings can be communicated and currently all communications are blocking.

subset_name: Python subset supported by ESBMC-Python
detail: Only built-in types int, float and boolean plus basic structures are supported; custom types such as uint64/uint128/uint256 required extensions.
rationale: Front-end coverage; the eth2spec case contained elements not initially handled.
quote: ESBMC-Python supports built-in types, i.e., int, float, and boolean, and basic structures.

subset_name: Python subset supported by ESBMC-Python
detail: Type information is needed; the tool infers and inserts AnnAssign type annotations on the AST before conversion.
rationale: Verifiers rely on concrete type information, which Python only assigns at run time.
quote: in Python, concrete-type information is assigned during execution by its interpreter, which makes it harder for verifiers to evaluate correctness, given that they rely on such knowledge.

subset_name: Python subset supported by ESBMC-Python
detail: OOP is modelled with structured programming; overloaded/inherited method calls resolved statically by searching base classes in inheritance-list order.
rationale: ESBMC was not designed to handle OOP.
quote: Note that ESBMC was not designed to handle object-oriented programming (OOP)[8]. Therefore, we had to model OOP features with structured programming.

subset_name: Python subset supported by ESBMC-Python
detail: Recursion depth / loop unwinding bounded by the --unwind option during symbolic execution.
rationale: Bounded model checking explores bounded executions.
quote: where −𝑢𝑛𝑤𝑖𝑛𝑑 limits the recursion depth during symbolic execution.

subset_name: Shelley-analysable MicroPython subset (intermediate representation abstracting MicroPython)
detail: Shelley does not support non-terminating behaviours; loops are modelled as terminating Kleene-star.
rationale: Part of a restricted programming model chosen to make the analysis scalable.
quote: To make our analysis scalable, Shelley makes two important design decisions: a restricted programming model, and an over-approximated behavior.

subset_name: Shelley-analysable MicroPython subset (intermediate representation abstracting MicroPython)
detail: Shelley ignores object aliasing.
rationale: Restricted programming model for scalability.
quote: Shelley does not support non-terminating (inﬁnite) behaviors, ignores object aliasing, and only considers method invocation of ﬁelds.

subset_name: Shelley-analysable MicroPython subset (intermediate representation abstracting MicroPython)
detail: Only method invocations of fields (constrained objects held as fields) are considered.
rationale: Restricted programming model for scalability.
quote: only considers method invocation of ﬁelds

subset_name: Shelley-analysable MicroPython subset (intermediate representation abstracting MicroPython)
detail: The analysis does not model Python exceptions.
rationale: NR
quote: our analysis does not model Python exceptions.

subset_name: Shelley-analysable MicroPython subset (intermediate representation abstracting MicroPython)
construct: Program internal state / data values (call arguments, branch conditions, loop bounds)
detail: Values are disregarded; if/match treated as nondeterministic choice, for/while as a loop of unknown iterations.
rationale: Over-approximated behaviour, closer to behavioural type checking, to keep analysis scalable.
quote: our tool disregards the program’s internal state, e.g., the arguments of method calls, the condition used to branch, and the loop bounds.

subset_name: Shelley-analysable MicroPython subset (intermediate representation abstracting MicroPython)
detail: Each annotated method must return the list of method names that may be invoked next (optionally a tuple whose first element is that list).
rationale: Allows Shelley to build the method-dependency graph and enforce intended order of actions.
quote: Each annotated method must return the set of methods of Valve that can be invoked subsequently.

subset_name: Shelley-analysable MicroPython subset (intermediate representation abstracting MicroPython)
detail: Classes manipulating physical resources must be annotated with ordering constraints and decorators to be verified.
rationale: To provide expected behaviour and prevent an unintended order of actions.
failure_class: incorrect method-call ordering on physical resources (e.g., valve left open)
quote: We use annotations, according to Table I, so that developers can provide more information about the expected behavior of methods and prevent an unintended order of actions from occurring.

subset_name: Shelley-analysable MicroPython subset (intermediate representation abstracting MicroPython)
detail: Results of calls to constrained methods with several exit points are matched with match/case and checked for exhaustiveness.
rationale: Check that all possible exit points are handled.
failure_class: unhandled exit point / invalid subsystem usage
quote: our tool checks if all possible exit points are being handled.

subset_name: Static Python (Cinder)
detail: Module-level variables cannot be mutated; typed modules prevent updates to module-level variables.
rationale: Enable sound types and strong optimizations
quote: module-level variables cannot be mutated

subset_name: Static Python (Cinder)
detail: Class attributes must be set in __init__; class attributes cannot serve as default values for instance attributes.
rationale: Ensure predictable object layouts
quote: class attributes must be set in an __init__ method to ensure predictable layouts

subset_name: Static Python (Cinder)
detail: Typed attributes are resolved statically and cannot be overridden with descriptors or properties.
rationale: Static resolution of typed attributes for optimized field access
quote: Typed ﬁelds cannot be overridden by descriptors or properties (@property).

subset_name: Static Python (Cinder)
detail: Multiple inheritance of typed classes or untyped children of typed classes is forbidden; classes with multiple parents fall back to unoptimized behaviour; at most one parent may be typed.
rationale: vtable layout conflicts: each method name must reside in a fixed slot across subclasses
quote: Static Python does not leverage types for classes with multiple parents because of vtable layout issues.

subset_name: Static Python (Cinder)
detail: To benefit from types, classes must be declared at module top level with at most one parent; otherwise the dynamic type is assigned.
rationale: Do not fit a nominal type system; not in performance-critical code
quote: To beneﬁt from types, classes must be declared at the module top level and may have at most one parent.

subset_name: Static Python (Cinder)
detail: Typed overrides cannot use less-precise types (e.g. cannot override an int-returning method with dynamic); static error.
rationale: Lets typed classes assume overrides are subtypes, enabling optimized dispatch and field reads
quote: In typed code, however, overrides cannot use less-precise types.

subset_name: Static Python (Cinder)
detail: Methods cannot be overloaded.
rationale: Restriction inherited from Python
quote: Methods cannot be overloaded. This restriction comes from Python.

subset_name: Static Python (Cinder)
detail: Unions are tracked statically but replaced by dynamic at run time, except Optional[S] which is enforced with run-time checks.
rationale: Only types that can be validated quickly with casts are enforced
quote: Union types are not, however, generally supported at run-time

subset_name: Static Python (Cinder)
detail: Functions only supported by shallow types; no first-class function or PEP 544 structural types.
rationale: Critical code relies on first-order functions/objects; low priority
quote: Static Python has no support for ﬁrst-class functions or for structural types as deﬁned by PEP 544

subset_name: Static Python (Cinder)
detail: Not supported (nor by Pyre or mypy).
rationale: NR
quote: Three other unsupported types bear special mention: ﬁrst-class class and object types (Section 2.4); ﬁrst-class function (callable) types; and recursive types.

subset_name: Static Python (Cinder)
detail: Calls to eval and exec are given the dynamic type; authors suggest removing dynamic execution rather than typing it.
rationale: Accurate static types would be burdensome; uses can often be removed
quote: Calls to eval and exec have the dynamic type.

subset_name: Static Python (Cinder)
construct: casts between primitive types and dynamic
detail: Primitive types (int64, uint64, double, Array, Vector) are incompatible with dynamic; casts are rejected statically; mixed primitive/non-primitive operands to e.g. 'and' not accepted.
rationale: Performance: unboxed values and arithmetic
quote: Casts between a primitive type and the dynamic type are rejected statically

subset_name: Static Python (Cinder)
construct: enums, @dataclass, __setattr__/__getattr__ overrides, keyword default expressions, **kwargs calls with custom object or extra keys
detail: Currently unsupported; code must be changed or moved to an untyped module. Team plans to lift these.
rationale: NR (not yet implemented)
quote: Several other Python features are unsupported at present: enums; the @dataclass decorator; overrides of the __setattr__ and __getattr__ methods

subset_name: Static Python (Cinder)
detail: Concrete types reject values not created via checked constructor; exact type-parameter match required, even with dynamic parameters; untyped writes are cast-checked.
rationale: Deep soundness of element types even when escaping to untyped code
quote: these checked dictionaries are guaranteed to contain well-typed keys and values even if they escape to untyped code.

subset_name: Static Python (Cinder)
construct: typed function arguments from untyped code
detail: Every typed function is compiled with CHECK_ARGS to cast all inputs; optimizer skips for typed-to-typed calls.
rationale: Arguments from untyped contexts are unchecked and threaten soundness
quote: For this reason, Static Python compiles every typed function to check its inputs.

subset_name: Static Python (Cinder)
detail: Replaced by dynamic type; module-level granularity: problematic expressions must move to untyped modules.
rationale: Focus on types that can be soundly optimized and validated quickly
quote: Static Python has no short-term plans to support all PEP 484 types.

subset_name: PyPrep IR-expressible subset
detail: PyPrep handles only programs expressible in its IR and refuses others; 94/113 benchmark programs (78.6%) were IR-expressible.
rationale: Translation is restricted to what the IR/search space can express so that summaries can be verified by Dafny.
quote: despite its formal correctness guarantees, the tool is limited to programs expressible in its IR and requires manual effort to extend to new patterns.

subset_name: PyPrep IR-expressible subset
detail: Only loops that iterate over data structures (lists, arrays, dictionaries) are identified as candidate fragments for translation.
rationale: Such loops are prime candidates for MapReduce parallelism.
enforcement: static-check (PyPrep program analyzer: live variable and dataflow analysis)
quote: The target fragments are loops that iterate over data structures (lists, arrays, dictionaries), which are prime candidates for MapReduce parallelism.

subset_name: PyPrep IR-expressible subset
detail: reduceByKey selected only for commutative and associative reductions; groupByKey otherwise.
rationale: Semantic equivalence of parallel reduction requires commutativity/associativity.
quote: NR

subset_name: Typpete-supported subset of Python 3
