rationale: Guarantees memory safety and freedom from data races; reading non-existent field would cause a runtime error
failure_class: data race; runtime error from reading non-existent field
quote: The permission system guarantees that veriﬁed code is memory safe and free of data races.

subset_name: Nagini-supported Python subset (Mypy/PEP 484 statically typed Python 3)
detail: Exceptional postconditions (Exsures) must specify which exceptions a method may raise; verified programs do not raise runtime errors or undeclared exceptions
rationale: Prevent runtime errors and undeclared exceptions
quote: Veriﬁed programs will not raise runtime errors or undeclared exceptions.

subset_name: Nagini-supported Python subset (Mypy/PEP 484 statically typed Python 3)
detail: Nagini verifies referenced names are defined before use (e.g. calls before class definition disallowed)
rationale: Mypy only checks this optimistically
quote: Nagini also veriﬁes some properties that Mypy only checks optimistically, e.g., that referenced names are deﬁned before they are used.

subset_name: Pythonic Type System (PyTS) fragment
detail: The formalization only covers programs where types are not dynamically altered at runtime.
rationale: Ensures the formalization applies to a well-defined and analyzable fragment of the language.
quote: Our focus is restricted to programs where types are not dynamically altered at runtime, thereby ensuring that the formalization applies to a well-defined and analyzable fragment of the language.

subset_name: Pythonic Type System (PyTS) fragment
detail: Generics are treated as having at least one parameter; instantiating typing.Generic without parameters is not modelled.
rationale: Described as a runtime quirk, seldom used.
quote: The odd fact that, in Python, typing.Generic itself is instantiable without parameters is a runtime quirk that we do not model in our type system.

subset_name: Pythonic Type System (PyTS) fragment
construct: type metaclass as a primitive in the blueprint layer
detail: Primitive existential types are derived from core classes excluding the type metaclass; classes-as-values are handled separately in a meta layer (TypeET).
rationale: NR
quote: These expressions are built using a set of primitives derived from Python’s core classes [18], excluding the type metaclass.

subset_name: Pythonic Type System (PyTS) fragment
construct: Behaviour specification of ADTs / behavioural subtyping
detail: Only the static aspect of ADTs is modelled; behavioural subtyping is not enforced.
rationale: Interest is in a static type system.
quote: Since we are interested in a static type system for Python, we are focusing only on the static aspect of the ADT, ignoring the specification of the behavior.

subset_name: Pythonic Type System (PyTS) fragment
construct: Decorators that alter function or class signatures
detail: Listed as complex dynamic concepts still to be addressed in future work.
rationale: NR
quote: decorator patterns that alter function or class signatures

subset_name: Numba nopython-mode Python subset
detail: Limited to fixed-width integer types up to 64 bits with semantics similar to C platforms.
rationale: Deviations from Python semantics allow aggressive optimization; acceptable for numeric use cases.
quote: The compiler does not support the “big integer” representation used in Python to represent integers of arbitrary size.

subset_name: Numba nopython-mode Python subset
detail: All polymorphism must be resolvable at compile time (when the function is called).
rationale: Allows aggressive optimization by the compiler.
quote: Polymorphic types are not supported during execution, requiring the compiler to be able to resolve all polymorphism at compile time

subset_name: Numba nopython-mode Python subset
construct: Assignment of a value of a different type to a variable
detail: Implicit coercion occurs; coercion only available for numeric and certain built-in types; reassignments visible to all subsequent blocks create new definitions to minimise mono-typing.
rationale: Type inference requires each value to have a single inferred type.
quote: Implicit coercion occurs when a type is assigned to a variable of a different type.

subset_name: Numba nopython-mode Python subset
construct: Values whose type cannot be inferred
detail: If type inference fails, function falls back to object mode relying on the Python C-API instead of nopython mode.
rationale: nopython mode needs a type for every value to lower to machine code.
quote: If Numba cannot determine the type of one of the values in the IR, it assumes to all values in the function to be a Python object.

subset_name: Numba nopython-mode Python subset
detail: Handling of mutual recursion is difficult because each function is compiled in a separate LLVM module and must be finalized immediately.
rationale: LLVM MCJIT does not support lazy compilation.
quote: This makes handling of mutual recursion difficult.

subset_name: PetPy
construct: Statements outside PetPy (while, del, try, and remaining Python AST statement nodes)
detail: Uninterpreted constructs default to a catch-all 'Other' rule: the postcondition is propagated as-is and the soundness flag is set False if the statement may modify locations read by the formula.
rationale: Grounds the analysis by stating exactly which constructs are interpreted precisely and which approximately, allowing reasoning about unsoundness due to difficult-to-interpret constructs.
quote: features that are handled approximately (ones that default to Other, including while, del, try, and the rest of the Statement nodes specified by the Python AST).

subset_name: PetPy
detail: PetPy productions cover constructs that modify heap locations or propagate heap addresses.
rationale: Needed for reference immutability analysis.
quote: the key criterion was to include constructs that modify heap locations or propagate heap addresses (for the purposes of reference immutability).

subset_name: PetPy
detail: If the left-hand side contains a star pattern (directly or nested) the assignment is handled by Other in WP; in 3-address code it matches the list as a whole, introducing infeasible value flow.
rationale: NR
quote: If lhs contains a star pattern, directly or indirectly, then the assignment is handled by Other

subset_name: PetPy
construct: Attribute and subscript assignment (exp1.f = exp2, exp1[exp2] = exp3)
detail: Default to Other in WP: no substitution into the formula; soundness flag turns False if modified and read locations intersect.
rationale: Heap modification cannot be substituted directly into the formula.
quote: These patterns trigger a modification to a heap variable and we cannot substitute directly into the formula.

subset_name: PetPy
construct: Loops (for) and other intricate constructs (slices, generators)
detail: For loops only guarded with membership when postcondition is True; otherwise postcondition propagated; loops handled via read/mod-set intersection rather than fixpoint computation. Quantified loop variables reaching the top-level function are ignored.
rationale: Loops are a known thorn in WP inference; intersecting read and mod sets avoids complex fixpoint approximation.
quote: Instead of defining handlers for those constructs (loops are a known thorn in weakest precondition inference), we consider the much easier problem of intersecting the read and mod sets.

subset_name: PetPy
construct: Side effects modifying locations read by a precondition
detail: Preconditions are flagged unsound when mod(S) and read(Q) intersect (reference immutability analysis).
rationale: Side effects make WP analysis unsound: an exception may still be raised even if the precondition holds.
quote: An exception can occur even if the precondition holds if a statement modifies a location referenced in the precondition as a side effect.

subset_name: PetPy
detail: New functions are interpreted in an empty environment, ignoring globals.
rationale: Simplifying assumption.
quote: We assume new functions are interpreted in an empty environment; this is a simplifying assumption as it ignores global variables.

subset_name: PetPy
construct: Expression calls, calls on receiver objects, calls through function pointers
detail: No comprehensive value-flow analysis; such calls remain unresolved by the name-based call graph.
rationale: Call graph construction for Python remains an open problem.
quote: there is no comprehensive value-flow analysis and expression calls such as self.random_state_.shuffle(ordered_idx) or est.fit(X), as well as calls through function pointers, remain unresolved.

subset_name: PetPy
detail: Cython files are not analysed; calls into them remain unresolved.
rationale: NR
quote: At this point, our analysis does not look at Cython files to try to find Cython class and function definitions.

subset_name: PetPy
detail: Assumed polymorphic w.r.t. immutability (do not modify arguments) unless the result is modified; external imports out of scope, identified by concrete evaluation.
rationale: Motivated by numpy/scipy behaviour in target ML libraries.
quote: We assume that library calls are polymorphic with respect to immutability, that is, they do not modify the argument

subset_name: PetPy
construct: Field access through non-self references / aliasing
detail: Heuristic assumes fields are written and read exclusively through self and self is a unique reference; any non-self x.f and y.g treated as potential aliases.
rationale: More precise mod sets needed for WP soundness reasoning.
quote: The extension is a heuristic that takes advantage of the well-known idiom in object-oriented programming, namely, that fields of objects are written and read exclusively through self.

subset_name: PetPy
detail: Subscript treated as a special field ignoring the index, since overriding makes its meaning unknown until runtime.
rationale: Complex Python semantics make translation to 3-address code non-trivial.
quote: In Python, however, one may override the subscript operation and the interpretation of exp1[exp2] into 3-address code may remain unknown until runtime.

subset_name: PetPy
detail: Can cause the analysis to miss exceptions.
rationale: NR
quote: There are occasions when the IWP analysis misses exceptions as well, for example, because of dynamic class loading.

subset_name: PetPy
detail: Formulas with more than 200 implications are pruned (unsound).
rationale: Scalability under path explosion; such formulas are uninterpretable.
quote: we apply a pruning heuristic that removes formulas that are excessively large, specifically ones that have more than 200 implications at any point during the analysis.

subset_name: PRuby/DRuby statically typable Ruby (transformed TinyRuby without eval/send/method_missing)
construct: eval, send, method_missing in type-checked code
detail: Well-typed programs in the formal type system may not contain eval, send or method_missing; the profile-guided translation replaces them with static code (conditionals over profiled strings, direct calls, explicit method definitions), with safe_eval fallback.
rationale: They cannot be checked statically.
quote: In order for our type system to be sound, we forbid well-typed programs from containing eval, send, or method missing (since we cannot check these statically)

subset_name: PRuby/DRuby statically typable Ruby (transformed TinyRuby without eval/send/method_missing)
detail: Translation completely eliminates method_missing, defining one method per profiled name; no fall-through, so unprofiled calls are rejected as undefined methods.
rationale: Static analysis need not handle method_missing and can find calls intercepted by the wrong method.
quote: Recall that the translation from Section 3.2 eliminates the three dynamic features that this type system does not permit

subset_name: PRuby/DRuby statically typable Ruby (transformed TinyRuby without eval/send/method_missing)
construct: Method definitions inside dynamically evaluated code (safe_eval)
detail: Method definitions in dynamically checked code are replaced by blame.
rationale: Redefining methods in dynamic code could undermine type safety of statically typed code.
quote: we cannot permit methods to be redefined in dynamically checked code, since this could undermine the type safety of statically typed code.

subset_name: PRuby/DRuby statically typable Ruby (transformed TinyRuby without eval/send/method_missing)
construct: Calls that change the class hierarchy in dynamic code (e.g. undef_method)
detail: safe_eval additionally disallows calls to methods that may change the class hierarchy.
rationale: Same as forbidding method definitions in dynamic code (protect static typing).
quote: in addition to forbidding method definitions, we must also disallow calls to methods that may change the class hierarchy, such as undef method.

subset_name: PRuby/DRuby statically typable Ruby (transformed TinyRuby without eval/send/method_missing)
detail: Any method syntactically present in source is assumed available everywhere; mock definitions that blame are inserted at program start and violations checked dynamically.
rationale: Avoids a complex flow-sensitive 'must be defined' analysis needed for soundness.
quote: we assume that any method syntactically present in the source code is available everywhere and rely on dynamic, rather than static, checking to find violations of our assumption.

subset_name: PRuby/DRuby statically typable Ruby (transformed TinyRuby without eval/send/method_missing)
detail: DRuby requires the number of block formal parameters to exactly match actual arguments (Ruby itself pads with nil/ignores extras); 24 refactorings applied.
rationale: Otherwise mismatched argument counts for blocks could never be discovered.
quote: DRuby, on the other hand, requires strict matching of the number of block arguments, since otherwise we could never discover mismatched argument counts for blocks.

subset_name: PRuby/DRuby statically typable Ruby (transformed TinyRuby without eval/send/method_missing)
detail: eval'ing a string containing eval, or send'ing to eval, is not recursively translated.
rationale: Implementation limitation; could be lifted with engineering effort.
quote: Currently, PRuby does not support nested dynamic constructs, e.g., eval’ing a string with eval inside it, or send’ing a message to the eval method.

subset_name: PRuby/DRuby statically typable Ruby (transformed TinyRuby without eval/send/method_missing)
construct: Redefinition of low-level special methods (Module#append_features, Class#new, Class#inherited, Module#method_added, Module#included)
detail: Not supported by PRuby; redefinition would change language semantics assumed by DRuby.
rationale: DRuby's type system treats these methods specially; redefining them changes semantics.
quote: DRuby’s type system treats certain low-level methods specially, but these methods could be redefined, effectively changing the semantics of the language.

subset_name: PRuby/DRuby statically typable Ruby (transformed TinyRuby without eval/send/method_missing)
construct: Dynamic constructs on eigen-classes, dynamic features via Method class, const_missing
detail: Not yet supported.
rationale: Not given beyond being unsupported (const_missing expected in future).
quote: PRuby also does not support applying dynamic constructs to per-object classes (eigen-classes) or calling dynamic features via the Method class.

subset_name: PRuby/DRuby statically typable Ruby (transformed TinyRuby without eval/send/method_missing)
construct: Low-level class/module manipulation (remove_method, undef_method, anonymous class creation, Singleton, Delegate)
detail: Code using these was considered untypable; DRuby does not support it and will not detect run-time errors from misuse.
rationale: Cannot be reasonably statically typed.
quote: DRuby does not support code that uses these lowlevel features and will not detect any run-time errors from their misuse.

subset_name: PRuby/DRuby statically typable Ruby (transformed TinyRuby without eval/send/method_missing)
construct: Run-time type tests on union-typed values
detail: DRuby does not model type tests; programmers add branch annotations (135 branches) that are checked dynamically at run time.
rationale: Type system limitation.
quote: DRuby does not currently model run-time type tests specially.

subset_name: PRuby/DRuby statically typable Ruby (transformed TinyRuby without eval/send/method_missing)
detail: Requires never triggered in test runs were hoisted to top level (21 refactorings) so files are included in type checking.
rationale: Profiling decides which files are analysed.
quote: We refactored cases like this by moving the require statement outside of the method, so that it was always executed when the file is loaded.

subset_name: PRuby/DRuby statically typable Ruby (transformed TinyRuby without eval/send/method_missing)
detail: Arrays/hashes used heterogeneously caused type errors; refactored (12 refactorings).
rationale: DRuby supports homogeneous containers and tuples with automatic coercion.
quote: DRuby supports homogeneous containers with types such as Array<T> and Hash<K,V>.

subset_name: PRuby/DRuby statically typable Ruby (transformed TinyRuby without eval/send/method_missing)
construct: Local variables in blocks assigned conflicting types
detail: Locals inside blocks are treated flow-insensitively; conflicting assignments rewritten to fresh variables (11 refactorings).
rationale: Needed for soundness.
quote: To be sound, we conservatively treat any local variables that appear inside of a block flow-insensitively

subset_name: PRuby/DRuby statically typable Ruby (transformed TinyRuby without eval/send/method_missing)
detail: Type-conflicting configuration branches were commented out (10 refactorings).
rationale: DRuby assumes both paths possible and reports wrong argument counts.
quote: To handle these typeconflicting cases, we commented out sections of code that were disabled by the platform configuration.

subset_name: Python subset for the Titan Python-to-dataflow (SPIR-V/SystemVerilog) compiler
detail: Imperative variable assignments are allowed syntactically but reinterpreted as immutable 'let' value definitions; each update defines a fresh named value (also for array writes).
rationale: Parallel dataflow needs values streaming to where needed; dependency on previous values introduces hazards and is no longer parallel.
quote: Whenever a variable is updated in user code, we interpret it as the deﬁnition of a fresh named value.

subset_name: Python subset for the Titan Python-to-dataflow (SPIR-V/SystemVerilog) compiler
detail: Basic types limited to 32-bit integers, floats and booleans.
rationale: Most common types used in DSP/AI programming.
quote: The subset’s basic types are limited to 32-bit integers, ﬂoats, and booleans.

subset_name: Python subset for the Titan Python-to-dataflow (SPIR-V/SystemVerilog) compiler
detail: Lists and tuples excluded; n-dimensional fixed-size NumPy arrays of ints/floats included (definition, indexing, slicing).
rationale: NR beyond fixed-size arrays giving the compiler shape/type information required since SPIR-V is strongly typed.
quote: We exclude lists and tuples from the subset, but include n-dimensional arrays of integers and ﬂoats, using a subset of NumPy syntax to deﬁne ﬁxed size arrays

subset_name: Python subset for the Titan Python-to-dataflow (SPIR-V/SystemVerilog) compiler
detail: Optional Python type hints become mandatory in the subset.
rationale: Make implementation easier.
quote: These make implementation easier so we strengthen these hints from an option to a requirement in the subset.

subset_name: Python subset for the Titan Python-to-dataflow (SPIR-V/SystemVerilog) compiler
detail: Allowed but interpreted as an alternate notation for the functional ternary if expression.
rationale: Functional programming has no program flow; enables conditionals without state or program flow.
quote: We allow both forms into the Python subset, but interpret the ﬁrst as an alternate notation for the second.

subset_name: Python subset for the Titan Python-to-dataflow (SPIR-V/SystemVerilog) compiler
construct: Iterative for loops (shared state between iterations)
detail: Iterative loops removed; mappable (independent-iteration) for loops retained and reinterpreted as parallel maps.
rationale: Iterative loops that update shared state are problematic to parallelise.
quote: We remove iterative loops from the subset but retain mappable loops, reinterpreting them as maps to be executed in parallel.

subset_name: Python subset for the Titan Python-to-dataflow (SPIR-V/SystemVerilog) compiler
detail: while loops removed from the subset.
rationale: Inherently sequential; iterations cannot be converted to maps.
quote: We also remove while loops from the subset, as they are inherently sequential.

subset_name: Python subset for the Titan Python-to-dataflow (SPIR-V/SystemVerilog) compiler
detail: Total functional programming: first argument of each call is a variant that must strictly decrease on each recursive call while remaining positive; simple calls are inlined as procedures. Subset is deliberately not Turing complete.
rationale: Ensures finite termination and avoids generating infinite digital logic at compile time; real-time code must complete in finite time.
quote: by design we have removed the ability to express non-halting programs.

subset_name: Python subset for the Titan Python-to-dataflow (SPIR-V/SystemVerilog) compiler
detail: Program is a step() function called repeatedly on a stream; no init() since there is no state to initialise.
rationale: Continuous pipeline model for real-time stream processing in a functional subset.
quote: As we are using a functional subset we do not need an init() call – there is no state to initialise.

subset_name: Python subset for the Titan Python-to-dataflow (SPIR-V/SystemVerilog) compiler
construct: Lagged/delayed signal state (e.g., globals as delay lines)
detail: Instead of stateful lagging code, the user declares which inputs are lagged and buffer depth; the compiler synthesises buffers.
rationale: Creating lagged signals is an inherently stateful process, unclear to describe in a functional language.
quote: Our subset language provides additional tools for the user to deﬁne which inputs should be lagged, and the depth of the buffer.

subset_name: QURE-supported Python/Pandas UDF subset (Table 2 grammar)
detail: Supported grammar: constants (bool, numbers, strings, lists, dicts), types bool/int/long/real/str, list[t]/DataFrame/Relation/Column, standard operators, pass, typed var, assignment, if/else, for, while, return, function calls (approximate summary).
rationale: Constructs must be expressible in Boogie for Hoare-style verification
enforcement: static-check (QURE Python-to-Boogie translator; verification fails and original UDF is kept)
quote: An abbreviated overview of the Python grammar for UDFs supported by QURE is given in Table 2

subset_name: QURE-supported Python/Pandas UDF subset (Table 2 grammar)
detail: Types inferred from DB schema, assignment rules and function repository; any ambiguity fails verification.
rationale: Boogie is statically typed
quote: If the type of any variable is ambiguous, the verification is considered unsuccessful.

subset_name: QURE-supported Python/Pandas UDF subset (Table 2 grammar)
construct: loops not matching the loop-summary model
detail: Loops must have an iterator, fixed increment/decrement and bound; at most one level of nesting; must map to [OP1]OP2 SQL operator patterns (filter, inner join, row-wise transformation, aggregation). Otherwise verification fails.
rationale: Inherent complexity of verifying equivalence between loops and SQL operators; prevent incorrectly declaring equivalence
quote: When we encounter a loop that does not fit our model of loop summary (e.g., due to additional or missing variables), we fail the verification and execute the original UDF

subset_name: QURE-supported Python/Pandas UDF subset (Table 2 grammar)
detail: Loops handled have an iterator with per-iteration increment/decrement and bound; ranking function R = B - i (or i - B) asserted to decrease and remain non-negative.
rationale: Ensure loop termination
quote: we handle loops with an iterator variable 𝑖, a per-iteration increment or decrement Δ𝑖, and a bound 𝐵 on 𝑖.

subset_name: QURE-supported Python/Pandas UDF subset (Table 2 grammar)
construct: operator semantics split across pre-/post-loop code or across multiple loops
detail: Input-output mapping and ordering must be confined within the loop body; multiple loops for one operator (except join variants) and uncharacterized operator combinations not covered.
rationale: Difficulty identifying precise invariants for partial semantics
quote: operators with any semantics not solely encapsulated within the loop’s body are not covered.

subset_name: QURE-supported Python/Pandas UDF subset (Table 2 grammar)
construct: yield, missing else branches, implicit ordering
detail: Coverage depends on constructs that can be logically modeled; yield operations, missing else parts, and unspecified ordering when SQL assumes one cannot be modeled.
rationale: Cannot be logically modeled
quote: QURE’s coverage is more dependent on existence of specific constructs that can or cannot (e.g., yield operations, no explicit ordering specified in UDF while the SQL operator assumes one, or missing else parts in conditional statements) be logically modeled

subset_name: QURE-supported Python/Pandas UDF subset (Table 2 grammar)
detail: Only functions registered in the function repository (>130 Python/DataFrame functions) with SQL equivalents are modeled, as uninterpreted functions with axioms.
rationale: Library source unavailable or too complex to verify
quote: QURE currently supports more than 130 frequently used Python and DataFrame functions

subset_name: QURE-supported Python/Pandas UDF subset (Table 2 grammar)
detail: A dictionary is inlined as a constant only if assigned once, never modified by a called function, and no reference passed; otherwise modeled as two arrays with axioms.
rationale: Precondition for semantics-preserving AST rewrite
quote: requires that index acts as a constant, i.e., it is assigned to once, we never invoke a function that modifies it, and no reference to index is passed.

subset_name: QURE-supported Python/Pandas UDF subset (Table 2 grammar)
detail: Translation of UDFs containing SQL statements is out of scope.
rationale: Not supported in Spark; future work
quote: Translation of UDFs containing SQL statements is outside the scope of this work.

subset_name: RPython (Restricted Python)
construct: dynamic features (class modification, exec, nested scopes, metaclasses)
detail: May be used in full only during the initialization/bootstrapping phase that builds live objects; the translated program is the resulting objects.
rationale: Preserve flexibility while allowing efficient execution of the final program
quote: Dynamic features like class modification can be used in full, but only during an initial, bootstrapping phase.

subset_name: RPython (Restricted Python)
detail: Final program must be well-typed per RPython type inference (Annotator); otherwise rejected. User supplies an entry point and its parameter types.
rationale: Static typing for efficient native representation and code generation
quote: If no suitable RPython type can be found for a variable, then the program is rejected and processing stops.

subset_name: RPython (Restricted Python)
construct: variables/returns of incompatible types (e.g. function returning int or str)
detail: Static type system forbids using values of incompatible types together.
rationale: Flexibility costs efficiency; such features cannot be efficiently implemented
quote: the static type system of RPython forbids using values of incompatible types together

subset_name: RPython (Restricted Python)
construct: run-time modification of class definitions (adding/removing methods, fields)
detail: Each class has a fixed set of fields, methods and superclasses, as in Java/C#; classes cannot be defined after initialization.
rationale: Necessary for generating efficient executables; enables native VM method calls
quote: it is not possible to dynamically change class definitions, by adding or removing methods and fields.

subset_name: RPython (Restricted Python)
detail: Only single inheritance; mixins (marked _mixin_) offer method sharing without affecting hierarchy.
rationale: Java-like object model for back-ends
quote: RPython only supports single inheritance; however, it also supports mixin definitions

subset_name: RPython (Restricted Python)
detail: Lists must hold items of the same type; dictionaries must be homogeneous in keys and in values.
rationale: Generic container types parameterized by item type; efficient representation
quote: As with lists, RPython dictionaries need to be homogeneous

subset_name: RPython (Restricted Python)
construct: primitive types (int, float, bool, char, string)
detail: Can only be used in restricted ways so they can be represented by native counterparts (e.g. scalar int).
rationale: Native representation during execution
quote: While in Python each of these types is an object, in RPython these types can only be used in restricted ways.

subset_name: RPython (Restricted Python)
detail: The only operation permitted on a class object is instantiation.
rationale: Easy to implement via reflection on JVM/CLI
quote: the only operation which RPython permits on a class object is to instantiate it.

subset_name: RPython (Restricted Python)
detail: Limited support for mixins and limited use of bound methods.
rationale: NR
quote: limited support for mixins, first-order function and class values, limited use of bound methods, metaclasses.

subset_name: RPython (Restricted Python)
detail: A function whose argument cannot be assigned a single type typechecks only if explicitly annotated as polymorphic, causing cloning per argument type.
rationale: Current type system limitation
quote: One of the main limitations of the current type system of RPython is that it does not directly support generic methods or functions.

subset_name: RPython (Restricted Python)
detail: Methods cannot be overloaded in Python/RPython (external overloaded .NET methods may be called).
rationale: Inherited from Python
quote: Although in Python and RPython methods can not be overloaded

subset_name: RPython (Restricted Python)
detail: All exceptions derive from exceptions.Exception (rooted at Object); on JVM Object split into two implementations so exceptions descend from Throwable.
rationale: Allow RPython exceptions to be thrown via VM mechanisms
quote: a distringuished subclass, exceptions.Exception, from which all exceptions are derived.

subset_name: Safe TypeScript (SafeTS core)
construct: eval and other inherently type-unsafe JavaScript features (e.g. stack walks)
detail: Features like eval are outside the type-safe language; programs needing them should resort to TS* type-based isolation.
rationale: eval and stack walks are inherently type-unsafe 'bad parts'.
quote: when parts of the program need to carefully utilize features of JavaScript like eval that are outside our typesafe language, one might instead resort to the type-based isolation mechanism

subset_name: Safe TypeScript (SafeTS core)
detail: null removed from well-typed programs, retaining only undefined; an option permits null in every reference type for existing programs.
rationale: Rationalizes JavaScript having two null-like values.
quote: Safe TypeScript rationalizes this aspect of JavaScript’s design, in effect removing null from well-typed programs while retaining only undefined.

subset_name: Safe TypeScript (SafeTS core)
detail: Use of this in a non-method function is precluded by typing it as the abstract type •{}.
rationale: JavaScript binds this to a global object in bare function calls, so relying on properties of this is unsafe.
quote: As such, relying on any properties of this in g is unsafe. We preclude the use of this in a nonmethod function

subset_name: Safe TypeScript (SafeTS core)
construct: Arbitrary prototype chains (proto property, arbitrary functions as constructors)
detail: proto treated as reserved and its access forbidden statically and at runtime; new may be called only on objects with a constructor signature (class types).
rationale: Direct manipulation of prototype chains cannot be proven type-safe.
quote: programmers cannot build arbitrary prototype chains using JavaScript’s proto property, or using arbitrary functions as object constructors.

subset_name: Safe TypeScript (SafeTS core)
detail: TypeScript's covariant and contravariant array subtyping is replaced by sound covariant subtyping only for immutable CheckedArray (excludes push; assignments checked).
rationale: TypeScript's array subtyping is unsound.
quote: More conservatively, Safe TypeScript supports sound covariant subtyping for immutable arrays

subset_name: Safe TypeScript (SafeTS core)
detail: Classes and interfaces may not override inherited field types; method overrides must be subtypes (arguments/results related by ∅-subtyping).
rationale: Fields are mutable.
quote: since fields are mutable, classes and interfaces are not permitted to override inherited field types.

subset_name: Safe TypeScript (SafeTS core)
detail: Only non-coercive ∅-subtyping allowed for function arguments, e.g. (x:Point)⇒3dPoint <: (x:3dPoint)⇒Point excluded.
rationale: Coercive wrappers would break observable object identity.
quote: Our solution is to require that higher order subtyping only use ∅-subtypes for relating function arguments

subset_name: Safe TypeScript (SafeTS core)
detail: All generic types are erased and subtyping from generic types to any is forbidden (no polymorphic values in dynamically typed code).
rationale: Keeps the compiler/runtime interface simple and sound; dynamic seals would break object identity.
quote: we erase all generic types, and we forbid subtyping from generic types to any.

subset_name: Safe TypeScript (SafeTS core)
construct: Dynamic idioms on erased types (field extension, reflection, deletion)
detail: Values of erased types (•t) must be used statically; they exclude field extension, reflection, or deletion and are not subtypes of any.
rationale: Without RTTI the runtime cannot enforce typing invariants of erased values.
quote: they exclude dynamic programming idioms (like field extension, reflection, or deletion) on values with erased types.

subset_name: Safe TypeScript (SafeTS core)
detail: Reading/writing the reserved rtti field name dies at runtime; property enumerations exclude it.
rationale: Well-typed code must never access the additional RTTI field.
quote: we must ensure that well-typed code never accesses this additional field.

subset_name: Safe TypeScript (SafeTS core)
detail: Excluded because an object may have only one prototype; implements clauses with interfaces used instead.
rationale: Class inheritance desugars to prototype-based inheritance.
quote: As an object may have only one prototype, multiple inheritance for classes is excluded.

subset_name: Safe TypeScript (SafeTS core)
detail: Class types treated nominally (but viewable structurally); interfaces may be qualified nominal.
rationale: Purely structural view of class types is incompatible with JavaScript semantics (instanceof).
quote: To fix this discrepancy, Safe TypeScript treats class-types nominally, but let them be viewed structurally.

subset_name: Safe TypeScript (SafeTS core)
detail: Dynamic field reads/writes and calls on any-typed values are mediated by runtime checks (readField, writeField, checkAndTag); a failed check stops execution.
rationale: Ensure any dynamic type error is caught.
quote: Our compiler achieves soundness by enforcing stricter static checks and embedding residual runtime checks in compiled code.

subset_name: Python 3.7 subset supported by the Mopsa type analysis
detail: Programs using eval cannot be analyzed; handling eval left as future work.
rationale: Not yet handled by the analysis; less used than in JavaScript and never encountered in benchmarks.
quote: In practice, we are nevertheless limited to programs that do not use eval.

subset_name: Python 3.7 subset supported by the Mopsa type analysis
detail: Analyzer detects recursive calls and stops at that point.
rationale: Not implemented yet (inlining-based interprocedural analysis); authors note recursion is not used a lot in Python.
quote: The analyzer does not support recursive functions for now, but the implementation would not be technically difficult

subset_name: Python 3.7 subset supported by the Mopsa type analysis
detail: Not supported.
rationale: Not implemented yet.
quote: Similarly, metaclasses are not supported but should not be technically difficult to implement.

subset_name: Python 3.7 subset supported by the Mopsa type analysis
detail: Not supported.
rationale: NR
quote: The super class and arbitrary code evaluation using eval are not supported.

subset_name: Python 3.7 subset supported by the Mopsa type analysis
detail: Not supported.
rationale: NR
quote: Asynchronous operators are not supported either

subset_name: Python 3.7 subset supported by the Mopsa type analysis
detail: Supported via Typeshed stub annotations; most but not all annotations supported; stubbed functions assumed side-effect free, so exceptions they raise are not reported.
rationale: Standard library is huge and partly written in C.
failure_class: unhandled exception (may go unreported for stubbed functions)
quote: Note that the use of these annotations changes the soundness of our analyzer: exceptions raised by concrete functions where we used their annotated counterpart will not be reported.

subset_name: Constructs supported by PType (static type annotation/inference tool)
detail: Only handled when the argument is a constant string, which is compiled to AST and spliced into the program.
rationale: exec and eval are pure dynamic.
quote: In Python, exec and eval, are pure dynamic. We could only handle the situation that the parameter is constant string.

subset_name: Constructs supported by PType (static type annotation/inference tool)
detail: Supported only when the attribute name is a constant string.
rationale: Conservative approach to dynamic attribute access.
quote: For getattr, we support a limited, conservative approach that is the attr have to be a constant string.

subset_name: Constructs supported by PType (static type annotation/inference tool)
detail: Make it hard or impossible to obtain accurate attributes; a main source of inaccuracy.
rationale: Dynamic attribute manipulation defeats static analysis.
quote: delattr make it hard or even impossible to obtain the accurate attributes of some objects in static analysis.

subset_name: Constructs supported by PType (static type annotation/inference tool)
detail: Exceptions changing control flow make type annotation inaccurate.
rationale: NR
quote: the exception would change the program`s control flow, which make it inaccurate for type annotation.

subset_name: Constructs supported by PType (static type annotation/inference tool)
detail: Transformed into a list storing all results.
rationale: Complex features are transformed into known simpler forms; the main concern is the returned items.
quote: The way we handle generator is transforming it to a list with all the results stored in it.

subset_name: Constructs supported by PType (static type annotation/inference tool)
detail: Replaced by simple statements (create empty list, traverse, append).
rationale: Simplify complex forms before type analysis.
quote: we replace the list comprehension with several simple statements.

subset_name: Constructs supported by PType (static type annotation/inference tool)
detail: Replaced by the equivalent assignment foo = wrapper(foo).
rationale: Simplify complex forms before type analysis.
quote: So we replace the decorator with this statement.

subset_name: Constructs supported by PType (static type annotation/inference tool)
detail: Simulated in Python: type-annotated if side-effect free, fully functionally simulated if they have side effects; context-dependent functions typed Tenv.
rationale: No source to analyse directly.
quote: Because these built-in modules have no Python source code, we cannot analyze their type information directly.

subset_name: Mini-Python (subset of Python 3.6 analysed by the prototype abstract interpreter, later MOPSA)
detail: Programs featuring code generation or calling eval or compile are rejected; dynamic code generation or retrieval not supported
rationale: Analysis embraces dynamic features but 'draws the line' here; existing JavaScript work on eval could help (future work)
enforcement: static-check (prototype abstract interpreter rejects/does not support)
quote: we nevertheless draw the line and reject programs featuring code generation, calling eval or compile builtins

subset_name: Mini-Python (subset of Python 3.6 analysed by the prototype abstract interpreter, later MOPSA)
detail: Programs importing modules from locations that are not statically known are rejected
rationale: NR
enforcement: static-check (prototype abstract interpreter rejects/does not support)
quote: importing modules from locations that are not statically known

subset_name: Mini-Python (subset of Python 3.6 analysed by the prototype abstract interpreter, later MOPSA)
detail: Recursive procedures not supported; language restricted to recursion-free programs
rationale: Recursive procedures are not much employed in Python; classic interprocedural techniques could apply (future work)
enforcement: static-check (prototype abstract interpreter rejects/does not support)
quote: we do not support recursive procedures, which are not much employed in Python

subset_name: Mini-Python (subset of Python 3.6 analysed by the prototype abstract interpreter, later MOPSA)
detail: Coroutines not supported at the moment (generators are supported)
rationale: NR
enforcement: static-check (prototype abstract interpreter rejects/does not support)
quote: Some other omitted features are not supported at the moment: eval and compile, recursion, coroutines (although we do support generators).

subset_name: Mini-Python (subset of Python 3.6 analysed by the prototype abstract interpreter, later MOPSA)
detail: Unified namespace; assumes all identifiers in the program are unique, so environments can be maps from names to values without ambiguity
rationale: Allows environments to be encoded as maps from names to values without ambiguity
quote: we assume that all identifiers in the program are unique

subset_name: Mini-Python (subset of Python 3.6 analysed by the prototype abstract interpreter, later MOPSA)
detail: Only a selected representative set of builtins/primitives and a small part of the standard library supported; tests using others are not fully analysed
rationale: Focus on novel relational and generator analyses rather than imprecise support of all primitives
enforcement: static-check (prototype abstract interpreter rejects/does not support)
quote: it handles only a small part of the builtin objects and standard library

subset_name: Mini-Python (subset of Python 3.6 analysed by the prototype abstract interpreter, later MOPSA)
detail: Mini-Python: significant subset of Python 3.6 with simplified syntax removing redundant constructions and syntactic sugar
rationale: NR
quote: using a simplified syntax removing redundant constructions and syntactic sugar, that we call Mini-Python

subset_name: typy regular string types (stringin) / λRS
language: Python (via typy extensible static type system)
detail: The regular expression determining substrings to replace must be specified statically (a string literal, checked via Python's ast module).
rationale: The type system must compute the resulting regular language (lreplace) statically.
quote: as in λRS , the only restriction here is that the regular expression must be specified statically.

subset_name: typy regular string types (stringin) / λRS
language: Python (via typy extensible static type system)
detail: Safe coercions only allowed when language inclusion holds (implicit, no run-time check); otherwise an explicit checked coercion (rcheck) with a run-time check and branches is needed; coercions only between types with the same type constructor.
rationale: Guarantee that sanitization is manifest in the type; run-time checks only when going from less to more precise types.
quote: These guarantees require run-time checks only when going from less precise to more precise types.

subset_name: typy regular string types (stringin) / λRS
language: Python (via typy extensible static type system)
detail: + is typed only if both operands are regular strings; otherwise typy.TypeError.
rationale: Concatenation is related to sequential composition of regular expressions (S-T-CONCAT).
quote: The method syn_BinOp_Add synthesizes a type for the string concatenation operation if both arguments are regular strings, consistent with rule S-T-C ONCAT.

subset_name: typy regular string types (stringin) / λRS
language: Python (via typy extensible static type system)
construct: String literals of a regular string type
detail: A literal checked against stringin[r] must be in L{r}, else type error.
rationale: Corresponds to rule S-T-STRINGIN-I; soundness of the security theorem.
quote: It checks that the string is in the language of the regular expression provided as the type index

subset_name: typy regular string types (stringin) / λRS
language: Python (via typy extensible static type system)
detail: Functions are annotated with the fn type constructor and argument types (stringin[...]) at interfaces; return types inferred locally.
rationale: Annotations at function interfaces let sanitization be statically verified.
quote: Simple type annotations at function interfaces can be used to statically verify that sanitization has been performed correctly without introducing redundant run-time checks.

subset_name: Core statement subset of the IWP weakest-precondition analysis (raise, assignment, if, for; other statements approximated)
construct: Statements outside the core subset (while, del, try, and remaining AST statement nodes)
detail: Handled by the 'Other' rule: postcondition propagated as-is; soundness flag set False if the statement may modify locations read by the formula.
rationale: Loops and intricate constructs largely have no impact on results and can be ignored safely if non-interference is shown.
quote: Other statements are Python statements that do not match the syntax of the core subset specified above. These include while, del, try, and the rest of the Statement nodes specified by the Python AST.

subset_name: Core statement subset of the IWP weakest-precondition analysis (raise, assignment, if, for; other statements approximated)
detail: Not given dedicated handlers; treated via read/mod-set non-interference. For loops only guarded with membership when postcondition is True; can be unsound and imprecise.
rationale: Loops are a known thorn in weakest precondition inference.
quote: Instead of defining handlers for those constructs (e.g., loops are a known thorn in weakest precondition inference), we observe that they largely have no impact on analysis results, and therefore can be ignored.

subset_name: Core statement subset of the IWP weakest-precondition analysis (raise, assignment, if, for; other statements approximated)
construct: Loop-bound quantified variables in top-level preconditions
detail: Quantified variables reaching fit are ignored.
rationale: Target language JSON Schema does not support such functionality.
quote: if 𝑄 pre reaches the top-level fit, we ignore it because our target language, JSON Schema, does not support such functionality.

subset_name: Core statement subset of the IWP weakest-precondition analysis (raise, assignment, if, for; other statements approximated)
construct: Side effects modifying locations referenced by a precondition
detail: Soundness flag computed via reference immutability (mod/read set disjointness).
rationale: Side effects make WP unsound: exception may occur even if precondition holds.
quote: An exception can occur even if the precondition holds if a statement modifies a location referenced in the precondition as a side effect.

subset_name: Core statement subset of the IWP weakest-precondition analysis (raise, assignment, if, for; other statements approximated)
construct: Expression calls, dynamic calls on receivers, calls through function pointers
detail: Remain unresolved by the name-based call graph (no value-flow analysis).
rationale: Call graph construction for Python remains an open problem.
quote: there is no comprehensive value-flow analysis and expression calls such as self.random_state_.shuffle(ordered_idx) or est.fit(X), as well as calls through function pointers, remain unresolved.

subset_name: Core statement subset of the IWP weakest-precondition analysis (raise, assignment, if, for; other statements approximated)
detail: Cython definitions are not analysed.
rationale: NR
quote: At this point, our analysis does not look at Cython files to try to find Cython class and function definitions.

subset_name: Core statement subset of the IWP weakest-precondition analysis (raise, assignment, if, for; other statements approximated)
detail: Assumed not to modify their arguments (polymorphic w.r.t. immutability).
rationale: NR
quote: We assume that library calls are polymorphic with respect to immutability, i.e., they do not modify the argument

subset_name: Core statement subset of the IWP weakest-precondition analysis (raise, assignment, if, for; other statements approximated)
detail: self assumed a unique reference on the stack frame; any non-self x.f and y.g treated as potential aliases.
rationale: NR
quote: The above computation assumes that self is a unique reference on the current stack frame.

subset_name: Core statement subset of the IWP weakest-precondition analysis (raise, assignment, if, for; other statements approximated)
detail: Causes missed exceptions.
rationale: NR
quote: There are occasions when the IWP analysis misses exceptions as well, e.g., because of dynamic class loading.

subset_name: Core statement subset of the IWP weakest-precondition analysis (raise, assignment, if, for; other statements approximated)
detail: Formulas with 200 or more implications are pruned.
rationale: Scalability; such formulas are uninterpretable.
quote: we apply a pruning heuristic that removes formulas that are excessively large, specifically, 200 implications or more.

subset_name: NR (proposed modified Lua engine and coding rules for DO-178C)
language: Lua (candidates compared: Python/CPython, MicroPython, Lua, eLua, JavaScript/Espruino, Ruby, Perl)
detail: Automatic garbage collector must be turned off and called manually at an appropriate time from a dedicated OS task (explicit time slots)
rationale: Automatic, arbitrary GC calls break real-time requirements; affects WCET and memory consumption
quote: the automatic garbage collector must be turned off and called manually at an appropriate time.

subset_name: NR (proposed modified Lua engine and coding rules for DO-178C)
language: Lua (candidates compared: Python/CPython, MicroPython, Lua, eLua, JavaScript/Espruino, Ruby, Perl)
detail: Script-level functions controlling the GC removed from the language; externalised to a dedicated OS task
rationale: Ensure the GC is not inadvertently enabled
quote: the language-internal functions for controlling the garbage collector need to be removed to ensure that it is not inadvertently enabled.

subset_name: NR (proposed modified Lua engine and coding rules for DO-178C)
language: Lua (candidates compared: Python/CPython, MicroPython, Lua, eLua, JavaScript/Espruino, Ruby, Perl)
detail: Implicit conversions must be tagged with annotations stating the intended conversion; verification tools check implicit conversions against annotations and warn on mismatch
rationale: DO-178C requires type conversions to be 'safe and the implications understood'; weak typing/implicit casts are a potential source of programming errors
quote: Lua only supports implicit casts, which is not generally forbidden, but the DO-178C standard requires that these type conversions are "safe and the implications understood".

subset_name: NR (proposed modified Lua engine and coding rules for DO-178C)
language: Lua (candidates compared: Python/CPython, MicroPython, Lua, eLua, JavaScript/Espruino, Ruby, Perl)
detail: Coding rules covering applicable DO-178C requirements to be established; features of Lua must be limited; enforced by model-based code verification tools qualified per DO-330
rationale: Needed so scripts comply with DO-178C requirements
enforcement: coding-rule/review with static-check (proposed, DO-330 qualified tools)
quote: While the engine that will execute the Lua code can be certified by these modifications, the features of the Lua language itself have to be limited.

subset_name: NR (proposed modified Lua engine and coding rules for DO-178C)
language: Lua (candidates compared: Python/CPython, MicroPython, Lua, eLua, JavaScript/Espruino, Ruby, Perl)
detail: Direct textual interpretation preferred over JIT compilation
rationale: WCET with JIT is not significantly better than direct interpretation (compiled code may be evicted) and JIT needs considerable memory; direct interpretation behaves more deterministically
quote: This technique is more suitable for use in realtime systems, as it behaves more deterministically and the just-in-time compilation used in MicroPython does not bring any performance advantage.

subset_name: Python fragment soundly analysed by Mopsa (no recursion, eval, super, metaclasses, async)
detail: Analysis not sound for programs with recursive functions; uses detected and reported as unsoundness alarms
rationale: Outside the fragment for which the Mopsa abstract-interpretation analysis is sound; no deeper reason given
quote: Our analysis strives to be sound for Python programs that do not include recursive functions, the eval and super statements, metaclasses, nor asynchronous operators.

rationale: Outside the fragment for which the Mopsa abstract-interpretation analysis is sound; no deeper reason given
quote: Our analysis strives to be sound for Python programs that do not include recursive functions, the eval and super statements, metaclasses, nor asynchronous operators.

detail: Analysis not sound in presence of super; reported as unsoundness alarm

detail: Only field access through constant names is precisely supported; access via computed names is soundly but imprecisely supported (all possible names considered)
rationale: Precision of the analysis

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
detail: Recursive VIs excluded; 'Detect Recursions' test
rationale: IEC 61508 says to treat recursion with caution; first system developments for a new FVL must withstand higher test criteria
quote: Since the first system developments for a new FVL have to withstand higher test criteria, this work initially excludes recursive VIs.

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
construct: Dynamic array resizing functions (Insert into array, Remove from array, Initialize array, Reshape array, Create matrix, etc.)
detail: Tests exclude array/string-resizing functions; existing tests restrict Build Array and string concatenation in loops
rationale: Each call can dynamically resize the array or string, affecting memory and processor time; IEC 61508 says dynamic variables/objects should be restricted
quote: Each call to these functions can dynamically resize the array or string, affecting memory and processor time.

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
detail: 'Exclusion of global variables' test
rationale: Global variables use the same memory for each block diagram instance; runtime problems can occur
quote: Global variables represent globally acting elements in a LabVIEW software project that use the same memory for each block diagram instance. Runtime problems can occur here.

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
detail: 'Limitation of local variables' test; use only when absolutely necessary (e.g. to end parallel loops)
rationale: Test effort increases when used
quote: This work suggests using local variables just if they are absolutely necessary, for example, to end parallel loops.

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
construct: Interrupt-like structures (event structures, semaphores, notifications, occurrences, queues, rendezvous, producer-consumer)
detail: Restriction tests detect use and alert developers to the dangers
rationale: IEC 61508: interrupts should at least be restricted
quote: So it is a good idea to create a test within the VI Analyzer that detects the use of interrupt-like structures, such as the event structure or the producer-consumer design pattern and alerts developers to the dangers.

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
detail: Programmatically adding new events strictly prohibited; 'Exclusion of event registration reference' test
rationale: NR
quote: When using event structures, make sure that functionalities such as programmatically adding new events are strictly prohibited.

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
detail: 'Limitation of FPGA Interrupts' test; avoid if possible
rationale: IEC 61508 interrupt restriction
quote: If possible, avoid using it.

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
construct: Data value references and pointer-like constructs (property/method nodes, type conversion node, FPGA I/O nodes)
detail: 'Restriction of pointer-like constructs' test excludes New/Delete data value reference, Type conversion, Property node, Method node, FPGA I/O property/method node
rationale: Do not follow the data-flow principle; can lead to performance problems and damage program understanding; IEC 61508 says pointers should be restricted
quote: These structures do not follow the data flow principle and can lead to performance problems and damage the program's understanding. This work prohibits them.

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
detail: 'Type conversion point' test: tolerated number of coercion points always zero; blue constraint points at polymorphic outputs also avoided
rationale: Developer cannot reliably state output data type and conversion method; IEC 61508 prohibits automatic type conversion
quote: Automatic type conversions are prohibited [7]. Type conversions should generally be visible.

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
detail: 'Exclusion of the functions Equal and Equal 0' test; use inequality comparisons instead
rationale: NR
quote: In LabVIEW, floating-point values must not be compared with the comparison functions “Equal?” or “Equal to 0?”.

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
detail: A case for every possible situation (default case) even if not programmatically possible
rationale: NR
quote: There should be a case for every possible situation within case structures, even if the situation is programmatically not possible.

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
detail: Tests 'Exclusion of formula nodes', 'Exclusion of MathScript', 'Exclusion of DLLs'
rationale: NR
quote: The use of formula nodes and DLLs will be excluded through the created tests "Exclusion of formula nodes", "Exclusion of MathScript", and "Exclusion of DLLs".

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
detail: Max nesting depth 5 ('Depth of Nesting of Structures' test)
rationale: Allows analysable functions without significantly influencing development
quote: In the adapted test, the depth is set to 5, as this allows analyzable functions but should not significantly influence the software development process.

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
detail: Adapted 'Cyclomatic Complexity' test; diagram and panel size tests to limit module size
rationale: Limiting complexity improves reliability (IEC 61508 modular approach)
quote: The software complexity control describes the limitation of the complexity to improve reliability.

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
detail: Ratio of SubVIs to total nodes must be at least 20% for VIs with 100+ nodes
rationale: Modular approach / complexity control
quote: If the value is below a level of 20%, the test will fail.

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
detail: Max 10 calling VIs and 10 called SubVIs
rationale: Hardly restricts design freedom but creates a clear program guide
quote: A reasonable value for both should be 10, as this hardly restricts the freedom of design but creates a clear program guide.

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
construct: Wiring layout (backwards wires, wire bends, crossings, wires under objects, unused code)
detail: Wire bends max 10, crossings max 10, no backwards wires, unreachable code detected
rationale: Control structured program flow; jumps/unstructured flow limit understanding
quote: "Unused Code" finds unreachable code.

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
detail: Automatic error handling must be deactivated for each VI; individual error handling; 'Merge errors' function required
rationale: Each VI uses individual solutions to avoid side effects
quote: The "Auto Error Handling Enabled"-test can check whether the developers deactivated automatic error handling for each VI.

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
detail: No duplicate names, homoglyphs excluded, name length 5-35 characters, constants must be named
rationale: Designations like I0 and IO are easy to confuse (IEC 61508)
quote: Developers should use unique names. Designations such as I0 and IO are easy to confuse [7].

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
detail: Every connector-pane control/indicator labelled and documented; VI documentation, revision history, minimum comments
rationale: Readability and traceability
quote: the test shows whether each of these controls and indicators has a label and documentation.

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
construct: Tunnels 'Use default value if not wired'
detail: 'CheckTunnelsUseDefaultValue' test
rationale: Can lead to unassigned states and makes testing more difficult
quote: This procedure can lead to not assigned states and makes testing more difficult.

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
detail: 'CheckReferencesAreClosed' test: all references properly closed
rationale: Unclosed references can endanger system stability long-term
quote: as this can endanger system stability in the long term.

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
detail: Avoid or document stringently
rationale: Create dependencies on drivers, hardware interfaces, device access
quote: Compiler-specific features should be avoided or documented more stringently [7].

subset_name: Safe language subset for G (LabVIEW) for functional safety
detail: Ambiguous assignments should be avoided
rationale: Increases test effort
quote: This procedure increases the test effort because developers should avoid ambiguous assignments as far as possible [7].

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java and HIJA safety-critical RTSJ profiles; Ada pragma Restrictions/Profile (Ravenscar) subsets (as discussed)

detail: Identified as a feature issue under DO-178B-derived requirements.
rationale: Simplifies algorithms but sacrifices storage predictability.
quote: Recursion can simplify some algorithms, at the sacrifice of storage predictability.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java and HIJA safety-critical RTSJ profiles; Ada pragma Restrictions/Profile (Ravenscar) subsets (as discussed)

rationale: Implicit loops and conditionals in object code problematic for Level A object-code structural coverage.
quote: The compiler will either generate alternative code, possibly less efficient, or reject the program if no such alternative is available.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java and HIJA safety-critical RTSJ profiles; Ada pragma Restrictions/Profile (Ravenscar) subsets (as discussed)

detail: Flagged as complicating analysis.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java and HIJA safety-critical RTSJ profiles; Ada pragma Restrictions/Profile (Ravenscar) subsets (as discussed)

construct: Polymorphism and dynamic binding (Ada class-wide types)

rationale: Polymorphism requires pointers/dynamic allocation (memory management, GC); dynamically bound calls may invoke code distant from the call, hindering structural coverage.
quote: a dynamically bound method call may invoke code distant from the context of the call itself.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java and HIJA safety-critical RTSJ profiles; Ada pragma Restrictions/Profile (Ravenscar) subsets (as discussed)
language: Ada 2005; Java / Real-Time Specification for Java (RTSJ)
detail: Ada 2005 syntax detects unintended overriding/non-overriding at compile time; Java @override covers only one direction.
rationale: Accidental overloading/overriding errors and data coupling complicate analysis.
quote: Ada 2005 has syntax that allows the detection (at compile time) of unintended overriding or non-overriding.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java and HIJA safety-critical RTSJ profiles; Ada pragma Restrictions/Profile (Ravenscar) subsets (as discussed)
language: Ada 2005; Java / Real-Time Specification for Java (RTSJ)
detail: Each generic instantiation must be analysed individually; inline expansion introduces implementation dependences.
rationale: Instances do not directly correspond to developer source code; harder to certify.
quote: for safety certification each instantiation must be analyzed individually.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java and HIJA safety-critical RTSJ profiles; Ada pragma Restrictions/Profile (Ravenscar) subsets (as discussed)

subset_name: Predictable Java (PJ) profile

subset_name: High-integrity real-time Java profile (Ravenscar-inspired subset of the RTSJ; later known as Ravenscar-Java)

subset_name: High-integrity real-time Java profile (Ravenscar-inspired subset of the RTSJ; later known as Ravenscar-Java)

quote: The profile supports temporal predictability by demanding that classes must be loaded and initialized during the initialization phase.

subset_name: High-integrity real-time Java profile (Ravenscar-inspired subset of the RTSJ; later known as Ravenscar-Java)

subset_name: High-integrity real-time Java profile (Ravenscar-inspired subset of the RTSJ; later known as Ravenscar-Java)

subset_name: High-integrity real-time Java profile (Ravenscar-inspired subset of the RTSJ; later known as Ravenscar-Java)

detail: Ravenscar computation model: a single processor, a fixed number of tasks, a single invocation event per task (time- or event-triggered)
rationale: Accurate analysis of real-time behaviour possible with suitable restrictions on interactions allowed between tasks
enforcement: NR (Ravenscar profile, a standard Ada 2005 profile defined via restriction identifiers/configuration directives)
quote: A single invocation event per task (either time-triggered or event-triggered tasks).

subset_name: Ravenscar profile (Ada 2005); also Ada restriction identifiers such as No_Dispatch
detail: Task interaction only by means of shared data (protected objects) with mutually exclusive access
rationale: Accurate timing analysis requires suitable restrictions on the interactions allowed between tasks
enforcement: NR (Ravenscar profile, a standard Ada 2005 profile defined via restriction identifiers/configuration directives)
quote: Task interaction only by means of shared data (protected objects) with mutually exclusive access.

subset_name: Ravenscar profile (Ada 2005); also Ada restriction identifiers such as No_Dispatch
detail: Conservative approach: allow type extension and inheritance but avoid dynamic dispatching; enforceable with language-defined restriction No_Dispatch
rationale: Flow of control is not known statically but at run time; certification is based on knowing the flow of control statically so it can be tested
quote: Second, this can be enforced by use of a language defined restriction (No_Dispatch).

subset_name: Ravenscar profile (Ada 2005); also Ada restriction identifiers such as No_Dispatch
detail: Each operation may declare explicitly whether it is intended to inherit (override); the compiler checks the intention is met
rationale: Avoids accidentally confusing Initialize and Initialise, a well known hazard in object-oriented languages
failure_class: accidental non-overriding due to misspelt operation name
quote: the compiler checks that the intention is met

subset_name: Ravenscar profile (Ada 2005); also Ada restriction identifiers such as No_Dispatch
detail: Not implemented in Ada 95 design; interfaces offered instead
rationale: Complexities introduced to the language appeared to overwhelm the benefits
quote: A conscious decision was made in the design of Ada 95 to not implement general multiple inheritance

subset_name: Ravenscar profile (Ada 2005); also Ada restriction identifiers such as No_Dispatch
detail: Users can further restrict use of allocators and deallocators through appropriate restrictions
rationale: NR (context: access types designed to prevent dangling references)
quote: Users can also further restrict the use of allocators and deallocators through appropriate restrictions.

subset_name: Ravenscar profile (Ada 2005); also Ada restriction identifiers such as No_Dispatch
detail: Use of exceptions makes verification more difficult unless restrictive strategies (ISO 15942) are used
rationale: Restrictive strategies simplify the verification process
quote: Its use makes verification more difficult, unless restrictive strategies (ISO 2000) are used which simplify the verification process.

subset_name: Ravenscar profile (Ada 2005); also Ada restriction identifiers such as No_Dispatch
detail: Configuration directives restrict individual features or define a complete set of restrictions; compiler can then remove unnecessary run-time support
rationale: Full language generality may interfere with traceability and certification; restrictions facilitate analysis and safety and prevent inclusion of inactive code
quote: the full Ada language is inappropriate since the generality and flexibility may interfere with traceability and certification requirements

subset_name: Ravenscar profile (Ada 2005); also Ada restriction identifiers such as No_Dispatch
construct: Elaboration-time task activation and interrupt delivery
detail: New configuration pragma guarantees atomicity of program elaboration: no interrupts delivered and task activations deferred until all library-level elaboration code completes
rationale: Certification concerns about race conditions from tasks/interrupt handlers accessing global data before it is elaborated
failure_class: race condition (access to unelaborated global data)
quote: This eliminates all hazards that relate to tasks and interrupt handlers accessing global data prior to it having been elaborated

detail: pragma Normalize-Scalars: compiler initialises every scalar not explicitly initialised to a documented default, preferably invalid (out-of-range) value.
