quote: The purpose of the pragma is two-fold: (1)to provide predictable behavior in the presence of uninitialized scalars

subset_name: Ada 95 Annex H (Safety and Security) restrictions via pragma Restrictions
detail: pragma Reviewable: compiler must provide information (elaboration order, object lifetime, initialization analysis, machine instructions, source-object correspondence, run-time checks) for review of object code.
rationale: Safety-critical certification is often based on object code, requiring clear source-object correspondence.
quote: developers of safety-critical applications tend to certify software correctness based on generated object code, and not on high-level language source code.

subset_name: Ada 95 Annex H (Safety and Security) restrictions via pragma Restrictions
detail: pragma Inspection-Point: values of named (or all live) objects must be determinable at corresponding object-code points.
rationale: Support object code checking and potentially formal verification of object code; partial substitute for assertions.
quote: a partial or full formal mathematical verification of object code would be possible.

subset_name: Ravenscar profile ported to C/RTEMS (with Ada Zero Footprint Profile)
detail: Allowed only in the initialization phase; forbidden in mission phase.
rationale: Introduce nondeterminism in memory usage.
quote: In fact, the malloc and free functions introduce nondeterminism in the memory usage.

subset_name: Ravenscar profile ported to C/RTEMS (with Ada Zero Footprint Profile)
detail: Allowed only in the initialization phase.
rationale: They modify the initial set of tasks; rtems_task_create can also create a task hierarchy.
quote: The RTEMS functions to create, start, delete and restart tasks modify the initial set of tasks, so calling them outside of the initialization phase is inhibited.

subset_name: Ravenscar profile ported to C/RTEMS (with Ada Zero Footprint Profile)
detail: Dynamic interrupt handler change forbidden (outside initialization).
rationale: It dynamically changes the interrupt handler.
quote: The function rtems_interrupt_catch() dynamically changes the interrupt handler, so it is also forbidden.

subset_name: Ravenscar profile ported to C/RTEMS (with Ada Zero Footprint Profile)
detail: Original (__real_) version only in initialization phase; a linker-wrapped (__wrap_) version that only reads the current priority may be called anywhere.
rationale: Changing priority dynamically violates Ravenscar (No_Dynamic_Priorities); reading it does not. Call graph lacks arguments, hence LD wrapping.
enforcement: static-check (RuleChecker on gcc -fcallgraph-info call graph) plus GNU LD --wrap
quote: the second one can be programmed to only obtain the priority of the current task and can be called anywhere.

subset_name: Ravenscar profile ported to C/RTEMS (with Ada Zero Footprint Profile)
detail: Forbidden during mission phase.
rationale: Local protected objects are not allowed by Ravenscar.
quote: Local protected objects are not allowed by Ravenscar, so creating a semaphore using rtems_semaphore_create() during the mission phase is forbidden.

subset_name: Ravenscar profile ported to C/RTEMS (with Ada Zero Footprint Profile)
detail: Not allowed.
rationale: Cancellation of a semaphore could alter the execution flow.
quote: Even the cancellation of a semaphore could alter the execution flux, so calling the rtems_semaphore_delete() function is not allowed.

subset_name: Ravenscar profile ported to C/RTEMS (with Ada Zero Footprint Profile)
detail: Avoid calls to rtems_task_wake_after (maps No_Relative_Delay).
rationale: Ravenscar prohibition of relative delays.
quote: the prohibition to use relative delays can be mapped by avoiding calls to rtems_task_wake_after() function.

subset_name: Ravenscar profile ported to C/RTEMS (with Ada Zero Footprint Profile)
detail: Ada.Calendar banned; corresponding RTEMS low-precision rtems_task_wake_when also forbidden.
rationale: Coarse-granularity timing library.
quote: The Ada.Calendar package is a coarse granularity timing library and for this reason its usage is banned.

subset_name: Ravenscar profile ported to C/RTEMS (with Ada Zero Footprint Profile)
construct: Potentially blocking functions inside critical sections
detail: EnclosedFunction rule forbids e.g. wake_after/wake_when between rtems_semaphore_obtain and rtems_semaphore_release.
rationale: Ravenscar objective to avoid potentially blocking functions (Detect_Blocking).
enforcement: static-check (RuleChecker on gcc -fcallgraph-info call graph) EnclosedFunction rule
quote: The second one is needed to reach the Ravenscar objective to avoid potentially blocking functions.

subset_name: Ravenscar profile ported to C/RTEMS (with Ada Zero Footprint Profile)
detail: Execution split into Initialization and Mission phases (following Ravenscar-Java).
rationale: Makes it easy to check in a call-graph tree whether a function is called from the Init branch.
quote: the two phases execution introduced by Ravenscar-Java has been useful to scan the source code by means of an automated software tools looking for violations

subset_name: Ravenscar profile ported to C/RTEMS (with Ada Zero Footprint Profile)
detail: RTEMS semaphores configured with priority ceiling policy (Ravenscar requires priority ceiling locking).
rationale: Ravenscar locking policy.
quote: RTEMS semaphores can be configured with the priority ceiling policy

subset_name: Ravenscar profile ported to C/RTEMS (with Ada Zero Footprint Profile)
construct: Ada tasking constructs forbidden by Ravenscar
detail: Ada code compiled with Zero Footprint Profile which already excludes all Ravenscar-forbidden constructs; Ada tasking unavailable, tasking managed by RTEMS.
rationale: XtratuM4 does not support the Ada run time.
quote: using the Zero Footprint Profile, all the Ada constructs forbidden by Ravenscar are already excluded from compilation.

subset_name: Ravenscar profile ported to C/RTEMS (with Ada Zero Footprint Profile)
construct: Ada Ravenscar tasking rules (No_Task_Allocators, No_Task_Hierarchy, No_Dynamic_Priorities, No_Local_Protected_Object, No_Protected_Type_Allocators, No_Dynamic_Attachment)
detail: Static task set and static synchronization objects (as listed in the original profile).
rationale: Static Existence Model: static task set and no dynamic features that could invalidate schedulability analysis.
quote: Static Existence Model, group of rules which ensures a static task set and the absence of dynamic features that could invalidate a schedulability analysis;

subset_name: Ravenscar profile ported to C/RTEMS (with Ada Zero Footprint Profile)
detail: Implicit heap allocation forbidden.
rationale: Deterministic Memory Usage: calculate maximum memory needed.
quote: Deterministic Memory Usage, group of rules which helps to calculate the maximum amount of memory needed during execution;

subset_name: Ravenscar profile ported to C/RTEMS (with Ada Zero Footprint Profile)
construct: Select, requeue, abort, entry queues >1, complex barriers (Ada Ravenscar)
detail: No_Select_Statements, No_Requeue_Statements, No_Task_Termination, Max_Entry_Queue_Length, Simple_Barriers; requeue/select/task attributes have no C/RTEMS correspondence.
rationale: Deterministic Execution Model: normal execution flow, avoid unexpected waitings.
quote: Deterministic Execution Model, group of rules which helps to obtain a normal execution flow and to avoid unexpected waitings.

subset_name: Anima
detail: Language does not support pointers; peek/poke used for memory access instead.
rationale: Pointers lead to memory leaks and dangling references; automatic reclamation steals CPU processing.
quote: it was decided to not adopt pointers into the Anima language.

subset_name: Anima
detail: Recursion not supported.
rationale: Incompatible with statically allocated memory (would need heap-allocated locals); recursion reduces deterministic behaviour.
quote: Since the Anima language has adopted statically allocated memory management, recursion is impossible since the implementation of recursion would require heap-based allocation of local variables within the subprogram.

subset_name: Anima
detail: Generics not allowed.
rationale: Run-time characteristics generally non-deterministic and unbounded type errors can occur.
quote: The Anima language does not allow Generics since their run-time characteristics are generally non-deterministic and unbounded type errors can occur[13].

subset_name: Anima
detail: All memory (constants, globals, locals) is statically allocated; no garbage collection.
rationale: Memory usage will not exceed available resources; deterministic resource use; eliminates run-time buffer overflow errors.
quote: The main advantage of statically allocated memory is that memory usage will not exceed the available system resources.

subset_name: Anima
detail: All functions, variables, assignments and expressions must be of the same type (strong typing); conversion by explicit casting or Standard.Convert.
rationale: NR
quote: The Anima language requires all functions, variables, assignments, and expressions to be of the same type.

subset_name: Anima
detail: All threads are non-terminating; a thread cannot be contained in another thread (tasks cannot be nested).
rationale: Influenced by Ravenscar profile; deterministic concurrency.
quote: enforces the following restrictions: 1) All threads are non-terminating and 2) a thread cannot be contained in another thread.

subset_name: Anima
detail: If two tasks have the same priority the compiler downgrades the second declared task.
rationale: Prevent a race condition.
quote: If two tasks are given the same priority, the compiler will downgrade the second declared task to prevent a race-condition.

subset_name: Anima
detail: Array size must be fixed; index cannot be uninitialized and must evaluate within bounds, checked at compile time; array components must be range-constrained.
rationale: Avoid run-time bounds checks that slow execution and add size/complexity.
quote: Array operations with the Anima language must conform to a strict set of rules which are checked during compilation time: 1) The size of the array must be fixed and 2) The index of an array cannot be uninitialized

subset_name: Anima
detail: Strings must be bound with lower and upper bounds; length determined at compile time.
rationale: NR
quote: As with arrays, strings must be bound with an upper and lower bounds.

subset_name: Anima
detail: Object based only; no dynamic dispatching or dynamic polymorphism.
rationale: NR (listed as limited OOP support for real-time needs).
quote: does not support dynamic dispatching

subset_name: Anima
detail: All functions, procedures, task entries and protected objects must have exception blocks.
rationale: Prevents a fault from propagating.
quote: it requires all functions and procedures to have Exception Blocks. This prevents a fault from propagating

subset_name: Anima
detail: Loop statements must contain an exit condition (loop until).
rationale: Prevents accidental infinite loop declarations.
quote: Loop statements start with the l oop keyword and must contain a exit condition defined. This prevents accidental infinite loop declarations.

subset_name: Anima
detail: Allowed but not recommended; limited to jumping to declared label block; added to port legacy C/C++.
rationale: Legacy porting.
quote: Goto statements are allowed but are not recommended.

subset_name: Anima
detail: Each conditional must end with 'end if'.
rationale: Prevent a dangling-else condition.
quote: must end with an ”end if” for each conditional test in order to prevent a ”dangling else” condition

subset_name: Anima
detail: Only // line comments; /* */ nested comments not allowed.
rationale: Hard to follow; discourage commenting out large blocks of code.
quote: Nested comments, such as /* .... */ in C and C++, are not allowed because nested comments can be hard to follow

subset_name: Anima
detail: Every possible value must be covered or compilation error; default for large ranges; testing components with ranges not allowed.
rationale: NR
quote: Every possible value for the record definition must be covered or a compilation error will occur.

subset_name: Anima
detail: Shared data updated only under mutual exclusion, enforced at compile time.
rationale: Protection against simultaneous use of shared resource.
quote: Protected Objects allow the Anima language to support mutual exclusion which is enforced at compilation time.

subset_name: Anima
detail: A locked variable must have an event to unlock it.
rationale: Prevent deadlocking.
quote: A type that is locked must have a event to unlock the variable to prevent deadlocking.

subset_name: Anima
detail: Guarantee blocks cannot be nested; not recommended for soft real-time applications.
rationale: Small run-time overhead of conditional test.
quote: Guarantee blocks cannot be nested

subset_name: Anima
detail: Only modular types can be used with peek/poke and bitwise operations.
rationale: Modular arithmetic stays within range, preventing overflow/underflow.
quote: All arithmetic on modular types results in a value within the modular type’s valid range which prevents modular types from generate overflow or underflow errors.

subset_name: Anima
detail: Must precede any package or method declaration; cannot be embedded.
rationale: NR
quote: The include statement must be before any package or method declarations and cannot be embedded within a package or method declaration

subset_name: Ravenscar-compatible restricted Ada Distributed Systems Annex (DSA) profile
construct: Remote access types (access to remote subprograms and remote class-wide types)
detail: No Remote Access Types; connections created at elaboration time and never closed; exact number of interconnections known at configuration time; implies no distributed object paradigm
rationale: Avoid excessive blocking time from new connections after elaboration; resources for connections predictable at compile time
quote: new connections should not be established after elaboration time to avoid an excessive blocking time

subset_name: Ravenscar-compatible restricted Ada Distributed Systems Annex (DSA) profile
construct: Concurrent remote calls to the same remote subprogram
detail: A remote operation cannot be called while processing a past invocation; no wait queue; Program_Error returned to caller if destination thread busy
rationale: Predictability; eases response time analysis; no loops in call graph so no distributed deadlock
enforcement: runtime-check (Program_Error) or static tools similar to SPARK Examiner; not compiler-detectable
quote: For predictability reasons, a remote operation cannot be called while processing a past invocation (to the same remote subprogram).

subset_name: Ravenscar-compatible restricted Ada Distributed Systems Annex (DSA) profile
detail: Coordinated elaboration: application cannot start until all partitions elaborated; static number of partitions at compile time
rationale: Not acceptable in real-time system to enqueue a remote call until invoked partition completes elaboration
quote: A distributed application cannot start until all its partitions had been elaborated.

subset_name: Ravenscar-compatible restricted Ada Distributed Systems Annex (DSA) profile
detail: Already disallowed via Ravenscar No_Task_Termination and No_Abort_Statements; remote calls cannot be cancelled
rationale: Simplifies middleware implementation
quote: It should be noticed that partition termination is already disallowed

subset_name: Ravenscar-compatible restricted Ada Distributed Systems Annex (DSA) profile
detail: Optional restriction (discarded as compulsory): only asynchronous calls simplify RTA; only asynchronous operations should be used unless the application is implemented in SPARK
rationale: A communication error during a synchronous call can raise an exception
quote: Otherwise, an exception can be raised if there is a communication error while performing a synchronous call.

subset_name: Ravenscar-compatible restricted Ada Distributed Systems Annex (DSA) profile
detail: Optional restriction considered and discarded: no blocking remote call within a synchronous remote subprogram
rationale: Would simplify RTA but greatly reduce expressiveness; deadlocks already avoided by no concurrent calls
quote: although no nested calls is a sufficient condition to avoid distributed deadlocks, they are already avoided if concurrent calls are disallowed.

subset_name: Ravenscar-compatible restricted Ada Distributed Systems Annex (DSA) profile
construct: Unconstrained types / complex data structures as remote parameters
detail: Optional: allowed in general but can be disallowed depending on certification level with external ASIS tools; programmer must supply marshalling ('Write/'Read) for types with non-remote access types
rationale: Could make maximum message size impossible to calculate
quote: if unconstrained types or complex data structures (e.g. linked list) are used as parameters in a remote operation, it could be impossible to calculate the size of the maximum message.

subset_name: Ravenscar-compatible restricted Ada Distributed Systems Annex (DSA) profile
detail: Implementation requirement: the invoking task should not delegate message generation to another task; receiver processes each call at message priority; one specific thread per remote operation
rationale: Avoid priority inversion
quote: It is desirable that a task invoking a remote operation does not delegate the message generation (including data marshalling, message partitioning, composition of message headers, and even message queueing) to another task to avoid priority inversion.

subset_name: C++ subset based on MISRA-C:2012 with SPARK-like contracts (Escher Technologies)
detail: Start from MISRA-C:2012 rules (almost all mapped to the C++ subset); further ban C constructs replaced by better C++ ones and constructs with different semantics in C and C++.
rationale: Avoid known C vulnerabilities (implicit conversions, identifier reuse, '=' vs '==', precedence)
quote: Further constrain the MISRA-C:2012 rules by banning C constructs that are not needed because better C++ constructs can replace them

subset_name: C++ subset based on MISRA-C:2012 with SPARK-like contracts (Escher Technologies)
detail: Avoided by preconditions on constructs proved by formal verification; unavoidable implementation-defined behaviours described via tool configuration.
rationale: Akin to proving exception freedom in SPARK
quote: For the most part, we can avoid these behaviours by defining appropriate preconditions for the constructs concerned, and using formal verification to ensure that these preconditions are satisfied.

subset_name: C++ subset based on MISRA-C:2012 with SPARK-like contracts (Escher Technologies)
detail: Plain pointers may never be assigned NULL; the 'null' keyword must be added to allow NULL; not_null() macro converts.
rationale: Null is usually not an appropriate parameter value
quote: our tool requires that every initialization of or assignment to that pointer is not the value NULL.

subset_name: C++ subset based on MISRA-C:2012 with SPARK-like contracts (Escher Technologies)
construct: array indexing and pointer arithmetic on plain pointers
detail: Forbidden unless pointer is declared with 'array' keyword; array pointers get ghost bounds fields for preconditions; array_ref<T> template carries length and optional run-time bounds checks.
rationale: C does not distinguish pointer to object from pointer to array; enable bounds verification
quote: use of the array index and pointer arithmetic operators on such a pointer is forbidden.

subset_name: C++ subset based on MISRA-C:2012 with SPARK-like contracts (Escher Technologies)
detail: C++ static_cast/reinterpret_cast/const_cast mandated for dangerous conversions; C cast allowed only where equivalent to static_cast.
rationale: C++ conversion operators show the intended conversion and are safer
quote: we mandate the use of C++ type conversion notation for the more dangerous forms of conversion.

subset_name: C++ subset based on MISRA-C:2012 with SPARK-like contracts (Escher Technologies)
detail: All classes must have at least one constructor and all constructors must initialize all member variables.
rationale: Avoid use of uninitialized or partially initialized objects
quote: Our subset requires all classes to have at least one constructor, and all constructors to initialize all member variables of the class.

subset_name: C++ subset based on MISRA-C:2012 with SPARK-like contracts (Escher Technologies)
detail: Only single inheritance and virtual functions included; LSP verified (preconditions not strengthened, postconditions not weakened).
rationale: Local type consistency per DO-332; preferable to function pointers
quote: We therefore include single inheritance and virtual functions in our subset.

subset_name: C++ subset based on MISRA-C:2012 with SPARK-like contracts (Escher Technologies)
detail: 'override' elevated to keyword and mandated.
rationale: Overriding could be inadvertent
quote: We elevate override to the status of a keyword and mandate its use.

subset_name: C++ subset based on MISRA-C:2012 with SPARK-like contracts (Escher Technologies)
detail: Function and class templates allowed; specialization excluded for now.
rationale: Less obvious that it is needed and safe
quote: It is less obvious that template specialization is needed and safe to use, so for the time being we have not included it in our subset.

subset_name: C++ subset based on MISRA-C:2012 with SPARK-like contracts (Escher Technologies)
detail: Only side-effect-free user-defined operators allowed; type conversion operators not allowed.
rationale: NR
quote: Our C++ subset also permits side-effect free user-defined operator declarations (but not type conversion operators)

subset_name: C++ subset based on MISRA-C:2012 with SPARK-like contracts (Escher Technologies)
construct: implicit conversion of string literals to char*
detail: Banned.
rationale: Unsafe C++ feature kept only for C compatibility
quote: We ban the use of this conversion in our subset.

subset_name: C++ subset based on MISRA-C:2012 with SPARK-like contracts (Escher Technologies)
detail: If a call potentially matches multiple overloads, it must match one without automatic type conversions.
rationale: C++ overload resolution rules are complex and give surprising results
quote: then it must match one of them without the use of automatic type conversions.

subset_name: C++ subset based on MISRA-C:2012 with SPARK-like contracts (Escher Technologies)
detail: Must be declared explicit (as in MISRA-C++ and JSF-C++).
rationale: Avoid implicit type conversions
quote: we require all single-argument constructors to be declared explicit.

subset_name: C++ subset based on MISRA-C:2012 with SPARK-like contracts (Escher Technologies)
construct: static initialization order across translation units
detail: No statically-initialized object with non-trivial initialization depending on non-trivially initialized object in another translation unit.
rationale: Initialization order between translation units is undefined
quote: Our subset therefore prohibits the declaration of any statically-initialized object whose initialization is non-trivial

subset_name: C++ subset based on MISRA-C:2012 with SPARK-like contracts (Escher Technologies)
detail: Allowed only in returns() specifications and loop invariants calling the containing function, bounded by a variant; forbidden elsewhere.
rationale: Usually prohibited by safety-critical standards
quote: We therefore allow recursion in these two specification contexts and forbid it elsewhere.

subset_name: C++ subset based on MISRA-C:2012 with SPARK-like contracts (Escher Technologies)
detail: Supported for variant records but not for type conversion; ghost discriminant tracks last-written member.
rationale: NR
quote: We support the use of C union types to implement variant records, but not for conversion between different types.

subset_name: C++ subset based on MISRA-C:2012 with SPARK-like contracts (Escher Technologies)
construct: dynamic memory allocation / standard library containers
detail: Dynamic allocation generally not permitted; set/vector/map unavailable; abstract unbounded collection types for specifications only.
rationale: Generally prohibited in high-integrity embedded systems
quote: Dynamic memory allocation is generally prohibited in critical embedded software, and this in turn limits the C++ features that can be used.

subset_name: C++ subset based on MISRA-C:2012 with SPARK-like contracts (Escher Technologies)
detail: Standard library NaN-supplying functions forbidden; preconditions on sqrt() and inverse trig functions forbid NaN-producing inputs.
rationale: NaN not equal to itself breaks equational reasoning
quote: Our solution is to avoid allowing the program to generate NaNs.

subset_name: C++ subset based on MISRA-C:2012 with SPARK-like contracts (Escher Technologies)
detail: Any non-local variable written must be declared in the function's writes-clause.
rationale: Enable verification of write permissions
quote: Declares what non-local variables the function modifies.

subset_name: C++ subset based on MISRA-C:2012 with SPARK-like contracts (Escher Technologies)
detail: Not modeled in the verifier; target software typically single-threaded.
rationale: Shared-variable concurrency remains a big challenge for formal verification
quote: We have not yet attempted to model concurrency in our verification tool.

subset_name: C++ subset based on MISRA-C:2012 with SPARK-like contracts (Escher Technologies)
detail: Planned, subject to safety analysis of argument-dependent name lookup.
rationale: Safety implications not yet analysed
quote: We intend to add namespaces to our C++ subset, subject to the results of an analysis of the safety implications of the argument-dependent name lookup

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302) as implemented in the CJ4ES project
detail: SCJ memory model has no traditional heap with a garbage collector; uses scoped memory areas (immortal, mission, private).
rationale: Make execution time behaviour more predictable.
quote: In an effort to make the execution time behavior of an application more predictable, the SCJ memory model does not include a traditional heap with a garbage collector.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302) as implemented in the CJ4ES project
detail: References may only point to objects in memory areas with a longer lifetime (deeper in the scope stack).
rationale: Avoid dangling references from deallocating a memory area still in use.
enforcement: static-check (WALA-based memory safety analysis) + runtime-check (IllegalAssignmentError, hardware scope check in JOP)
quote: In order to avoid dangling references, the SCJ memory model dictates that reference assignments are allowed only when the reference points to an object stored in a memory area at a deeper level in the scope stack

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302) as implemented in the CJ4ES project
detail: Private memories used by a single MSO, cannot contain shared objects or be shared between threads; scopes form a simple stack.
rationale: Simpler structure than RTSJ 'cactus stack' enabling precise analysis and efficient checks.
quote: While private memory areas in the SCJ memory model may be nested, they cannot be shared between different threads of execution.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302) as implemented in the CJ4ES project
detail: Data shared between handlers must be in mission memory; data shared between missions in immortal memory.
rationale: NR
quote: Data shared between handlers must be allocated in mission memory, while data shared between missions must be allocated in immortal memory.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302) as implemented in the CJ4ES project
detail: Once executing, no new MSOs can be registered or started; allocation in mission memory during execution strongly discouraged.
rationale: NR
quote: Once the application is executing, no new MSOs can be registered or started and temporary objects are allocated in the MSO’s private memory.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302) as implemented in the CJ4ES project
detail: Size of needed backing store must be explicitly given by the programmer for all levels; computed by worst-case memory consumption tool.
rationale: Proper sizing of memory scopes.
quote: For all three levels, the specific size of the needed backing store must be explicitly given by the application programmer as part of the SCJ program.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302) as implemented in the CJ4ES project
detail: Level 0 supports only single-threaded applications under a cyclic executive; not allowed on multicores.
rationale: Lowest certification effort; synchronization between truly concurrent handlers undermines the simplicity of a cyclic executive.
quote: At the most restrictive level, termed level 0, only single threaded applications running under a cyclic executive are supported.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302) as implemented in the CJ4ES project
detail: Level 1 introduces preemptive scheduling with ceiling-based locks; SCJ requires priority ceiling emulation.
rationale: Avoid priority inversion.
quote: This infrastructure class is also used for implementing the priority ceiling emulation that SCJ requires to avoid priority inversion.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302) as implemented in the CJ4ES project
detail: Synchronized blocks are forbidden (synchronized methods allowed).
rationale: NR
quote: This is also the case in SCJ, although synchronized blocks are forbidden.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302) as implemented in the CJ4ES project
detail: Handlers pinned to a core at initialization and cannot migrate (partitioned scheduler).
rationale: Partitioned scheduler defined by SCJ.
quote: Handlers are pinned to a core at initialization phase and cannot migrate to a different core.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302) as implemented in the CJ4ES project
construct: Running on full RTSJ for certification
detail: SCJ can run on RTSJ but this is not recommended for certification.
rationale: Would also require certification of the full RTSJ.
quote: However, for certification purposes this is not recommended since that would also require certification of the full RTSJ.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302) as implemented in the CJ4ES project
detail: Scope-safe library versions: explicit change of allocation context, bounded internal arrays, loop exit conditions changed for loop-bound detection, constructors with unguaranteed time/memory removed.
rationale: Maintain referential integrity, predictable memory consumption and predictable WCET.
enforcement: static-check (memory safety tool, WCMC tool, JOP WCET analysis)
quote: removing constructors where we cannot guarantee the execution time or memory consumption.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302) as implemented in the CJ4ES project
construct: Prior profile restrictions (static priorities, sleep, wait/notify, dynamic class loading)
detail: Puschner and Wellings' RTSJ subset restrictions (static priorities, no sleep, no wait/notify, no dynamic class loading) are very similar to SCJ level 1 restrictions.
rationale: NR
quote: The restrictions (e.g., static priorities, no call of sleep, no wait/notify, and no dynamic class loading) are very similar to the restrictions of the level 1 of SCJ.

subset_name: Proposed restricted profile for object-oriented Ada in high-integrity systems (workshop, not yet defined)
detail: Starting hypothesis: by certification time the program is complete and all classes are known; dynamic class loading excluded.
rationale: Makes a dispatching call equivalent to a 'big case' of static calls to each possible implementation, enabling testing for certification.
quote: by the time of certification, the program is complete, and all the classes involved are known (i.e. dynamic loading of classes is a no-no for certification).

subset_name: Safety Critical Java (SCJ) Level 0, as implemented by oSCJ
detail: The heap is completely abandoned; only immortal, mission and private memory areas; programmer specifies maximum memory in advance.
rationale: Scoped memory further restricted to make certification easier.
quote: The main differences with the RTSJ are that the heap has been completely abandoned and that scoped memory has been further restricted to make certification easier.

subset_name: Safety Critical Java (SCJ) Level 0, as implemented by oSCJ
construct: Scoped memory navigation (RTSJ enter(), cactus stacks)
detail: RTSJ enter() removed and replaced by enterPrivateMemory(), which only creates a subscope if none is active; navigation restricted to linear sequences of scopes.
rationale: Simplification for certification.
quote: Unlike the RTSJ where cactus stacks are allowed, the SCJ specification restricts navigation to linear sequences of scopes.

subset_name: Safety Critical Java (SCJ) Level 0, as implemented by oSCJ
detail: Every write to a field holding an object reference must be checked (scope check); optional annotations can prove stores safe at compile time, allowing checks to be omitted.
rationale: Memory safety: prevent dangling references.
enforcement: runtime-check (VM scope checks) or static-check (SCJ annotation checker)
quote: For memory safety, every write to a field holding an object reference must be checked to prevent dangling references.

subset_name: Safety Critical Java (SCJ) Level 0, as implemented by oSCJ
detail: Restricted to periodic event handlers, aperiodic event handlers and managed threads; at Level 0 only Periodic Event Handlers.
rationale: Simplify feasibility analysis.
quote: schedulable objects have a dedicated thread and are restricted to periodic event handlers (PEH), aperiodic event handlers (AEH), and managed threads (MT) to simplify feasibility analysis.

subset_name: Safety Critical Java (SCJ) Level 0, as implemented by oSCJ
detail: Single-threaded cyclic executive with a single mission on a single CPU; all PEHs run under one thread so synchronization can be ignored; a blocking operation blocks the entire application.
rationale: Simple frame-based cyclic executive model.
quote: The first level, Level 0, provides a simple, frame-based cyclic executive model which is single threaded with a single mission.

subset_name: Safety Critical Java (SCJ) Level 0, as implemented by oSCJ
detail: These Java platform features are restricted.
rationale: Reduce the code base and simplify certification.
quote: Other features of the Java platform, such as threading, reflection, and class loading, are restricted to reduce the code base and simplify certification.

subset_name: Safety Critical Java (SCJ) Level 0, as implemented by oSCJ
detail: Programs organised as missions with a bounded number of schedulable objects, created in initialization phase, started in execution phase; mission memory reclaimed at end.
rationale: NR
quote: Each mission is composed of a bounded number of schedulable objects.

subset_name: Safety Critical Java (SCJ) Level 0, as implemented by oSCJ
detail: Different parts of the SCJ API are available in different mission phases (e.g. private memory for temporaries during initialization).
rationale: NR
quote: Different parts of the SCJ APIs are available during the various phases of a mission.

subset_name: Safety Critical Java (SCJ) Level 0, as implemented by oSCJ
detail: Classes annotated with @SCJAllowed level and allocation-context annotations (@Scope, @RunsIn), used by static analysis to prove allocation safety.
rationale: Prove allocation safety statically.
quote: these annotations are used during the static analysis to prove allocation safety of the application.

subset_name: Control-C
detail: Strong typing of all functions, variables, assignments and expressions, using C types.
rationale: Basic type safety for memory safety.
quote: (T1) The Control-C language requires strong typing of all functions, variables, assignments, and expressions, using the same types as in C.

subset_name: Control-C
detail: Casts to or from any pointer type disallowed; casts among integers, floats, chars allowed.
rationale: Type safety; illegal casts can be used to jump to code hidden in data (attack demo).
enforcement: static-check (Control-C compiler in LLVM) (checks LLVM cast instructions)
quote: (T2) The language disallows casts to or from any pointer type.

subset_name: Control-C
detail: A union may only contain mutually castable types; no pointer types in unions.
rationale: Follows from the cast restriction (type safety).
quote: (T3) A union can only contain types that can be cast to each other; consequently a union cannot contain a pointer type.

subset_name: Control-C
detail: No use of uninitialized local pointer variables; must be explicitly assigned before use or address-taken.
rationale: Dereferencing via an alias of an uninitialized pointer is unsafe and hard to detect.
quote: (T4) The language requires that there are no uses of uninitialized local pointer variables within a procedure.

subset_name: Control-C
detail: If relying on a trapped reserved address range to avoid NULL checks, no data object may exceed the reserved range size; otherwise runtime NULL checks are inserted.
rationale: Avoid checking uninitialized pointer values in global/dynamic aggregates; uninitialized pointer fields point into trapped range.
enforcement: by-construction (memory initialised to reserved address) or runtime-check
quote: (T5) If the application chooses to exploit assumption (S3) above to avoid runtime NULL pointer checks, then any individual data object

subset_name: Control-C
detail: Disallowed; array traversal must use explicit indexing.
rationale: Interprocedural array-bounds analysis becomes significantly more difficult with pointer arithmetic.
quote: (T6) Pointer arithmetic is disallowed in Control-C.

subset_name: Control-C
detail: String traversal requires strlen plus explicit indexing; other string library operations not currently permitted (safe string library planned).
rationale: Consequence of no pointer arithmetic.
quote: We do not currently permit other string library operations and we aim to provide a safe string library in the future.

subset_name: Control-C
detail: Every array index must evaluate within bounds on all control-flow paths.
rationale: Guarantees safe array accesses.
enforcement: static-check (Control-C compiler in LLVM) (Omega integer set library)
quote: (A1) The index expression used in an array access must evaluate to a value within the bounds of the array.

subset_name: Control-C
detail: Size of dynamically allocated arrays must be a positive expression.
rationale: Needed for compiler to check A1.
quote: (A2) For all dynamically allocated arrays, the size of the array has to be a positive expression.

subset_name: Control-C
detail: Loop bounds must be provably affine in array size/outer indices; index provably affine in loop indices or array size; symbolic offsets must not affect locations accessed.
rationale: Static analysis relies on decidable Presburger arithmetic (linear constraints with constant coefficients); multiplication of symbolic variables is undecidable.
quote: Exploiting static analysis based on Presburger arithmetic requires that our language only allows linear expressions with constant (known) coefficients

subset_name: Control-C
detail: Index must be provably an affine expression of the array length.
rationale: Same: enable compile-time bounds proof.
quote: (A4) If an array is accessed outside of a loop then (a) the index expression of the array has to be provably an affine expression of the length of the array.

subset_name: Control-C
detail: Replaced by region intrinsics RInit, RMalloc, RFree; no free of individual objects; whole region freed at once.
rationale: Allow static checking of dynamic memory safety without annotations or GC.
quote: There is no free operation for individual memory objects; the entire region must be freed at once.

subset_name: Control-C
detail: Only one region active at any point; RInit/RFree must alternate on every path starting with RInit; region must be active at every RMalloc.
rationale: Single active region enables compiler analysis instead of region annotations.
enforcement: static-check (Control-C compiler in LLVM) (interprocedural RegionStatus analysis)
quote: (R1) Only one region is active at any point in the program.

subset_name: Control-C
detail: Local and global scalar pointers (relaxed: those that may hold region addresses) must be explicitly reinitialized after RFree before use.
rationale: Region memory must not be accessed after a region is freed.
enforcement: static-check (Control-C compiler in LLVM) (interprocedural live-variable analysis)
quote: Because region memory must not be accessed after a region is freed, any pointer value that contains a region address must be provably dead (unused or unreachable) at a call to RFree.

subset_name: Control-C
detail: Structures/arrays containing pointers must be allocated via RMalloc or alloca, not in global/local variables (relaxed: allowed if pointers provably never hold heap addresses and address never taken).
rationale: Tracking contents of aggregate objects is generally difficult.
enforcement: static-check (Control-C compiler in LLVM) (data structure graph points-to)
quote: Rule R3(b) is necessary because tracking the contents of aggregate objects (e.g., an array of structures containing pointer fields) is generally difficult.

subset_name: Control-C
detail: Only a known set of trusted functions may be called without source; source code required for any other invoked function.
rationale: Disallow invoking untrusted functions not in the target source.
quote: We require the source code to be provided for any untrusted function invoked by the target code.

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: Tasks only at library level; no tasks local to procedures or other tasks
rationale: Static task set required for schedulability analysis; nested tasks cause unwanted visibility and termination dependencies
enforcement: compiler/translator rejects (pragma Restrictions under pragma Profile(Ravenscar))
quote: If a variable task set were to exist, then it would be impractical to perform static timing analysis of the program because of the dynamic nature of the requirements for CPU time and the meeting of deadlines.

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: No dynamic creation of tasks via allocators
rationale: Static task set for schedulability; memory for task stacks resolved before/during elaboration
enforcement: compiler/translator rejects (pragma Restrictions under pragma Profile(Ravenscar))
quote: Another consequence of requiring a static task set for schedulability analysis purposes is that the Ravenscar Profile must prohibit the dynamic creation of tasks and protected objects via allocators.

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: All tasks non-terminating; effect of termination implementation-defined; tasks end with infinite loop
rationale: Mitigate hazard of tasks terminating silently; thread of control would be permanently lost
enforcement: runtime/implementation-defined (static analysis of task body + absence of exceptions proposed)
quote: The restriction attempts to mitigate the hazard that may be caused by tasks terminating silently.

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: No abort_statements or calls to Task_Identification.Abort_Task
rationale: Significantly reduces run-time system size and complexity; reduces non-determinacy
enforcement: compiler/translator rejects (pragma Restrictions under pragma Profile(Ravenscar))
quote: The removal of abort statements (and select then abort) significantly reduces the size and complexity of the runtime system. It also reduces non-determinacy.

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: No calls to Ada.Interrupts operations; handlers attached statically via pragma Attach_Handler on library-level protected procedures
rationale: Static existence model: fixed set of interrupts for analysis
enforcement: compiler/translator rejects (pragma Restrictions under pragma Profile(Ravenscar))
quote: this implies that interrupt handlers can only be attached statically by use of pragma Attach_Handler applying to protected procedures within library-level protected objects.

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: No dependence on Ada.Dynamic_Priorities; base priority fixed
rationale: Static properties (base priority) after elaboration for timing analysis
enforcement: compiler/translator rejects (pragma Restrictions under pragma Profile(Ravenscar))
quote: thereby ensuring that the priority assigned at task creation is unchanged during task execution

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: Protected objects only at library level
rationale: Locally declared PO meaningless for synchronisation; static set of POs required for schedulability analysis
enforcement: compiler/translator rejects (pragma Restrictions under pragma Profile(Ravenscar))
quote: Furthermore, a static set of protected objects is required for schedulability analysis.

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: No dynamic creation of protected objects
rationale: Static synchronisation model for schedulability analysis
enforcement: compiler/translator rejects (pragma Restrictions under pragma Profile(Ravenscar))
quote: The restriction No_Protected_Type_Allocators prevents the dynamic creation of protected objects via Ada allocators.

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
construct: Rendezvous: select statements and task entries (No_Select_Statements, Max_Task_Entries => 0)
detail: No select statements, no task entries; synchronisation only via protected entries and suspension objects
rationale: Only primitives with time-deterministic execution properties needed for static timing analysis
enforcement: compiler/translator rejects (pragma Restrictions under pragma Profile(Ravenscar))
quote: which both exhibit time-deterministic execution properties needed for static timing analysis.

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: Implementation may not allocate from standard storage pool except for explicit allocators
rationale: Deterministic memory usage
enforcement: compiler/translator rejects (pragma Restrictions under pragma Profile(Ravenscar))
quote: The Profile contains two restrictions that are designed to prevent implicit dynamic memory allocation by the implementation.

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: No dependence on Ada.Task_Attributes
rationale: Attribute creation may cause implicit dynamic memory allocation; not compatible with static nature
enforcement: compiler/translator rejects (pragma Restrictions under pragma Profile(Ravenscar))
quote: Attribute creation may cause implicit dynamic allocation of memory.

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: At most one entry per protected object
rationale: Avoid non-determinism of selecting which of several open barriers to service; tight time bound on epilogue
enforcement: compiler/translator rejects (pragma Restrictions under pragma Profile(Ravenscar))
quote: It also avoids two or more barriers becoming open simultaneously as the result of a protected action, with the associated non-determinism of selecting which entry should be serviced first.

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: At most one task queued on an entry; violation raises Program_Error at call; static check possible if only one task calls each entry
rationale: Avoid queues with non-deterministic waiting time
enforcement: runtime-check (Program_Error); static check if each entry has a single statically identified caller
quote: This avoids the possibility of queues of tasks forming on an entry, with the associated non-determinism of the length of the waiting time in the queue.

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: Barrier is a static Boolean expression or a Boolean component of the protected object
rationale: Deterministic execution time and absence of side effects in barrier evaluation; statically avoids exceptions raised by barriers
enforcement: compiler/translator rejects (pragma Restrictions under pragma Profile(Ravenscar))
quote: ensures a deterministic execution time and absence of side effects for the evaluation of entry barriers at the epilogue of protected actions

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: No requeue statements
rationale: Ensures deterministic task release; requeue makes static analysis of task release difficult
enforcement: compiler/translator rejects (pragma Restrictions under pragma Profile(Ravenscar))
quote: The restriction No_Requeue_Statements ensures deterministic task release from protected entry barriers used for task synchronization.

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: No dependence on Ada.Asynchronous_Task_Control (asynchronous suspension)
rationale: Temporally deterministic task execution
enforcement: compiler/translator rejects (pragma Restrictions under pragma Profile(Ravenscar))
quote: This ensures that task execution is temporally deterministic.

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: No delay_relative_statement; use delay until
rationale: Non-determinism of absolute expiry time if preempted between computing and suspending
enforcement: compiler/translator rejects (pragma Restrictions under pragma Profile(Ravenscar))
quote: This statement exhibits non-determinism with respect to the absolute time at which the delay expires

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: No dependence on Ada.Calendar; use Ada.Real_Time
rationale: Calendar time has coarser precision; less accurate task release times
enforcement: compiler/translator rejects (pragma Restrictions under pragma Profile(Ravenscar))
quote: its use could result in less accuracy in task release times.

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
construct: Potentially blocking operations in protected actions (pragma Detect_Blocking)
detail: Entry calls, delay until, Suspend_Until_True etc. within a protected action must be detected and raise Program_Error
rationale: Allows efficient, temporally deterministic Ceiling_Locking on monoprocessor without mutexes or queues
enforcement: runtime-check (Program_Error via Detect_Blocking); static call-tree analysis proposed
quote: The rationale for requiring detection of potentially-blocking operations is to allow a highly efficient and temporally deterministic implementation of Ceiling_Locking policy on a mono-processor.

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: Ceiling_Locking and FIFO_Within_Priorities required
rationale: Absence of deadlock; bounded priority inversion; minimal worst-case blocking
quote: The Profile definition assures absence of deadlocks by requiring use of an appropriate locking policy.

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: All inter-task/interrupt communication via protected, suspension or atomic objects (recommended; detection not mandated)
rationale: Prevent erroneous execution from concurrent unprotected access
enforcement: static-check (proposed, given statically identifiable global use); not mandated
quote: This prevents any erroneous execution that might arise if concurrent access (that includes a write operation) to the same unprotected shared variable is permitted.

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: Defer task activation and interrupt attachment until elaboration complete; shared variables initialised during library-level elaboration
rationale: Avoid access-before-elaboration, uninitialised data and races during initialisation
quote: This scenario could give rise to the following undesirable effects

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: Recommended only with static proof that no run-time check failures can occur
rationale: Suppressed checks make execution erroneous (undefined behaviour) if check would fail
quote: the recommendation for high integrity systems is that the No_Exceptions restriction should only be used in conjunction with verification and analysis techniques

subset_name: Ada Ravenscar Profile
detail: Each task has a single invocation event; cyclic/sporadic tasks with infinite loop and no other voluntary suspension
rationale: Undermining schedulability analysis
quote: All tasks must have a single invocation event and allow other parameters to be analysed or measured

subset_name: JSR-302 Safety-Critical Java (baseline and annotated) and PERC Pico
detail: Only MissionMemory (sized at mission initialization) and PrivateMemory (on handler start or explicit request) scopes, instantiated only by infrastructure.
rationale: Simplify run-time model and guarantee memory fragmentation does not prevent timely creation of memory areas
quote: Unlike the RTSJ, JSR-302 supports only two very restrictive scope types.

subset_name: JSR-302 Safety-Critical Java (baseline and annotated) and PERC Pico
construct: references from outer scopes to inner-nested scopes
detail: Objects in a scope may never refer to objects in more inner-nested scopes; violations throw IllegalAssignmentError in baseline JSR-302; annotated JSR-302 checker statically guarantees absence.
rationale: Scope assignment safety; avoid run-time error termination
enforcement: runtime-check (baseline); static-check (JSR-302 annotation checker) for annotated
quote: objects residing within a particular memory scope are never allowed to refer to objects residing within more inner-nested memory scopes.

subset_name: JSR-302 Safety-Critical Java (baseline and annotated) and PERC Pico
detail: Annotated classes instantiated only when current scope matches named scope; unannotated classes may not escape their allocation scope; certain subclass-to-superclass upcasts forbidden.
rationale: Static enforcement of scope safety
quote: With Annotated JSR-302, classes that are not annotated are not allowed to escape the scope in which they are allocated.

subset_name: JSR-302 Safety-Critical Java (baseline and annotated) and PERC Pico
detail: Annotations are mandatory (not optional) and interact with code generation; scopes entered/exited implicitly and sized automatically.
rationale: Clarify scoped-memory intentions; enable static analysis of scope safety and sizes
quote: Unlike JSR302, the use of annotations in this semantic model is not optional.

subset_name: JSR-302 Safety-Critical Java (baseline and annotated) and PERC Pico
detail: Programmers must insert stylized assertions bounding loop iterations; compiler rejects otherwise; bounds not proved but checked by AssertionError when testing with assertions enabled.
rationale: Automatic computation of scope sizes and thread stack sizes
quote: The PERC Pico compiler rejects programs that are declared to be @StaticAnalyzable if the required iteration bounds are not specified.

subset_name: JSR-302 Safety-Critical Java (baseline and annotated) and PERC Pico
construct: BigInteger and variable-size objects in @StaticAnalyzable code
detail: Assertions bounding the digits must precede construction/allocation.
rationale: Memory requirements computable only with a bound
quote: the memory requirements can only be computed (for any given context) if the programmer supplies an assertion to bound the value to be stored within the constructed BigInteger object.

subset_name: JSR-302 Safety-Critical Java (baseline and annotated) and PERC Pico
detail: No API to refer to a scope, query its size, find an object's scope, or allocate from a chosen scope.
rationale: Direct manipulation would make static analysis of scope safety much harder
quote: If application software were allowed to directly manipulate scopes, then static analysis of scope safety would be much more difficult.

subset_name: JSR-302 Safety-Critical Java (baseline and annotated) and PERC Pico
detail: Immortal objects can only refer to other immortal objects (both PERC Pico and JSR-302).
rationale: Scope safety
quote: Immortal objects can only refer to other objects residing in immortal memory.

subset_name: JSR-302 Safety-Critical Java (baseline and annotated) and PERC Pico
detail: JSR-302 requires all classes loaded into immortal memory before initialization; static variables refer only to immortal memory; in mixed-model applications reflection libraries are not supported.
rationale: NR
quote: JSR-302 requires all classes to be loaded into immortal memory prior to initialization of the application.

subset_name: JSR-302 Safety-Critical Java (baseline and annotated) and PERC Pico
construct: mission constructor arguments in mixed-model deployment
detail: Must be primitive types or references to declared interfaces (of interfaces and primitives); objects never shared directly across models; cross-model calls via proxies with run-time scope checks.
rationale: Isolate scope assignment issues between semantic models
quote: The proxy generation tool requires that all arguments to the mission’s constructors are either primitive types or are references to a declared interface.

subset_name: JSR-302 Safety-Critical Java (baseline and annotated) and PERC Pico
detail: Traditional GC Java never used at DO-178B level A or B; used at levels C and D.
rationale: GC adds complexity to binary, schedulability analysis and certification
quote: Common practice today is that tracing garbage collection is never used in DO-178B level A or level B software.

subset_name: High-integrity subset of the Ada Distributed Systems Annex (DSA) with Ravenscar and SPARK
detail: Only asynchronous RPCs (APCs, pragma Asynchronous with in parameters only) are permitted; producer-consumer (dataflow) model.
rationale: Synchronous RPC causes local blocking, pessimistic timing analysis, hard-to-derive worst-case blocking with nested RPCs, and failure-handling requirements.
quote: Thus, only asynchronous RPCs, i.e. APCs are permitted.

subset_name: High-integrity subset of the Ada Distributed Systems Annex (DSA) with Ravenscar and SPARK
construct: Remote Access Subprogram (RAS) and Remote Access to Class Wide type (RACW)
detail: Not permitted.
rationale: SPARK restrictions: no access types or dynamic dispatching.
quote: Both RAS and RACW are not permitted within the restrictions of SPARK (i.e. no access types or dynamic dispatching is permitred).

subset_name: High-integrity subset of the Ada Distributed Systems Annex (DSA) with Ravenscar and SPARK
detail: Consumer task and protected object must be in the same partition.
rationale: Only asynchronous RPC allowed.
quote: Note, that the consumer and the protected object must always be within the same partition as only asynchronous RPC are allowed.

subset_name: High-integrity subset of the Ada Distributed Systems Annex (DSA) with Ravenscar and SPARK
construct: Dynamic allocation of tasks and protected objects (Ravenscar)

rationale: Ravenscar limits concurrency to objects allowing easy timing analysis.
quote: The limitations as imposed by Ravenscar include no dynamic allocation of tasks or protected objects,

subset_name: High-integrity subset of the Ada Distributed Systems Annex (DSA) with Ravenscar and SPARK
detail: Single entry only, at most one task queuing, simple Boolean guard; no entry queues; synchronization only one-to-one.
rationale: Easy timing analysis.
quote: The fact that entry queues are disallowed means that synchronization can only be used o n a one to one scale.

subset_name: High-integrity subset of the Ada Distributed Systems Annex (DSA) with Ravenscar and SPARK
detail: Tasks are not allowed entries; communication via protected objects.
rationale: Easy timing analysis.
quote: As tasks are not allowed entries in Ravenscar, they must communicate via protected objects.

subset_name: High-integrity subset of the Ada Distributed Systems Annex (DSA) with Ravenscar and SPARK
detail: No use of exceptions; PCS Communication_Error for asynchronous calls is of little value and may be discarded.
rationale: Static analysability.
quote: Restrictions of SPARK include no use of exceptions and no dynamic operations, including memory or run-time dispatching.

subset_name: High-integrity subset of the Ada Distributed Systems Annex (DSA) with Ravenscar and SPARK
construct: Dynamic operations: dynamic memory, run-time dispatching, access types (SPARK)
detail: No dynamic memory, run-time dispatching or access types.
rationale: Static analysability.
quote: The motivation for SPARK is static analysability, hence the disallowing of features such as avcess types or dynamic operations.

subset_name: High-integrity subset of the Ada Distributed Systems Annex (DSA) with Ravenscar and SPARK
construct: Dynamic task creation in PCS task pool
detail: GLADE's dynamic task creation when pool is exhausted unavailable; fixed pool gives static upper bound on requests.
rationale: Ravenscar forbids dynamic creation of tasks.
quote: This solution is not available to us, as Ravenscar forbids d y n a m i c creation o f tasks.

subset_name: High-integrity subset of the Ada Distributed Systems Annex (DSA) with Ravenscar and SPARK
detail: System.RPC interface is not SPARK compliant because it relies on Ada.Streams, which relies heavily on tagged types; possible use if calls statically bound, but this departs from SPARK/Ravenscar.

subset_name: Type-safe subset of C with semantic restrictions (T1-T3, P1-P3, A1-A5) checked by the Dhurjati et al. safety-checking compiler
detail: C type system further restricted by T2 and T3.
rationale: Compiler techniques apply only to programs following basic type-safety rules.
quote: (T1) Our type system is the same as that of the C language, but is further restricted by rules T2 and T3.

subset_name: Type-safe subset of C with semantic restrictions (T1-T3, P1-P3, A1-A5) checked by the Dhurjati et al. safety-checking compiler
detail: Casts to a pointer type from any other type disallowed, except some pointer-to-pointer casts between primitive types of same or smaller size.
rationale: Type safety; needed for pool allocation and memory safety.
quote: (T2) Casts to a pointer type from any other type are disallowed, except certain pointer-to-pointer casts for compatible targets.

subset_name: Type-safe subset of C with semantic restrictions (T1-T3, P1-P3, A1-A5) checked by the Dhurjati et al. safety-checking compiler
detail: Union may contain only mutually castable types (e.g. not a pointer and a non-pointer).
rationale: Unions are implemented using casts.
quote: (T3) A union can contain only types that can be cast to each other, for example, a union cannot include a pointer and a non-pointer type.

subset_name: Type-safe subset of C with semantic restrictions (T1-T3, P1-P3, A1-A5) checked by the Dhurjati et al. safety-checking compiler
detail: Every local pointer variable must be initialized before being used or having its address taken.
rationale: Taking address of uninitialized pointer makes later uses hard to detect statically.
quote: (P1) Every local pointer variable must be initialized before being referenced, that is, before being used or having its address taken.

subset_name: Type-safe subset of C with semantic restrictions (T1-T3, P1-P3, A1-A5) checked by the Dhurjati et al. safety-checking compiler
detail: No individual (non-array) data type larger than the reserved address range; otherwise run-time null checks needed.
rationale: Uninitialized pointer fields are set to base of reserved range so dereference triggers safe hardware trap.
enforcement: by-construction (initialization to reserved range; hardware trap)
quote: (P2) Any individual data type (i.e., not an array) should be no larger than the size of the reserved address range.

subset_name: Type-safe subset of C with semantic restrictions (T1-T3, P1-P3, A1-A5) checked by the Dhurjati et al. safety-checking compiler
detail: Address of a stack location cannot be stored in a heap object or global, nor returned from a function.
rationale: Prevent pointers into dead stack frames that could violate type safety.
enforcement: static-check (LLVM safety-checking compiler) (escape analysis on DS graph)
quote: (P3) The address of a stack location cannot be stored in a heap-allocated object or a global variable and cannot be returned from a function.

subset_name: Type-safe subset of C with semantic restrictions (T1-T3, P1-P3, A1-A5) checked by the Dhurjati et al. safety-checking compiler
detail: Explicit free permitted, but heap is transformed into type-homogeneous pools (automatic pool allocation) whose memory is not released to the system until pooldestroy; dangling pointers can only reach same-type objects.
rationale: Memory safety without GC: type homogeneity principle; dangling pointer dereference cannot cause a type violation.
quote: If a freed memory block holding a single object were to be reallocated to another object of the same type and alignment, then dereferencing dangling pointers to the previous freed object cannot cause a type violation.

subset_name: Type-safe subset of C with semantic restrictions (T1-T3, P1-P3, A1-A5) checked by the Dhurjati et al. safety-checking compiler
detail: Pools with allocations from other pools between poolfree and pooldestroy may increase memory; must be approved by the programmer via compiler option.
rationale: Potential increase in memory consumption.
enforcement: static-check (LLVM safety-checking compiler) (pool categorization) + programmer approval
quote: Our transformation in this case may lead to increased memory consumption, and we require this to be approved by the programmer via a compiler option.

subset_name: Type-safe subset of C with semantic restrictions (T1-T3, P1-P3, A1-A5) checked by the Dhurjati et al. safety-checking compiler
detail: Index must be within array bounds on all control-flow paths.
rationale: Guarantees safe array accesses.
quote: (A1) The index expression used in an array access must evaluate to a value within the bounds of the array.

subset_name: Type-safe subset of C with semantic restrictions (T1-T3, P1-P3, A1-A5) checked by the Dhurjati et al. safety-checking compiler
detail: Size of dynamically allocated arrays must be a positive expression.
rationale: Needed so compiler can check A1.
quote: (A2) For all dynamically allocated arrays, the size of the array must be a positive expression.

subset_name: Type-safe subset of C with semantic restrictions (T1-T3, P1-P3, A1-A5) checked by the Dhurjati et al. safety-checking compiler
construct: Array index expressions and loop bounds (A3)
detail: Index must be provably affine in array size, or inside loops with affine index of loop variables and affine loop bounds; symbolic offsets must not affect locations accessed. Pointer arithmetic handled uniformly under same rules.
rationale: Satisfiability of integer constraints with symbolic multiplication is undecidable; Presburger arithmetic requires linear expressions with constant coefficients.
quote: Exploiting static analysis based on Presburger arithmetic requires that programs only use linear expressions with (known) constant coefficients

subset_name: Type-safe subset of C with semantic restrictions (T1-T3, P1-P3, A1-A5) checked by the Dhurjati et al. safety-checking compiler
detail: Only trusted library routines with specified preconditions may be used and arguments must satisfy the preconditions (e.g. read buf.size >= count).
rationale: Prevent buffer overruns within library routines.
quote: (A4) A set of trusted library routines with specified preconditions may be used, and arguments passed to those routines must satisfy the preconditions.

subset_name: Type-safe subset of C with semantic restrictions (T1-T3, P1-P3, A1-A5) checked by the Dhurjati et al. safety-checking compiler
detail: Program cannot access last element of a char array (always null-initialized); only trusted calls like strlen may.
rationale: Ensure string routines will not read beyond the array.
quote: (A5) The last element of a character array cannot be accessed by the program (trusted library calls like strlen can access it).

subset_name: Type-safe subset of C with semantic restrictions (T1-T3, P1-P3, A1-A5) checked by the Dhurjati et al. safety-checking compiler
detail: Source of all non-trusted functions must be available to the compiler.
rationale: Whole-program interprocedural analysis.
quote: We assume (and check) that the source code of all other functions is available to the compiler.

subset_name: Type-safe subset of C with semantic restrictions (T1-T3, P1-P3, A1-A5) checked by the Dhurjati et al. safety-checking compiler
detail: Program must be single threaded.
rationale: Assumption of current work; multithreading not supported.
quote: We also require that the program be single threaded.

subset_name: Type-safe subset of C with semantic restrictions (T1-T3, P1-P3, A1-A5) checked by the Dhurjati et al. safety-checking compiler
construct: Array accesses depending on recursive functions
detail: Implementation cannot prove safety of accesses depending on recursive functions and rejects them.
rationale: Such accesses very rarely provably affine.
quote: Our current implementation cannot prove the safety of accesses which depend on recursive functions and hence simply rejects them.

subset_name: Type-safe subset of C with semantic restrictions (T1-T3, P1-P3, A1-A5) checked by the Dhurjati et al. safety-checking compiler
detail: Assumed absent; must be guaranteed by hardware overflow exceptions or trap-on-overflow instructions after relevant arithmetic.
rationale: Static verification of no overflow is extremely difficult.
quote: Our static checking algorithm assumes that there will be no overflows and underflows in the integer arithmetic involved in index or array size computations.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Ravenscar-Java VM does not support GC; only immortal and linear-time scoped memory; heap used to start main is treated as immortal.
rationale: Reluctance to rely on real-time GC for high integrity systems; predictability.
quote: Although real-time garbage collection has made significant advances in recent years [16, 32], there is still a reluctance to rely on it for high integrity systems.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Initialisation phase creates all memory areas, schedulable objects and loads all classes; mission phase only executes; properties of memory areas and scheduling parameters cannot be altered in mission phase.
rationale: System-level activities hinder timing analysis and precise memory utilization analysis; worst-case memory bounds infeasible otherwise.
quote: If such events are blended with complex program logic, it will become infeasible to obtain even the worst-case memory consumption bounds.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Objects needed for application lifetime allocated in immortal memory only in initialisation phase.
rationale: Prevent memory exhaustion or corruption.
quote: objects (including memory area objects) that are needed for the lifetime of the application should be allocated in the area only in the initialisation phase.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: LTMemory areas not shared by more than one schedulable object; one active LTMemory per schedulable object; share data via immortal memory.
rationale: Hard to validate correct use when shared; eliminates dynamic memory access checking overheads and simplifies VM.
enforcement: static-check (profile conformance test at compile time)
quote: Scoped memory areas will not be shared by more than one schedulable object as it is difficult to costeffectively validate if a given scoped memory area is exploited correctly when different schedulable objects share it.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Access to LTMemory areas must not be nested.
rationale: Otherwise VM must perform heavy assignment checks and single-parent rule at run time, with ambiguous time/memory requirements.
enforcement: static-check (profile conformance test at compile time)
quote: access to LTMemory areas must not be nested and LTMemory areas must not be shared between Schedulable objects

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Size of all memory objects static; scoped memory size cannot be altered once set; other RTSJ memory area classes disallowed.
rationale: Cost of extending size at runtime; statically analysed program should never run short of memory.
quote: The size of all memory objects must be static and not be extended in the course of the program

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Assignments in immortal memory must not reference objects in LTMemory; to be validated statically by points-to/escape analysis.
rationale: Could result in a dangling reference.
quote: any assignment to memory in immortal (or heap) must be checked to ensure the referenced object does not reside in an LTmemory area (as this could potentially result in a dangling reference)

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
construct: Dynamic class loading in mission phase
detail: ClassLoader, Class.forName, URLClassLoader, SecureClassLoader must not be used in mission phase.
rationale: Main source of delay and unpredictable memory use.
enforcement: static-check (profile conformance test at compile time)
quote: dynamic class loading is one of the main sources of delay and unpredictable use of memory.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: No finalizers on immortal objects; LTMemory finalizers compact, must not block or acquire locks used by other threads; overhead included in schedulability analysis.
rationale: Possible execution delay and deadlock when thread holding a lock enters scope whose finalizer wants that lock; applications do not terminate.
quote: On the whole, finalizers should be as compact as possible and must not block.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Recursive (incl. mutually recursive) calls must be avoided; may be relaxed if memory consumption and termination formally verified and bounded.
rationale: Can dramatically consume memory; erroneous termination condition causes unbounded recursion.
enforcement: static-check (profile conformance test at compile time)
quote: Recursive method calls (including mutually recursive calls, and loops in some cases) can dramatically consume available memory space at runtime, and an erroneous termination condition can cause unbounded recursion.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Priority Ceiling Emulation for all synchronized methods/blocks.
rationale: Supports offline fixed-priority schedulability analysis.
quote: Priority Ceiling Emulation must be implemented and used for all synchronized methods/blocks,

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Must be periodic or sporadic with minimum inter-arrival times, programmed using PeriodicThread and SporadicEventHandler.
rationale: Facilitate offline schedulability analysis.
enforcement: static-check (profile conformance test at compile time)
quote: Schedulable objects have to be either periodic or sporadic with minimum inter-arrival times

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Not allowed.
rationale: Complex feature; conformance prevents errors such as deadlocks; simplifies data race analysis.
enforcement: static-check (profile conformance test at compile time)
quote: Object queues are not allowed (i.e. no wait, notify, and notifyAll operations),

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: ATC not allowed.
rationale: Complex feature hard to analyse; RTSJ run-time overhead source.
quote: Asynchronous Transfer of Control (ATC) mechanism is not allowed,

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
construct: Processing groups, overrun and deadline-miss handlers
detail: Not supported.
rationale: NR
quote: Processing groups, overrun and deadline-miss handlers are not supported,

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Not permitted.
rationale: NR
quote: continue and break statements in loops are not permitted, and

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Not allowed.
rationale: Conformance test prevents side effects in expressions.
enforcement: static-check (profile conformance test at compile time)
quote: Expressions with possible side effects are not allowed.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Reads and writes on a shared object in a method enclosed within the same synchronized block/method.
rationale: Avoid data races arising from weak Java memory model.
quote: any reads and writes on a shared object in a method must be enclosed within the same synchronized block (or method) in order not to have any data races

subset_name: Predictable real-time Java profile (three-layer Creation/Execution/Recycle architecture)
detail: Key threads allocated in Immortal Memory as NoHeapRealtimeThreads; scoped LTMemory not collected by GC; memory recovered by explicit periodic Recycle Layer instead
rationale: GC start time and duration unpredictable; other threads suspended when GC starts
quote: The time behavior of automatic garbage collector (GC) in Java is unpredictable; this is because both the starting up time of GC and the duration of each action in GC rely on dynamic property

subset_name: Predictable real-time Java profile (three-layer Creation/Execution/Recycle architecture)
construct: Standard Java threads and RealtimeThread on heap
detail: Profile does not support standard Java threads; RealtimeThread not used directly; only NoHeapRealtimeThread (and PeriodicThread subclass)
rationale: Heap affected by GC causing uncertain delay; avoids synchronisation issues between NHRTs and regular threads
quote: Besides, the profile does not support standard Java threads.

subset_name: Predictable real-time Java profile (three-layer Creation/Execution/Recycle architecture)
detail: Classes loaded once by creating thread groups in the Creation Layer
rationale: Makes memory requirements hard to predict; class initialization chains make initialization time unpredictable
quote: But the dynamic class loading mechanism will make it difficult to predict the memory space required by the system running.

subset_name: Predictable real-time Java profile (three-layer Creation/Execution/Recycle architecture)
detail: Only Immortal Memory and LTMemory used
rationale: VTMemory allocation time variable and relatively long; LTMemory linear-time allocation increases predictability
quote: In order to increase the predictability and shorten the response time of a system, we use LTMemory for storage area of Scoped Memory.

subset_name: Predictable real-time Java profile (three-layer Creation/Execution/Recycle architecture)
detail: LTMemory not nested and not shared between schedulable objects (one thread per LTMemory)
rationale: Nesting legitimacy checks cost time and space, increase complexity and influence program analysis
quote: If the memory space supports nested designs, the virtual machine needs to check the legitimacy of nested, and this checking will not only bring costs of time and space, but also will increase the complexity of programs

subset_name: Predictable real-time Java profile (three-layer Creation/Execution/Recycle architecture)
detail: Priority Ceiling Emulation Protocol
rationale: Traditional synchronisation causes priority inversion
quote: Traditional synchronous methods will cause the inversion of priorities. In order to avoid the inversion of priorities, this profile adopts the Priority Ceiling Emulation Protocol

subset_name: Predictable real-time Java profile (three-layer Creation/Execution/Recycle architecture)
detail: Creation Layer creates all necessary objects at once, default in Immortal Memory; objects in Immortal Memory not released during operation (except Recycle Layer for finished thread groups)
rationale: Predictability of memory
quote: The Creation Layer once creates all necessary objects that the application needs.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
