detail: Ravenscar-Java VM does not support GC; heap usable only as part of immortal memory.
rationale: Predictability and efficiency of the VM.
quote: For example, a Ravenscar-Java VM (RVM) does not support garbage collection.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: All threads, memory objects, event handlers, events, scheduling parameters and classes created/loaded in initialisation phase by Initializer thread at highest priority; no schedulable objects created in mission phase.
rationale: Creating schedulable objects in mission phase hampers static memory usage analysis.
quote: It is also disallowed to create or instantiate any schedulable objects in the mission phase as this will hamper static memory usage analysis.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Objects needed for application lifetime allocated in immortal memory only during initialisation.
rationale: Prevent memory exhaustion or corruption.
quote: in an attempt to prevent memory exhaustion or corruption, objects (including memory area objects) that are needed for the lifetime of the application should be allocated in the area only in the initialisation phase.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Only immortal and LTMemory areas (plus physical/raw if needed); all memory areas created in initialisation; sizes static and not extended; other RTSJ memory areas disallowed.
rationale: Predictable and bounded memory use.
quote: The size of all memory objects must be static and not be extended in the course of the program. Any other memory area objects defined in the RTSJ are disallowed

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Access to LTMemory areas must not be nested and areas not shared between schedulable objects.
rationale: Aid efficient RVM and simplify timing and memory usage analyses.
quote: To aid in the production of an efficient RVM and to simplify timing and memory usage analyses, access to LTMemory areas must not be nested and LTMemory areas must not be shared between Schedulable objects.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Use of class loaders in mission phase restricted.
rationale: Predictable memory utilisation.
quote: The rules place restrictions on, for example, the use of class loaders in the mission phase, on the use of specific memory area objects (and garbage collector), and on recursive method calls.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Restricted (details in technical report).
rationale: Predictable memory utilisation.
quote: The rules place restrictions on, for example, the use of class loaders in the mission phase, on the use of specific memory area objects (and garbage collector), and on recursive method calls.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Use or overriding of java.lang.Thread to create threads disallowed; Thread class reduced.
rationale: Most methods obsolete for high integrity real-time; only periodic threads and sporadic event handlers supported.
quote: the profile does not support regular threads by disallowing the use or overriding of the class java.lang.Thread to create threads.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Not directly available to application programmers; use PeriodicThread and SporadicEventHandler.
rationale: RealtimeThread may use the heap; AsyncEventHandler hinders accurate timing and memory analyses.
quote: The RealtimeThread and AsyncEventHandler classes are not directly available to the applications programmer, as the former may use the heap memory, whereas the latter hinders accurate timing and memory analyses.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Scheduling characteristics and memory areas statically allocated in initialisation and not changed; set methods excluded; Schedulable is an empty interface.
rationale: Facilitate fixed-priority scheduling and schedulability analysis.
quote: Attributes such as scheduling characteristics and memory areas must be statically allocated to schedulable objects in the initialisation phase, and shall not be changed afterwards

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
construct: Scheduler feasibility checks, ImportanceParameters, aperiodic activities
detail: Only fixed-priority scheduling; schedulers perform no feasibility checks; AperiodicParameters undefined.
rationale: All schedulability analysis performed offline; no dynamic admission control needed.
quote: Overall, this approach does not necessitate any dynamic feasibility test and admission control by the RVM at runtime.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Periodic threads use waitForNextPeriod; sleep() and other mechanisms should not be used.
rationale: Prone to inaccurate timing model.
quote: Other mechanisms (e.g. sleep() method) are prone to have an inaccurate timing model, thus should not be used.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Events and handlers unchanged once set up; each handler bound to one server thread and vice versa; handlers bound at event creation.
rationale: Predictability.
quote: For predictability, it is assumed that each handler is bound to one server thread and each server thread has only one handler bound to it.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
construct: Processing groups, overrun and deadline-miss handlers
detail: Not supported.
rationale: Processing groups need runtime feasibility support hampering static timing analysis; handlers unnecessary as schedulability analysed offline.
quote: Processing groups (i.e. instances of the ProcessingGroupParameters class) are not supported in the profile, as they require runtime support for the scheduler to determine the feasibility

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Priority ceiling protocol (PriorityCeilingEmulation) must be implemented and explicitly used for all objects with synchronized blocks or methods.
rationale: Prevent unbounded priority inversions and possible deadlocks.
quote: in order to prevent unbounded priority inversions and possible deadlocks, the priority ceiling protocol (PriorityCeilingEmulation class) must be implemented and explicitly used

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Not supported; condition synchronization via sporadic event handlers.
rationale: Ensures timing properties of synchronization are properly addressed.
quote: All condition synchronization between real-time threads must be via sporadic event handlers as this ensures that the timing properties of the synchronization are properly addressed.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Timer and subclasses not available; WaitFreeQueues not required.
rationale: Periodic/sporadic classes suffice; no regular Java threads to communicate with.
quote: the Timer and its subclasses are not necessary and not available.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
construct: Asynchronous Transfer of Control and thread aborting
detail: ATC and any thread aborting mechanisms disallowed.
rationale: One of the most complicated RTSJ features; hinders timing and functional analyses.
quote: The Asynchronous Transfer of Control (ATC) mechanism is not allowed, as it is one of the most complicated features of the RTSJ and hinders timing and functional analyses [10].

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: All user-defined classes must include constructors that initialise all internal variables and objects.
rationale: Predictability of control and data flow for static analysis and WCET.
quote: All user-defined classes must include constructors that initialise all internal variables and objects.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Should be minimised.
rationale: Predictability of control and data flow.
quote: Dynamic method binding should be minimised. In particular, method overriding and the use of interfaces should be minimised.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Disallowed.
rationale: Predictability of control flow.
quote: Use of continue and break statements in loops is disallowed.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: All constraints, e.g. in for loops, must be static.
rationale: Predictability of control flow / WCET analysis.
quote: All constraints, such as one used in a for loop, must be static.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Must be eliminated.
rationale: Predictability of data flow.
quote: Compound expressions in parameter passing to methods must be eliminated.

subset_name: Ravenscar-Java profile
detail: Should be disallowed.
rationale: Predictability of data flow.
quote: Expressions whose values are dependent on the order of evaluations should be disallowed.

subset_name: Restricted IEC 61131-3 subset for high integrity applications (extending PLCopen safety specification)
detail: Boolean literals must be prefixed (BOOL#1) or TRUE/FALSE; bit string literals must carry type prefix (WORD#1234); bare numerals are integer literals.
rationale: Strong type safety; type should not be determined from context
quote: Strongly typed (safe) language should not leave this determination to be done from the context in which the literal is used.

subset_name: Restricted IEC 61131-3 subset for high integrity applications (extending PLCopen safety specification)
detail: Not allowed; within functions they break idempotence; in FBs/programs they bypass external interface.
rationale: Functions could become non-idempotent; data transfer outside defined interfaces
quote: directly represented variables are no longer required, and their use should therefore not be allowed.

subset_name: Restricted IEC 61131-3 subset for high integrity applications (extending PLCopen safety specification)
detail: May only be defined in configurations and passed by reference as external variables; not within programs and function blocks; alternatively prohibit them to fix FBD evaluation order dependence.
rationale: Avoid data exchange bypassing external interfaces and evaluation-order dependence
quote: The definition of located variables should also be restricted to configurations, and simply not allowed within programs and functions blocks.

subset_name: Restricted IEC 61131-3 subset for high integrity applications (extending PLCopen safety specification)
construct: shared global variables across pre-emptive tasks
detail: Either no pre-emptive multitasking or the compiler forbids passing the same global variable to programs in distinct tasks (PLCopen forbids multitasking).
rationale: Remove race conditions; synchronization primitives would add undesirable complexity (priority inheritance)
quote: In order to remove the possibility of race-conditions occurring, then either pre-emptive multitasking cannot be used, or variables must not be shared.

subset_name: Restricted IEC 61131-3 subset for high integrity applications (extending PLCopen safety specification)
construct: global variables inside programs / external variables inside function blocks
detail: Inhibited without loss of expression (PLCopen also prohibits VAR_IN_OUT).
rationale: Reference vs copy semantics differ only under pre-emption; safe to remove
quote: high integrity programs may be safely inhibited, without any loss of expression, of the use of global variables inside programs, and of external variables inside function blocks.

subset_name: Restricted IEC 61131-3 subset for high integrity applications (extending PLCopen safety specification)
detail: Latching of physical inputs and outputs per task execution must be mandated.
rationale: Programs widely rely on this unmandated behaviour; no high-integrity program should rely on assumptions
failure_class: inconsistent input values within a cycle
quote: No high integrity program should rely on assumptions.

subset_name: Restricted IEC 61131-3 subset for high integrity applications (extending PLCopen safety specification)
construct: dependence on implicit operator precedence / operand evaluation order (ST)
detail: E.g. side-effecting function in expression; tools needed to detect such use.
rationale: Unlikely to be understood properly and penalties for getting it wrong are high (citing Hatton)
quote: any dependency on implicit operator precedence or order of evaluation of operands should be absolutely forbidden in safety-related systems

subset_name: Restricted IEC 61131-3 subset for high integrity applications (extending PLCopen safety specification)
construct: FBD evaluation order dependence (feedback loops, arrays)
detail: Correct execution must not depend on block evaluation order; PLCopen bans arrays and feedback loops in basic FBD; evaluation order must be clearly defined for every FBD.
rationale: Evaluation order is implementation dependent
quote: Ideally the correct execution of a FBD program should not be dependent on the evaluation order of each block in the diagram.

subset_name: Restricted IEC 61131-3 subset for high integrity applications (extending PLCopen safety specification)
detail: All functions must always explicitly return a value.
rationale: Return value otherwise undefined by the standard
quote: all functions in high integrity programs should always explicitly return a value.

subset_name: Restricted IEC 61131-3 subset for high integrity applications (extending PLCopen safety specification)
detail: Use application-specific wrapper functions with defined behaviour for unrepresentable values; PLCopen bans conversions at basic level and limits integers to INT and DINT.
rationale: Implementation-defined result; most dangerous implementation-dependent feature
quote: Relying on a certain behaviour should be avoided in high integrity applications.

subset_name: Restricted IEC 61131-3 subset for high integrity applications (extending PLCopen safety specification)
construct: languages IL, ST, SFC for safe programs (PLCopen)
detail: PLCopen safety specification allows only LD and FBD for safe programs, and forbids arrays; paper notes no rationale given for many.
rationale: NR
quote: It also declares that only the LD and FBD languages should be used for safe programs

subset_name: Restricted IEC 61131-3 subset for high integrity applications (extending PLCopen safety specification)
detail: Safety-related data must use SAFEBOOL, SAFEINT etc., never derived from non-safe data.
rationale: Prevent contamination of safety data
quote: All data related to safety issues are expected to use this data type, whose values should never be contaminated (i.e. derived from) data from other non-safe data types.

subset_name: MISRA C (1998); plus a proposed definition/taxonomy of 'safer language subsets'
detail: Most programming standards contain a rule that goto shall not be used; some languages made it illegal. Classified as category B.1 ('folklore') since no failure evidence exists
rationale: Suspicion of failure without objective evidence (author criticises this)
quote: most programming standards contain a rule even today to the effect that the goto statement shall not be used

subset_name: MISRA C (1998); plus a proposed definition/taxonomy of 'safer language subsets'
detail: Using the value of an object with no specific initialisation; example of a category B.2 rule (known failure data: 1 per 846 lines in C; 1.46% of failures per Beizer)
rationale: Known by measurement to have led directly to system failures
quote: using the value of an object when it has had no specific initialisation is known to have led directly to systems failure

subset_name: MISRA C (1998); plus a proposed definition/taxonomy of 'safer language subsets'
construct: Reliance on default operator precedence (MISRA C Rule 47)
detail: No dependence on precedence; C has 15 levels of precedence, a known failure mode acknowledged by Ritchie
rationale: Known failure mode in programming languages for years (common mode failure)
failure_class: wrong expression evaluation due to precedence misunderstanding
enforcement: static-check (author's tool; one of the four noisiest MISRA rules)
quote: Rule 47, (no dependence on precedence)

subset_name: MISRA C (1998); plus a proposed definition/taxonomy of 'safer language subsets'
detail: Requires compliance with ISO C 9899:1990; described as a BIG, non-atomic rule effectively impossible to decide given ambiguities in base language
rationale: Strongly biased to category B.2 behaviour
quote: Rule 1 requires ISO C 9899:1990 conformance

subset_name: MISRA C (1998); plus a proposed definition/taxonomy of 'safer language subsets'
detail: Forbids register keyword; trivially decidable
rationale: Author aware of no reliability implications; apparently category B.1
quote: Rule 28 forbids the use of the register keyword in C

subset_name: MISRA C (1998); plus a proposed definition/taxonomy of 'safer language subsets'
detail: No dependency on evaluation order
rationale: A well-known problem in most programming languages, particularly C and C++
quote: Rule 46 - no dependency on evaluation order, a well-known problem in most programming languages and particularly in C and C++

subset_name: MISRA C (1998); plus a proposed definition/taxonomy of 'safer language subsets'
detail: Talks about objects needing to be declared at function scope; author notes it is miswording since only labels have function scope in C90
rationale: NR
quote: Rule 22 which talks about objects needing to be declared at function scope

subset_name: MISRA C (1998); plus a proposed definition/taxonomy of 'safer language subsets'
construct: void expressions as function parameters (MISRA C Rule 80)
detail: Prohibits passing void expressions as function parameters; redundant with Rule 1
rationale: NR (cited as redundant with Rule 1)
quote: Rule 80 which prohibits passing void expressions as function parameters

subset_name: MISRA C (1998); plus a proposed definition/taxonomy of 'safer language subsets'
detail: Rules relating to the security of function interfaces; cited for cross-talk
rationale: Security of function interfaces
quote: Rules 1, 72, 76 and 78 which all relate to the security of function interfaces

subset_name: MISRA C (1998); plus a proposed definition/taxonomy of 'safer language subsets'
construct: Bitwise operations on signed integers (MISRA C Rule 37)
detail: Prohibits bitwise operations on signed integer types; undecidable whether integral promotions count; one of four noisiest rules
rationale: NR
quote: Rule 37 which prohibits bitwise operations on signed integer types

subset_name: MISRA C (1998); plus a proposed definition/taxonomy of 'safer language subsets'
detail: Don't test floating point variables for equality/non-equality; has an exception embedded in rule 117
rationale: NR
quote: rule 50 (don'ttest floating point variables for equality / non-equality)

subset_name: MISRA C (1998); plus a proposed definition/taxonomy of 'safer language subsets'
detail: Values passed to library functions shall be checked for validity
rationale: NR
quote: values passed to library functions shall be checked for validity

subset_name: MISRA C (1998); plus a proposed definition/taxonomy of 'safer language subsets'
detail: Arguments to macros must be parenthesized; one of the four noisiest rules
rationale: NR
quote: Rule 96 (arguments to macros must be parenthesized)

subset_name: MISRA C (1998); plus a proposed definition/taxonomy of 'safer language subsets'
detail: Numeric constants should have an appropriate suffix; one of the four noisiest rules
rationale: NR
quote: rule 18 (numeric constants should have an appropriate suffix)

subset_name: Safety Critical Java (JSR-302, early draft characteristics)
detail: Many RTSJ functions eliminated or simplified; specification will include a minimum of functionality.
rationale: Certification requires minimal complexity in infrastructure and application.
quote: The single most important impact of safety critical certification is its required minimal complexity, both in the infrastructure and in the application.

subset_name: Safety Critical Java (JSR-302, early draft characteristics)
detail: Application divided into initialization phase (objects created in Mission memory) and mission phase in which objects generally not created in Mission memory but in a limited form of scoped memory.
rationale: NR
quote: A safety critical application developed under this specification will be divided into two phases – an initialization phase and a mission phase.

subset_name: Safety Critical Java (JSR-302, early draft characteristics)
detail: Certifiable implementation required to provide neither heap memory nor a garbage collector.
rationale: Application not subject to unpredictable delays associated with garbage collection.
quote: The implementation of a certifiable safety critical Java environment will be required to provide neither heap memory nor a Garbage Collector.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302), levels 0-2
detail: SCJ extends RTSJ classes and interfaces and then disallows certain more dynamic features
rationale: RTSJ features were very dynamical and thus hard to justify in critical systems where memory consumption and timing must be predictable
quote: This resulted in a definition where SCJ extends RTSJ classes and interfaces and then disallow certain more dynamic features.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302), levels 0-2
detail: Static priorities only (restriction from Puschner & Wellings adopted by SCJ)
rationale: NR (inherited from Ravenscar-Java heritage)
quote: The restrictions, e.g., static priorities, no call of sleep, no wait/notify, and no dynamic class loading, have been taken up by the SCJ expert group for the SCJ specification.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302), levels 0-2
detail: No call of sleep
rationale: NR
quote: The restrictions, e.g., static priorities, no call of sleep, no wait/notify, and no dynamic class loading, have been taken up by the SCJ expert group for the SCJ specification.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302), levels 0-2
detail: No wait/notify in the original restrictions; at level 2 wait, notify and notifyAll are provided for managed schedulable objects
rationale: NR
enforcement: NR (SCJ specification; available only at level 2)
quote: The restrictions, e.g., static priorities, no call of sleep, no wait/notify, and no dynamic class loading, have been taken up by the SCJ expert group for the SCJ specification.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302), levels 0-2
detail: No dynamic class loading
rationale: NR
quote: The restrictions, e.g., static priorities, no call of sleep, no wait/notify, and no dynamic class loading, have been taken up by the SCJ expert group for the SCJ specification.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302), levels 0-2
construct: Schedulable objects per mission / program phases
detail: Missions contain a fixed number of managed schedulable objects; all threads, handlers and shared objects set up in initialization phase before mission phase
rationale: NR
quote: An SCJ application consists of missions that contain a fixed number of cooperating sequential processes, the managed schedulable objects (MSO).

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302), levels 0-2
detail: Level 0: missions consist of periodic handlers only, statically scheduled by a cyclic executive; defined only for a single core
rationale: Ease certification for different application complexity; single core avoids lock contention issues on multicore
quote: To avoid issues with lock contention on a multicore, level 0 is defined only for a single core.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302), levels 0-2
detail: Preemptive scheduling at level 1 requires a priority ceiling protocol (priority ceiling emulation) for objects shared among handlers
rationale: Avoid priority inversion
enforcement: runtime-check (implemented in SCJ infrastructure Monitor class)
quote: this infrastructure class is used for implementing the priority ceiling emulation that SCJ requires to avoid priority inversion

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302), levels 0-2
detail: Only objects with synchronized methods may function as locks (no synchronized blocks)
rationale: NR
quote: SCJ only allows objects with synchronized methods function as locks.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302), levels 0-2
detail: SCJ level 1 defines partitioned scheduling: each thread pinned to exactly one core
rationale: Partitioned scheduling is easier to analyze with regards to real-time properties and simpler to implement
quote: Partitioned scheduling is easier to analyze with regards to properties of real-time systems and simpler to implement.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302), levels 0-2
detail: No garbage collector; restricted RTSJ scoped memory (immortal, mission, private memories) with defined lifetimes
rationale: Dynamic memory allocation in any form is considered with caution by safety-critical standards
quote: Dynamic memory allocation, in any form, is considered with some caution by standards for safetycritical applications.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302), levels 0-2
detail: References only allowed to objects in same or longer-lived scopes (deeper in the stack); violations throw IllegalAssignmentError
rationale: Avoid dangling references from programmer-managed memory areas
enforcement: runtime-check (IllegalAssignmentError; hardware check in JOP MMU) and static-check (CJ4ES WALA-based memory safety analysis)
quote: In order to avoid dangling references, the SCJ memory model dictates that reference assignments are allowed only when the reference points to an object in a memory area deeper in the stack.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302), levels 0-2
detail: Objects in an MSO's private memory cannot be shared with other MSOs or linked to structures in other memory areas; only mission and immortal memory shared
rationale: NR
quote: These objects cannot be shared with other MSOs or be linked to structures in other memory areas.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302), levels 0-2
detail: Application must declare sizes of memory areas (immortal size via Safelet, StorageParameters)
rationale: Enables bounded memory; WCMC tool assists sizing
enforcement: static-check (CJ4ES worst-case memory consumption analysis, IPET/ILP)
quote: The size of the memory areas of the different kinds must be declared by the application.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302), levels 0-2
detail: Developers must show no runtime exceptions (e.g. memory-related) will be thrown
rationale: Runtime exceptions usually unacceptable for certified safety-critical systems
quote: For safety-critical systems, especially for systems that must be certified, runtime exceptions are usually unacceptable

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ, JSR 302), levels 0-2
detail: Since SCJ v0.93 API, application programmers can no longer get a reference to a memory area
rationale: Simplifies analyses for illegal memory assignments (no need to track variables holding memory area references)
quote: it is no longer possible for application programmers to get a reference to a memory area

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance levels 0, 1 and 2
detail: SCJ restricts the RTSJ memory model to prohibit use of the heap; immortal, mission and per-release/private scoped memory areas instead.
rationale: NR
quote: SCJ restricts the RTSJ memory model to prohibit use of the heap, and defines a policy for the use of RTSJ’s immortal and scoped memory areas.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance levels 0, 1 and 2
detail: Only periodic handlers, executed sequentially in a clock-driven cyclic executive timeline; single mission sequencer.
rationale: Applications schedulable by cyclic-executive techniques.
quote: In this model, only periodic handlers are supported and within a mission these are executed sequentially in a precise, clock-driven timeline

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance levels 0, 1 and 2
detail: Prohibited at Level 1 (allowed at Level 2).
rationale: Level 1 applications must be analysable with standard fixed-priority schedulability analysis, which assumes well-defined release patterns and no self-suspension.
quote: notable restriction of the Level 1 programming model is that use of Object.wait() and Object.notify() is prohibited.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance levels 0, 1 and 2
detail: Any access to shared data must be performed by synchronized methods.
rationale: Avoid race conditions.
quote: any access to shared data has to be performed by synchronized methods to avoid race conditions.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance levels 0, 1 and 2
detail: No suspension-based delay (Services.delay) or timeouts on waits at Level 1; only at Level 2.
rationale: Same schedulability rationale (no self-suspension).
quote: Since it is not possible to have a suspension-based delay at Level 1, this requirement can only be implemented at Level 2.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance levels 0, 1 and 2
construct: Managed threads and nested mission sequencers (Levels 0/1)
detail: Managed (no-heap) threads and nested mission sequencers only available at Level 2.
rationale: Level 2 certification effort may be significantly greater.
quote: it is accepted that the effort required to certify at compliance Level 2 may be significantly greater than at Levels 0 and 1.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance levels 0, 1 and 2
detail: Global scheduling across multiple processors only at Level 2.
rationale: State of the art in multiprocessor schedulability analysis still advancing.
quote: Support for global scheduling only at Level 2 reflects the fact that the state of the art in multiprocessor schedulability analysis is still advancing

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance levels 0, 1 and 2
detail: Managed threads are simplified RTSJ no-heap threads: no automatic release mechanism (no waitForNextPeriod) and no mechanism to add a deadline; per-release memory cleared only on termination.
rationale: NR
quote: there is no automatic release mechanism (i.e., no support for waitForNextPeriod) and there is no mechanism to add a deadline.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance levels 0, 1 and 2
detail: Aperiodic handlers assumed to be released sporadically with bounded minimum inter-arrival times (not checked by the SCJ infrastructure).
rationale: Schedulability analysis assumptions.
quote: Note that SCJ aperiodic handlers are assumed to be released sporadically with bounded minimum inter-arrival times (although this is not checked by the SCJ infrastructure).

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance Level 2 (with Levels 0 and 1)
detail: SCJ restricts the RTSJ memory model to prohibit use of the heap; uses immortal, mission and per-release/private scoped memory areas
rationale: NR
quote: SCJ restricts the RTSJ memory model to prohibit use of the heap

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance Level 2 (with Levels 0 and 1)
detail: Three compliance levels with increasing feature sets; Level 0 cyclic executive with periodic handlers only on a single processor
rationale: Higher levels increase complexity and the effort required for certification
quote: The compliance levels reflect increased levels of complexity in terms of the available programming features and, therefore, of the supported programs, with direct impact on the effort required for certification.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance Level 2 (with Levels 0 and 1)
detail: Any access to shared data must be performed by synchronized methods
rationale: Avoid race conditions and ensure changes to shared variables propagate to all threads
quote: any access to shared data has to be performed by synchronized methods to avoid race conditions

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance Level 2 (with Levels 0 and 1)
detail: Prohibited at Level 1 (and 0); available only at Level 2 with other suspension features (HighResolutionTime.waitForObject, Services.delay)
rationale: Arbitrary use complicates schedulability analysis
quote: Arbitrary use of such methods complicates the ability to perform schedulability analysis.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance Level 2 (with Levels 0 and 1)
detail: Available only at Level 2
rationale: State of the art in multiprocessor schedulability analysis is still advancing
quote: The availability of global scheduling only at Level 2 reflects the fact that the state of the art in multiprocessor schedulability analysis is still advancing

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance Level 2 (with Levels 0 and 1)
detail: Mission sequencers can only be registered to a mission at Level 2; must be registered during mission initialisation
rationale: NR (Level 2 certification effort may be significantly greater)
quote: While mission sequencers are schedulable objects and are used at all compliance levels, they can only be registered to a mission at Level 2

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance Level 2 (with Levels 0 and 1)
detail: A mission's handlers and threads are created and registered during its initialisation phase
rationale: NR
quote: A mission’s handlers and threads are created and registered during its initialisation phase.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance Level 2 (with Levels 0 and 1)
detail: Managed threads are a simplified no-heap real-time thread: no automatic release (no waitForNextPeriod) and no mechanism to add a deadline
rationale: NR
quote: there is no automatic release mechanism (that is, no support for waitForNextPeriod) and there is no mechanism to add a deadline

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance Level 2 (with Levels 0 and 1)
detail: Deadlines of event handlers cannot be dynamically changed
rationale: NR
quote: In SCJ, deadlines cannot be dynamically changed

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance Level 2 (with Levels 0 and 1)
detail: Mission sequencer only has a priority, no release parameters, hence no deadline or deadline-miss handler (authors propose adding deadline-miss methods)
rationale: NR
quote: As an SCJ mission sequencer is a managed event handler, it only has a priority; it does not have any release parameters.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance Level 2 (with Levels 0 and 1)
detail: Neither SCJ nor RTSJ supports hierarchical scheduling (authors propose CPU budgets via restricted ProcessingGroupParameters and simulated multi-level priorities)
rationale: NR (possibly lack of RTOS vendor support)
quote: Neither SCJ nor the RTSJ directly support hierarchical scheduling.

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance Level 2 (with Levels 0 and 1)
detail: Level 1 does not support a queue of outstanding release events for aperiodic event handlers; suspension-based delay not possible at Level 1
rationale: NR
quote: it does not support a queue of outstanding release events for aperiodic event handlers

subset_name: Safety-Critical Java (SCJ) compliance Level 2 (with Levels 0 and 1)
detail: Authors propose removing this method; schedulables may only request termination of their controlling mission, and Mission.cleanUp() returns a boolean to continue/terminate the sequencer
rationale: Allows arbitrary schedulables to terminate arbitrary mission sequencers, breaking mission encapsulation and complicating the termination protocol; removal reduces model states by 94.5%
quote: We propose that schedulable objects are only allowed to request that their controlling mission is terminated.

subset_name: SCCP/x compilation profile (structural code-coverage preservation)
construct: code transformations in general under a profile (e.g. cc --SCCP/DC)
detail: Compiler restricted to transformations whose effect satisfies the formal preservation criteria (Theorems 3.1-3.3) for the selected coverage.
rationale: Guarantee test data from source code achieves the same structural coverage on object code; no hidden paths missed
quote: The compiler will be restricted to use only those code transformations that do not disrupt a given structural code coverage.

subset_name: SCCP/x compilation profile (structural code-coverage preservation)
detail: Does not guarantee preservation of code coverage.
rationale: Can shrink the reachability/satisfiability valuation sets of decisions or conditions
quote: Branch optimization does not guarantee code coverage as it can shrink the sets IVR (), IVT (), and IVF () of decisions or conditions.

subset_name: SCCP/x compilation profile (structural code-coverage preservation)
detail: Allowed only under SC profile; does not preserve CC, DC, MC/DC.
rationale: Splits the loop exit decision into two decisions
quote: Loop inversion splits the loop exit decision d into two separate decisions, i.e., it splits the sets IVR (d), IVT (d), and IVF (d), thus all coverages except SC are not preserved.

subset_name: SCCP/x compilation profile (structural code-coverage preservation)
construct: loop blocking, loop interchange, loop peeling, software pipelining, loop unrolling
detail: Preserve none of the coverage criteria.
rationale: May split valuation sets so original loop paths are not guaranteed covered
quote: Loop blocking, loop interchange, loop peeling, software pipelining, and loop unrolling do not preserve any of the mentioned code coverage

subset_name: SCCP/x compilation profile (structural code-coverage preservation)
construct: algebraic simplification introducing conditional control flow
detail: Preserves coverage only if implementation does not introduce new operators with conditional control flow.
rationale: New conditional operators split reachability sets
quote: Algebraic simpliﬁcation preserves the coverage criteria in case of common implementations that do not introduce new operators with conditional control ﬂow.

subset_name: SCCP/x compilation profile (structural code-coverage preservation)
detail: Not treated as a serious coverage criterion.
rationale: Without strict code guidelines a source line is undefined
quote: Line coverage: is not a serious code coverage criteria, as without strict code guidelines it is not deﬁned what a source line consists of.

subset_name: GNAT Pro Cert Run-Time Profile (Ada 95/2005)
construct: Ada language features and libraries outside the Cert profile
detail: Cert supports Zero Footprint Profile features plus thread-safe restrictions; unsupported features/libraries produce compiler errors. Specific features not enumerated.
rationale: Pre-defined certified coding standard supporting DO-178B certification
quote: A run-time profile (RTP) is a compiler-enforced Ada language [3] subset with a corresponding (minimal or none) run-time library [4].

subset_name: GNAT Pro Cert Run-Time Profile (Ada 95/2005)
construct: exception handling, dynamic memory allocation, thread management, object deallocation
detail: Key areas addressed by the Cert profile; exact restrictions not given.
rationale: Safety/security; traceability from source code to object code; optimization issues
quote: Some of the key areas that this profile addresses are exception handling, dynamic memory allocation, thread management, object deallocation, traceability from source code to object code, and optimization issues

subset_name: GNAT Pro Cert Run-Time Profile (Ada 95/2005)
detail: Replaced by Cert-compliant ARINC 653 APEX interface.
rationale: Not supported by Cert
quote: The VxWorks [7] semaphore interfaces used in the code base was not supported by Cert.

subset_name: GNAT Pro Cert Run-Time Profile (Ada 95/2005)
detail: Build mode changed to Non-Debug; all debug-related information removed.
rationale: NR
quote: Other key changes included removing all debug related information

subset_name: GNAT Pro Cert Run-Time Profile (Ada 95/2005)
construct: standard library packages not in Cert (e.g. random number generators)
detail: User-defined Ada packages developed and verified against Cert restrictions.
rationale: Not in approved library set
quote: developing userdefined Ada packages that are not supported in the Cert RTP (e.g. random number generators)

subset_name: GNAT Pro Cert Run-Time Profile (Ada 95/2005)
detail: Mechanisms implemented to prevent deadlocks; Cert adds thread-safe restrictions.
rationale: Prevent deadlock
quote: implementing mechanisms to prevent dead-locks.

subset_name: SPARK (and RavenSPARK)
detail: Pointers and heap storage disallowed in SPARK
rationale: Eliminates CWEs 122 heap overflow, 244 heap inspection, 401 memory leak, 415 double free, 416 use after free, 468 pointer scaling, 476 null dereference
failure_class: heap overflow; memory leak; double free; use after free; null pointer dereference; incorrect pointer scaling
quote: In SPARK, pointer types and heap storage are disallowed. Immediately, CWEs 122, 244, 401, 415, 416, 468, and 476 are eliminated.

subset_name: SPARK (and RavenSPARK)
detail: Recursion forbidden
rationale: Storage requirements determinable statically; prevents stack-based buffer overflow (CWE 121)
quote: The storage requirements of a SPARK program can be determined statically. This is achieved by forbidding recursion and dynamic arrays.

subset_name: SPARK (and RavenSPARK)
detail: Dynamic arrays forbidden; object bounds known via subtype at declaration
rationale: Storage requirements determinable statically
quote: The storage requirements of a SPARK program can be determined statically. This is achieved by forbidding recursion and dynamic arrays.

subset_name: SPARK (and RavenSPARK)
detail: Out-of-range indices flagged by Examiner; dynamic indices require proof via Simplifier VCs
rationale: Proof of absence of buffer overflow
failure_class: buffer overflow / index out of range
enforcement: static-check (SPARK Examiner VCs discharged by Simplifier/Proof Checker)
quote: In this instance, full analysis and proof for absence of buffer overflows requires the Simplifier to be run on the VCs.

subset_name: SPARK (and RavenSPARK)
detail: Only assignment and concatenation on strings; fixed-length strings with statically known size; no null termination
rationale: Sizes of string objects always known statically; precludes CWE 251 and 170
failure_class: string buffer overflow; improper null termination
quote: CWE 251 cannot occur because the only operations on string objects are assignment and concatenation. This is to ensure that the sizes of the string objects are always known statically.

subset_name: SPARK (and RavenSPARK)
detail: No printf-style subprogram in SPARK
rationale: Precludes uncontrolled format string (CWE 134)
quote: In SPARK there is no ‘format string’ as there is no printf-style subprogram.

subset_name: SPARK (and RavenSPARK)
detail: SPARK subset eliminates all predefined exceptions; no exceptions raised
rationale: Precludes unchecked/ignored exception conditions (CWE 391)
quote: The SPARK subset of Ada eliminates all predefined exceptions.

subset_name: SPARK (and RavenSPARK)
detail: Examiner flags error conditions ignored in program flow; values must be used meaningfully
rationale: Precludes programmatic unchecked error condition (CWE 391)
quote: The Examiner insists that the code be used in a meaningful fashion and will flag an error if it is not.

subset_name: SPARK (and RavenSPARK)
detail: All variables must be initialized; arbitrary (unused) initialization also flagged
rationale: Prevents use of uninitialized variable (CWE 457) and heap/memory inspection leaks
quote: CWE 457 is detected by the Examiner in SPARK. All variables must be initialized.

subset_name: SPARK (and RavenSPARK)
detail: Variable number of arguments and parameter defaults not permitted
rationale: Prevents hidden debug back-door via optional parameter (CWE 489 example)
quote: SPARK does not permit variable number of arguments.

subset_name: SPARK (and RavenSPARK)
detail: Shared data must be in protected objects; Ravenscar tasking profile with additional constraints
rationale: Prevents race conditions (CWE 367) and externally accessible locks (CWE 412) for shared data
failure_class: data race; TOCTOU race; externally controlled lock
quote: In RavenSPARK, an unprotected but shared variable is absolutely not permitted, so a programmer cannot forget to properly control access to a shared variable.

subset_name: SPARK (and RavenSPARK)
detail: Foreign subprograms encapsulated in a package with preconditions validating data passed
rationale: Foreign code not subject to SPARK rigor; injection weaknesses (CWE 78, 80, 89, 99) can be reduced but not eliminated
quote: The general approach is to encapsulate the use of the foreign subprogram (FSP) in a package.

subset_name: SPARK 2014
detail: No pointers in SPARK (references and formalized containers instead).
rationale: Language definition forbids the construct so pointer-related CWE issues (untrusted, NULL, expired pointer dereference) cannot happen.
quote: There are a number of CWE issues that cannot happen in S PARK programs as the language deﬁnition forbids these constructs in the ﬁrst place.

subset_name: SPARK 2014
detail: All variables must be initialized before first use, checked by flow analysis (no need to mandate initialization-at-declaration).
rationale: Eliminates CWE-456 Missing Initialization; initialization-at-declaration rules are less helpful.
quote: all variables must be initialized at some point before their ﬁrst use in S PARK

subset_name: SPARK 2014
detail: Verification conditions for every point where a run-time exception might be raised must be discharged (proof of absence of run-time exceptions).
rationale: Guarantees run-time exceptions never occur regardless of input; eliminates overflow, buffer overflow, bad array index, bad numeric conversion CWEs; can justify turning off run-time checks.
failure_class: unhandled exception (overflow, buffer overflow, index out of range)
enforcement: static-check (SPARK proof tools via WhyML and SMT solvers Alt-Ergo, CVC4)
quote: Discharging all VCs guarantees absence of all run-time exceptions (no arithmetic over- or underﬂow, buffer overﬂows, etc.)

subset_name: SPARK 2014
detail: Global and Depends data/information-flow contracts verified so data does not leak directly or indirectly into another variable.
rationale: Mitigates CWE-807 reliance on untrusted inputs; security.
quote: a depends contract that can be used to verify that one set of data does not leak directly or indirectly into another.

subset_name: SPARK 2014
construct: Object orientation (tagged types, dynamic dispatch) and tasking
detail: Not yet in the SPARK 2014 subset; planned: a useful subset of tagged types, interfaces and dynamic dispatch following LSP, and Ravenscar for tasking.
rationale: To extend verification to a wider class of programs (future work).
quote: Larger language subset - in particular OO and tasking.

subset_name: Ravenscar Profile, and a proposed augmented Ravenscar profile with Ada 2005 timing constructs
construct: tasking constructs with unbounded execution time or non-determinism
detail: Ravenscar specifies a reduced tasking model; compilation system rejects forbidden semantics.
rationale: Static analysability in the time dimension (e.g. Response Time Analysis); small footprint and qualifiable kernels
quote: it specifies a reduced tasking model for the Ada language [9] which excludes the language constructs that are exposed to unbounded execution time or nondeterminism.

subset_name: Ravenscar Profile, and a proposed augmented Ravenscar profile with Ada 2005 timing constructs
detail: RP forbids them (No_Dependence); paper proposes allowing them if declared only at library level and at most one per task.
rationale: Proposed restriction avoids overly complex implementation
quote: they could be safely and efficiently used, provided that they are only declared at library level and there is at most one execution-time timer per task [17], so as to avoid an overly complex implementation of them.

subset_name: Ravenscar Profile, and a proposed augmented Ravenscar profile with Ada 2005 timing constructs
detail: RP forbids them; paper proposes allowing them if declared at library level.
rationale: Could be safely and efficiently used at library level for partition-level monitoring
quote: The RP does not include group budgets.

subset_name: Ravenscar Profile, and a proposed augmented Ravenscar profile with Ada 2005 timing constructs
detail: Allowed only if declared at library level (No_Local_Timing_Events).
rationale: NR
quote: allows the use of timing events only if declared at library level.

subset_name: Ravenscar Profile, and a proposed augmented Ravenscar profile with Ada 2005 timing constructs
construct: dispatching policies other than FIFO within priorities; Priority_Specific_Dispatching
detail: RP disallows; static analysability of priority-specific dispatching not yet studied.
rationale: Static analysability not established
quote: The RP allows neither dispatching policies other than FIFO within priorities nor priority specific dispatching.

subset_name: Ravenscar Profile, and a proposed augmented Ravenscar profile with Ada 2005 timing constructs
detail: Overrunning tasks cannot be killed under RP.
rationale: Greatly reduces implementation complexity
quote: Task termination is disallowed in the RP and with good reason, since this greatly reduces the complexity of the implementation

subset_name: Ravenscar Profile, and a proposed augmented Ravenscar profile with Ada 2005 timing constructs
construct: dynamic priorities and asynchronous task control
detail: Cannot hold tasks (Ada.Asynchronous_Task_Control) or lower priorities (Ada.Dynamic_Priorities) under RP; authors also prefer not adding full dynamic priorities.
rationale: Would increase kernel complexity, footprint, overhead and timing-analysis complexity
quote: The full availability of dynamic priorities to applications, although potentially useful, for example, in mode changes, might also greatly increase system complexity from the timing analysis point of view.

subset_name: Ravenscar Profile, and a proposed augmented Ravenscar profile with Ada 2005 timing constructs
detail: Guard of an entry must be a simple Boolean variable.
rationale: NR
quote: The RP prescribes that a guard of an entry is composed exclusively by a simple Boolean variable.

subset_name: Ravenscar Profile, and a proposed augmented Ravenscar profile with Ada 2005 timing constructs
detail: Use task archetypes and delay until to enforce period/MIAT.
rationale: Preserve timing properties assumed by schedulability analysis
quote: The adoption of appropriate task archetypes [2] and the use of the delay until construct make it possible to accurately enforce the period or the MIAT under the RP.

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
construct: Non-definite behaviour (undefined, critical unspecified, implementation-defined behaviour, compiler extensions)
detail: Rule 1.3: no undefined or critical unspecified behaviour; implementation-defined behaviour and extensions constrained.
rationale: C's non-definite behaviour conflicts with safety and security requirements; subset removes or reduces opportunity to make mistakes.
enforcement: static-check (MISRA C compliance checkers, semantic static analysis) with documented deviation process
quote: The guidelines ban critical non-deﬁnite behavior and constrain the use of implementation-deﬁned behavior and compiler extensions.

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
construct: Easily misused or misunderstood language features
detail: General MISRA C design aim.
rationale: Improve reliability, readability, portability and maintainability.
enforcement: static-check (MISRA C compliance checkers, semantic static analysis) with documented deviation process
quote: They also limit the use of language features that can easily be misused or misunderstood.

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
detail: Avoid run-time failures; undecidable, requires semantic analysis.
rationale: NR
enforcement: static-check (semantic analysis; directive needs extra information)
quote: Avoid run-time failures

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
detail: No direct or indirect recursion; decidable approximation finds call-graph cycles and flags all calls via function pointers.
rationale: NR (paper explains checking approach only).
quote: Rule 17.2, which disallows recursion, admits a decidable approximation that requires ﬁnding cycles in the call graph

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
detail: Using a smaller subset without function pointer calls removes false positives for Rule 17.2.
rationale: Rigid programming schemes make undecidable rules checkable without false positives.
quote: If function calls via pointers are not used (i.e., the program is written in a smaller subset of C than that strictly mandated by the rule) then there will be no false positives.

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
detail: Advised against except where needed and safe, with deviation.
rationale: Implementation-defined with undefined behaviours from truncation and invalid/misaligned pointers.
quote: such conversions are implementation-deﬁned and have undeﬁned behaviors (due to possible truncation and the formation of invalid and/or misaligned pointers)

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
detail: Value of automatic object must not be read before set; authors recommend a decidable Definite-Assignment-like approximation over deep semantic analysis for reviewability.
rationale: Undefined behaviour; checks must remain explainable to reviewers.
quote: whereby the value of an automatic object must not be read before it has been set, since otherwise we have undeﬁned behavior.

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
detail: Right-hand operand of a shift must be in range.
rationale: Shifting by negative or too-large amounts is undefined behaviour (e.g., IA-32 masks shift count).
quote: Right-hand operand of a shift operator must be in range

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
detail: No side effects in initializers; do not depend on unspecified evaluation order; no side effects in right operand of && or ||.
rationale: Order of sub-expression evaluation is unspecified behaviour.
quote: Do not depend on unspeciﬁed evaluation order of expressions

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
detail: No floating-point loop counters.
rationale: NR
quote: No ﬂoating-point loop counters

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
detail: Restricted form of for loops.
rationale: NR
quote: Restricted form of for loops

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
detail: No invariant controlling expressions.
rationale: NR
quote: No invariant controlling expressions

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
detail: No unreachable code; no dead code.
rationale: NR
quote: No unreachable code

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
detail: Pointer arithmetic must not exceed array limits; no subtraction/comparison of pointers to different arrays/objects.
rationale: NR
quote: Pointer arithmetic must not exceed array limits

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
detail: Pointer object must not outlive its pointees.
rationale: NR
quote: Pointer object must not live longer than corresponding pointees

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
detail: Objects must not be assigned or copied to overlapping objects.
rationale: NR
quote: Objects must not be assigned or copied to overlapping objects

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
detail: Do not modify function parameters.
rationale: NR
quote: Do not modify function parameters

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
detail: All dynamically obtained resources must be explicitly released; do not free memory not dynamically allocated.
rationale: NR
quote: All dynamically-obtained resources must be explicitly released

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
detail: Use of <string.h> functions must not result in buffer overflow; size_t arguments in range.
rationale: NR
quote: Use of functions from <string.h> must not result in buﬀer overﬂow

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
detail: Do not trust values received from external sources.
rationale: Security (Amendment 1).
quote: Do not trust values received from external sources

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
detail: Check validity of values passed to library functions; <ctype.h> functions must not receive out-of-spec values.
rationale: NR
quote: Check the validity of values passed to library functions

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
construct: Unions, unrestricted pointer casts, backward gotos
detail: Deprecated or severely regulated by MISRA C.
rationale: Such features pose significant problems to static analysis designers; banning them improves efficiency and precision of static analysis.
enforcement: static-check (MISRA C compliance checkers, semantic static analysis) with documented deviation process
quote: It is not a coincidence that such features (e.g., unions, unrestricted pointer casts, backward gotos) pose signiﬁcant problems to the designers of static analyses tools.

subset_name: MISRA C:2012 (with Technical Corrigendum 1 and Amendment 1)
detail: Mandatory guidelines: no deviation; required: formal deviation; advisory: documented non-compliance; disapplication needs rationale in a recategorization plan.
rationale: A guideline means 'this is dangerous: only do it if needed, safe, and a peer can be convinced of both'.
quote: “This is dangerous: you may only do that if (1) it is needed, (2) it is safe, and (3) a peer can easily and quickly be convinced of both (1) and (2).”

subset_name: J Consortium Real-Time Core High Integrity Profile (Ravenscar-like)
construct: dynamic class loading and VM plug-in mode
detail: Only Static Core Java Execution Environment; statically-linked native code in protected memory; no object exchange with the VM; dynamic update only at partition level.
rationale: Spatial firewall protecting critical code from less-trusted code
quote: Consequently there is no exchange of objects between the VM and the high integrity program, nor are any of the VM features used, such as dynamic loading.

subset_name: J Consortium Real-Time Core High Integrity Profile (Ravenscar-like)
construct: automatic garbage collection and general heap
detail: Objects allocated by lifetime: stack allocation, per-thread fixed-size allocation contexts, or immortal allocation at initialization.
rationale: Deterministic memory management; memory must never be exhausted; no fragmentation
quote: Thus the high integrity partition makes no use of a general heap, with all its associated non-deterministic compaction and garbage collection requirements.

subset_name: J Consortium Real-Time Core High Integrity Profile (Ravenscar-like)
detail: All threads created at program startup; no thread classes declared as inner classes within methods.
rationale: No need for implicit join to prevent access to exited method's locals
quote: All threads are created at program startup, for example as part of the initialization code for the classes.

subset_name: J Consortium Real-Time Core High Integrity Profile (Ravenscar-like)
detail: Priority Ceiling Protocol is the only supported locking mechanism.
rationale: Static computation of worst-case blocking time; PCP gives optimal bounds
quote: PCP is mandated by the high integrity profile as the only supported locking mechanism for protected objects.

subset_name: J Consortium Real-Time Core High Integrity Profile (Ravenscar-like)
detail: Excluded.
rationale: Co-existence of priority inheritance and PCP adds complexity to timing analysis and runtime
quote: Since the co-existence of priority inheritance and PCP adds significant complexity both to timing analysis and to the runtime implementation, these constructs are excluded from the high integrity profile.

subset_name: J Consortium Real-Time Core High Integrity Profile (Ravenscar-like)
detail: Excluded.
rationale: Potential source of unbounded priority inversion undermining schedulability analysis
quote: Since these constructs undermine schedulability analysis as a potential sourca o f unbounded priority inversion, they are excluded from the high-integrity profile.

subset_name: J Consortium Real-Time Core High Integrity Profile (Ravenscar-like)
construct: asynchronous thread operations: Stop (abort), SetPriority, asynchronous Suspend/Resume, event-based ATC
detail: Excluded; removes need for abort-deferred regions and priority/suspension deferral.
rationale: Ensure predictability of execution; simplify implementation
quote: Core Java tasking constructs that define asynchronous thread-to-thread operations are also excluded from the high integrity profile in order to ensure predictability o f execution.

subset_name: J Consortium Real-Time Core High Integrity Profile (Ravenscar-like)
detail: All threads global; no requeue; FIFO_Within_Priorities scheduling.
rationale: Compatibility with Ravenscar
quote: There is no requeue, abort, dynamic priority change, asynchronous suspension or ATC.

subset_name: J Consortium Real-Time Core High Integrity Profile (Ravenscar-like)
detail: Throw/catch supported for fault detection, but all exceptions pre-allocated and carry no state information.
rationale: Error recovery without dynamic allocation
quote: Java exception throwing and catching is supported, though all exceptions are pre-allocated, and so exception

subset_name: J Consortium Real-Time Core High Integrity Profile (Ravenscar-like)
detail: Eliminated to reduce footprint, increase speed and simplify runtime verification.
rationale: Formal certification of runtime system
quote: Elimination of complex constructs to reduce the footprint, increase execution speed, and simplify the verification of the runtime system required for formal certification.

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
detail: Only at library level; no task hierarchy.
rationale: No exit protocols needed from blocks and subprograms.
quote: that is, no hierarchy of tasks, and hence no exit protocols needed from blocks and subprograms.

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
construct: Unchecked deallocation of protected and task objects
detail: Not allowed.
rationale: Removes the need for dynamic objects.
quote: removes the need for dynamic objects.

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
construct: Dynamic allocation of task or protected objects
detail: Not allowed.
rationale: Removes the need for dynamic objects.
quote: NR

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
detail: Tasks assumed non-terminating; violation of No_Task_Termination is a bounded error causing permanent suspension (user handler hook).
rationale: Task termination generally an error for a long-running real-time program that defines all tasks at startup.
quote: this is primarily because task termination is generally considered to be an error for a real-time program which is long-running and defines all of its tasks at startup.

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
detail: Library-level only.
rationale: Provide atomic updates to shared data and can be implemented simply.
quote: these provide atomic updates to shared data and can be implemented simply.

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
detail: Library level, at most a single entry.
rationale: Used for invocation signalling while removing overheads of a complicated exit protocol.
quote: used for invocation signaling; but removes the overheads of a complicated exit protocol.

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
detail: Barrier must consist of a single boolean variable.
rationale: No side effects possible and exit protocol becomes simple.
quote: no side effects are possible and exit protocol becomes simple.

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
detail: Only a single task may queue on an entry (Max_Entry_Queue_Depth=1); in Raven a runtime check raising Program_Error.
rationale: No queue required; static property easily verified, or bounded error at runtime.
quote: this is a static property that can easily be verified, or it can lead to a bounded error at runtime

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
detail: No requeue.
rationale: Complicated protocols, significant overheads, difficult to analyse functionally and temporally.
quote: leads to complicated protocols, significant overheads and is difficult to analyse (both functionally and temporally).

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
construct: abort and asynchronous transfer of control (ATC)
detail: No abort or ATC.
rationale: Greatest run-time overhead due to protecting data structures against asynchronous task actions.
quote: these features leads to the greatest overhead in the runtime system due to the need to protect data structures against asynchronous task actions.

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
detail: No use of select.
rationale: Non-deterministic behaviour is difficult to analyse; protected objects diminish its importance.
quote: non-deterministic behaviour is difficult to analyse, moreover the existence of protected objects has diminished the importance of the select statement to the tasking model.

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
detail: No task entries, hence no accept statement.
rationale: Not necessary to program systems that can be analysed.
quote: not necessary to program systems that can be analysed; it follows that there is no need for the accept statement.

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
detail: 'delay until' allowed, but no relative 'delay'.
rationale: Absolute delay is the correct form for constructing periodic tasks.
quote: the absolute form of delay is the correct one to use for constructing periodic tasks.

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
detail: No Calendar package; Real_Time package used for the real-time clock.
rationale: Real-Time package is sufficient.
quote: 'Real-Time' package is sufficient.

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
detail: Used for shared data.
rationale: Needed to enforce correct use of shared data.
quote: needed to enforce the correct use of shared data.

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
detail: Allowed but not within entry barriers.
rationale: Useful for some algorithms with low overhead.
quote: NR

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
detail: Available in reduced form (no Abort_Task or task attribute functions Callable or Terminated).
rationale: Useful with low overhead.
quote: NR

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
detail: Not allowed.
rationale: Introduces a dynamic feature into the runtime with complexity and overhead.
quote: introduces a dynamic feature into the runtime that has complexity and overhead.

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
detail: No use of dynamic priorities.
rationale: Priority assigned at task creation remains unchanged except while executing a protected operation.
quote: ensures that the priority assigned at task creation is unchanged during the task's execution, except when the task is executing a protected operation.

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
detail: Interrupt handlers must be protected procedures.
rationale: Required if interrupts are to be handled.
quote: required if interrupts are to be handled.

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
detail: FIFO within priorities with Ceiling Locking for protected objects; a non-preemptive policy is also allowed.
rationale: Fixed-priority analysis; non-preemption reduces testing cost and run-time size.
quote: The profile defines dispatching to be F I F O within p r i o r i t y with protected objects having Ceiling Locking.

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
detail: Each task an infinite loop with a single invocation event (delay until or protected entry call).
rationale: Enables system-wide worst-case timing analysis.
quote: With the profile, each task should be structured as an infinite loop within which is a single invocation event.

subset_name: Ravenscar tasking profile
construct: Dynamically acquired memory (sequential code, Raven implementation)
detail: No dynamically-acquired memory in runtime or application sequential code; stack/TCB areas declared in Board Support Package.
rationale: Eliminates need for a heap and its non-determinism during allocation.
quote: which is also a restriction on the sequential code of the application, thereby eliminating the need to support a heap with its associated non-determinism during allocation.

subset_name: Ravenscar Profile as implemented in Aonix Raven (plus sequential restrictions)
detail: Enforced via configuration pragma Restrictions; new identifiers introduced to define the Profile exactly: Boolean_Entry_Barriers, Max_Entry_Queue_Depth => 1, No_Calendar, No_Relative_Delay, No_Protected_Type_Allocators, No_Local_Protected_Objects, No_Requeue, No_Select_Statements, No_Task_Attributes, No_Task_Termination.
rationale: Simple tasking subset for efficient high-integrity applications whose timing must be analysed
quote: Thus a number o f new identifiers were inlxoduced to define the Profile subset exactly.

subset_name: Ravenscar Profile as implemented in Aonix Raven (plus sequential restrictions)
detail: No_Task_Termination violation defined as a run-time Bounded Error, behaviour documented by implementer.
rationale: NR
quote: All the restrictions except for two are enforced at compiletime.

subset_name: Ravenscar Profile as implemented in Aonix Raven (plus sequential restrictions)
detail: Violation raises Program_Error at run time; build-time enforcement judged too restrictive on code.
rationale: At most one waiting task per protected object; consistency with suspension objects
quote: W e define violation o f Max__Entry_Queue__Depth => 1 to ra~e P r o g r a m _ E r r o r exception.

subset_name: Ravenscar Profile as implemented in Aonix Raven (plus sequential restrictions)
construct: sequential features needing non-deterministic runtime support or unsuitable for bare targets
detail: Sequential restrictions: No_Exception_Handlers, No_Standard_Storage_Pools, No_IO, No_Nested_Finalization (default storage pool and Ada exception handling excluded), reused from DO-178B Level A qualified C-SMART runtime.
rationale: Retain functional and temporal determinism; Ravenscar defines only a tasking subset
quote: It was therefore necessary to add a suitable subset for the sequential (non-tasking) part o f execution to retain determinism both at the functional and the temporal level.

subset_name: Ravenscar Profile as implemented in Aonix Raven (plus sequential restrictions)
detail: Not restricted by default because handled purely by code generator; users may add No_Dispatch to enable functional and temporal analysis.
rationale: Keep subset as large as possible; restrict only runtime-support features
quote: This approach k e e p s the subset as large as possible so as not to impose restrictions needlessly on users that do not require full static analysis

subset_name: Ravenscar Profile as implemented in Aonix Raven (plus sequential restrictions)
detail: Optional restrictions Static_Storage_Size and Static_Priorities offered (not mandatory).
rationale: Memory-size determinism and use of schedulability analyzers
quote: that we thought might prove useful for memory-size determinigm and use o f schedulability analyzers:

subset_name: Ravenscar Profile as implemented in Aonix Raven (plus sequential restrictions)
detail: Treated as a soft restriction users may remove; as specified it also excludes Boolean literals, which authors find over-restrictive.
rationale: Portability with Profile subset
quote: This seems over-restrictive,

subset_name: Ravenscar Profile as implemented in Aonix Raven (plus sequential restrictions)
construct: tasks readied by an interrupt handler
detail: At most one task may be made ready by an interrupt handler.
rationale: Avoid linked list of tasks; consistent with at most one waiting task per protected object
quote: In order to avoid use o f a linked list o f tasks, we restricted the maximum number o f tasks that could be made ready via the action o f an interrupt handler to one.

subset_name: Ravenscar Profile as implemented in Aonix Raven (plus sequential restrictions)
construct: library-level elaboration order relative to task activation
detail: All library unit elaboration code executes before any task is activated.
rationale: Ensure determinism and eliminate access before elaboration of global data
quote: In order to ensure determinism and to eliminate all possibility o f access before elaboration o f global data b y any task, all library unit elaboration code was executed prior to the activation o f any task.

subset_name: Ravenscar Profile as implemented in Aonix Raven (plus sequential restrictions)
detail: No recursion, minimal linked lists and indirection in the runtime kernel.
rationale: Simplify analysis for formal qualification
quote: Certain rules were enforced to simplify the analysis needed for formal qualification, including no use o f recursion,

subset_name: TTF-Ravenscar (Tolerance to Timing Faults Ravenscar) profile
detail: No dispatching domains can be created by the program
rationale: In keeping with Ravenscar's static nature
quote: No dispatching domains can be created by the program.

subset_name: TTF-Ravenscar (Tolerance to Timing Faults Ravenscar) profile
detail: Each task, including the environment task, set to run on a single CPU via Set_CPU; explicit migration allowed (possibly restricted)
rationale: In keeping with Ravenscar; migration needed for error recovery/load balancing
quote: Each task, including the environment task, should be set to run on a single CPU (using the Set CPU subprogram).

subset_name: TTF-Ravenscar (Tolerance to Timing Faults Ravenscar) profile
detail: Each interrupt handler should run on a single processor
rationale: In keeping with Ravenscar
quote: Each interrupt handler should only run on a single processor – but this may not be under the control of the program.

subset_name: TTF-Ravenscar (Tolerance to Timing Faults Ravenscar) profile
detail: Allowed (added to Ravenscar) but only one handler per task
rationale: Needed to detect WCET budget overrun without inefficient polling
quote: Only one handler per task is needed.

subset_name: TTF-Ravenscar (Tolerance to Timing Faults Ravenscar) profile
detail: Allowed only for tasks residing on the same processor
rationale: Group budgets challenging to implement on multicore; needed for damage confinement (servers, temporal isolation)
quote: we suggest that group budgets can only be set for tasks that reside on the same processor.

subset_name: TTF-Ravenscar (Tolerance to Timing Faults Ravenscar) profile
detail: Possibly allowed; ceilings must be ceiling of all priority settings or dynamic ceilings included
rationale: Undermines static nature of Ravenscar but valuable for error confinement and recovery

subset_name: TTF-Ravenscar (Tolerance to Timing Faults Ravenscar) profile
detail: Alternative to dynamic priorities; concerns over vendor support (no one implements it)
rationale: Hard to get semantics without OS support; obviated by dynamic priorities
quote: As far as we are aware, no one implements this package.

subset_name: TTF-Ravenscar (Tolerance to Timing Faults Ravenscar) profile

rationale: Ravenscar restriction leads to obfuscated code for mode changes
quote: At a minimum, having a single entry but multiple tasks queued (or multiple entries but with only one task allowed to queue) is required.

quote: We feel that support for this is a step too far for a restricted high-integrity proﬁle. Full fault tolerance requires the full language.

detail: Retained from Ravenscar: all tasks created during initialisation
rationale: Static task set (Ravenscar)
quote: Ravenscar does not support the dynamic creation of tasks, so all tasks must be created during the initialization phase.

detail: Size of a scoped memory area cannot be changed once set.

detail: No nested scoped memory areas; scoped memory areas not shared between Schedulable objects.
rationale: Greatly eases memory usage analysis algorithm.
quote: These restrictions greatly ease the development of an algorithm that will inspect each thread’s logic to discover all classes it instantiates.
