subset_name: XRTJ environment based on the Ravenscar-Java profile (plus distributed run-time restrictions)
detail: RMI only allowed in initialisation phase; no remote invocation in mission phase; profile main classes have no remote interfaces and are not serialisable.
rationale: High predictability and reliability while providing some distributed support.
quote: In the mission phase of the RVM or after executing the real-time threads in a standard RTJVM, no remote method invocation is allowed.

subset_name: XRTJ environment based on the Ravenscar-Java profile (plus distributed run-time restrictions)
detail: Objects statically allocated to cluster nodes at design phase; allocation, registration and reference collection of remote objects used in mission phase done during initialisation.
rationale: High-integrity environments; enable schedulability analysis of remote objects as sporadic threads.
quote: For high-integrity environments, objects should be statically allocated to each node in the cluster.

subset_name: XRTJ environment based on the Ravenscar-Java profile (plus distributed run-time restrictions)
detail: Not allowed (assumption for WCET and schedulability analysis).
rationale: Enables WCET estimation and schedulability analysis in distributed setting.
quote: we assume that one compatible virtual machine resides on each node in the cluster network and no recursive remote method invocations are allowed.

subset_name: XRTJ environment based on the Ravenscar-Java profile (plus distributed run-time restrictions)
construct: Remote calls across phases (Mission Distributed Environment)
detail: A VM in mission phase must not invoke a remote method on a VM not in mission phase; pre-mission phase synchronises VMs.
rationale: Could result in unpredictable and unanalysable real-time threads.
quote: a virtual machine executing in its mission phase must not attempt to invoke a remote method on another virtual machine that is not running under the mission phase.

subset_name: XRTJ environment based on the Ravenscar-Java profile (plus distributed run-time restrictions)
detail: Assumption of data-race analysis: reads and writes on a shared object in a method enclosed in the same synchronized block or method.
rationale: Avoid data races (lost reads/writes) under the weak Java memory model.
quote: any reads and writes on a shared object in a method must be enclosed within the same synchronized block (or method) in order not to have any data races.

subset_name: Safety-oriented restricted SYCL (post-processing restrictions on SYCLomatic output, toward SYCL SC)
detail: All array dimensions fixed at compile time; statically sized structures; no runtime dynamic allocation in generated code.
rationale: emxArray introduces implicit memory management, auxiliary allocation functions and non-deterministic execution paths, complicating memory analysis and transformation.
quote: dynamically sized arrays based on emxArray structures are eliminated, as they introduce implicit memory management, auxiliary allocation functions, and non-deterministic execution paths

subset_name: Safety-oriented restricted SYCL (post-processing restrictions on SYCLomatic output, toward SYCL SC)
detail: MATLAB Function blocks use coder.inline('always') so code is emitted as a single consolidated function.
rationale: Decomposition introduces duplicated local variables, redundant/duplicated allocations that complicate static analysis and memory transformations.
quote: Function decomposition in automatically generated code often introduces duplicated local variables and redundant memory allocations.

subset_name: Safety-oriented restricted SYCL (post-processing restrictions on SYCLomatic output, toward SYCL SC)
construct: Generated error-handling functions (exceptions, callbacks, implicit control flow)
detail: Automatically generated (dpct) error-handling functions and calls removed.
rationale: ISO 26262-6:2018 Table 1 Rec. 1b: exclude constructs that may result in unhandled run-time errors; implicit control paths hinder static analysis and WCET estimation.
enforcement: static-check (Clang-based static analysis and automated rewriting)
quote: This transformation is motivated by the recommendation on the exclusion of language constructs that may result in unhandled run-time errors, as stated in ISO 26262-6:2018, Table 1, Recommendation 1b.

subset_name: Safety-oriented restricted SYCL (post-processing restrictions on SYCLomatic output, toward SYCL SC)
construct: Dynamic memory allocation / raw USM pointers
detail: Replaced by explicit template design USMBuffer<T> coupling pointer with allocation size (strong typing).
rationale: Dynamic allocation introduces nondeterminism from runtime memory management and fragmentation; raw pointers lose bounds information (ISO 26262-6 Rec. 1e, 1h).
enforcement: static-check (Clang-based static analysis and automated rewriting)
quote: Dynamic allocation introduces nondeterministic behaviour due to runtime memory management and potential fragmentation.

subset_name: Safety-oriented restricted SYCL (post-processing restrictions on SYCLomatic output, toward SYCL SC)
detail: Explicit synchronisation barriers (and cudaDeviceSynchronize after each kernel launch) enforced.
rationale: Implicit synchronisation and undefined execution order can cause race conditions and non-reproducible behaviour; controlled concurrency per ISO 26262-6.
enforcement: static-check (Clang-based static analysis and automated rewriting)
quote: Implicit synchronisation and undefined execution order between work-items can lead to race conditions and non-reproducible behaviour.

subset_name: Safety-oriented restricted SYCL (post-processing restrictions on SYCLomatic output, toward SYCL SC)
detail: All dependencies on dpct removed.
rationale: Opaque tool-generated abstractions outside the SYCL standard obscure control flow and memory semantics, limiting traceability and certification (consistent with ISO 26262-6 Rec. 1b).
enforcement: static-check (Clang-based static analysis and automated rewriting)
quote: Such abstractions obscure control flow and memory semantics, thereby limiting traceability and the feasibility of certification.

subset_name: Safety-oriented restricted SYCL (post-processing restrictions on SYCLomatic output, toward SYCL SC)
detail: Only native SYCL queues used.
rationale: Compatibility queues may introduce hidden synchronisation or deferred execution; native queues give explicit control needed for predictable scheduling and timing analysis.
enforcement: static-check (Clang-based static analysis and automated rewriting)
quote: Queue abstractions provided through compatibility layers may introduce implicit behaviours such as hidden synchronisation or deferred execution.

subset_name: Safety-oriented restricted SYCL (post-processing restrictions on SYCLomatic output, toward SYCL SC)
detail: Replaced by Unified Shared Memory where possible (local memory still requires buffer-accessor in AdaptiveCpp).
rationale: Buffer-accessor enforces implicit memory management and data movement, complicating static analysis and predictability (ISO 26262-6 Table 3 Rec. 1i).
enforcement: static-check (Clang-based static analysis and automated rewriting)
quote: the buffer–accessor programming model enforces implicit memory management and data movement, complicating static analysis, reducing predictability of performance
